text:
The Miami-based AI startup Subquadratic came out of stealth mode last month with a huge claim. It announced that it had solved a mathematical bottleneck that had been holding back large language models for almost a decade.

The details were thin, and many people were unconvinced. But Subquadratic has started to bring the receipts, sharing the results of an independent evaluation of its new tech. The results suggest that the company’s claims might be worth paying attention to.

According to Subquadratic, it has developed a new kind of LLM, called SubQ, that is faster and cheaper and uses a lot less energy than any other model on the market. The company also claims that SubQ is able to process up to 12 times as much text at once as most other models, allowing it to carry out a range of data-heavy tasks, such as analyzing hundreds of documents or entire code bases.

What’s more, Subquadratic says, SubQ does this while more or less matching the performance of the best models put out by Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Anthropic on key tasks like coding.

The problem was that the company at first provided little evidence for its claims beyond a handful of self-published test scores. And it has yet to make SubQ widely available for people to try out themselves.

So it’s no surprise that Subquadratic’s claims were met with skepticism. Dan McAteer, an artificial-intelligence engineer, captured the overall response on X: “SubQ is either the biggest breakthrough since the Transformer … or it’s AI Theranos.”

A month on, the company has published more information about its model, including the results of additional independent tests run by the third-party firm Appen.

“We expected healthy skepticism,” says Subquadratic cofounder and chief technology officer Alex Whedon. “In hindsight, releasing the third-party benchmarks alongside the initial announcement would have preempted much of the skepticism, which is why we’re taking the time to make sure any future results are fully verified before putting them out.”

Subquadratic asked Appen, which evaluates other companies’ models, to run its tests on SubQ. The results seem to back up a lot of Subquadratic’s claims. “That was really exciting to me, it validated their architecture,” says Jeanine Sinanan-Singh, Appen’s director of generative AI research.

“I was like, ‘Wow, this could be a game changer,’ because models struggle with speed and inefficiency,” she adds. “But when you have kind of shocking results, it’s really not as credible when you say it yourself.”

SubQ won’t replace existing top models across the board, but it could offer huge increases in speed at a fraction of the typical cost for certain tasks. Subquadratic insists that in the long run, though, its breakthrough could change how LLMs are built. “We hope we’re kicking off a new age of efficiency,” says Justin Dangel, the firm’s cofounder and CEO. “We don’t think anybody will be building on transformers in a few years.”

Attention!

To understand why Subquadratic’s claims are a big deal, let’s dig into how most LLMs work. The key mechanism inside an LLM is a type of neural network called a transformer, which runs a process known as dense attention. Today’s LLMs typically chain together multiple transformers. (The foundational paper of the LLM era, published by researchers at Google in 2017, was titled “Attention Is All You Need.”)

Dense attention works like this: When a transformer processes a chunk of text, it first encodes each word (or part of a word, known as a token) with a number. To capture the meaning of the full text, it then multiplies each of those numbers with every other number for that text. For example, a piece of text 10,000 words long would kick off almost 50 million individual multiplications. That’s a lot of computation and the main reason that LLMs are notorious power hogs.

“If you want to summarize The Great Gatsby, you have to look at the first word and the last word together, and then you have to look at every other combination,” says Dangel.

As the length of the text increases, the number of computations skyrockets. That’s because each additional number must be multiplied by all other previous numbers. Double the number of words, and you roughly quadruple the number of computations, a rate of increase known as a quadratic expansion.

(You can picture this yourself: Draw a circle and mark dots around its edge. Each dot is a token. Then draw lines between pairs of dots to represent the multiplication of those two tokens. A circle with five dots will have 10 lines crossing it. Make it 10 dots and you will have 45 lines, 20 dots and you will have 190 lines, and so on.)

Slashing costs

Subquadratic’s solution is to ditch dense attention, the core operation of a transformer, in favor of what’s known as sparse attention, which slashes the number of computations needed. Instead of multiplying the number assigned to each token by every other number, sparse attention selects just some of the numbers to multiply. The idea is that not all relationships between words in a piece of text matter.

“Sparse attention says not all of those relationships are important, because they’re not,” says Whedon. “If you’re reading a book, you’re not going to look at the first and second words, first and third—that’s insane.”

It’s a simple approach, and Subquadratic is not the first to try it. “Pretty much everything under the sun has been attempted,” says Will Depue, an independent AI researcher who previously worked at OpenAI. “It’s not impossible, but it’s akin to running a four-minute mile.”

Previous techniques for selecting which numbers to multiply and which to ignore have not produced a mechanism that can capture the meaning of a document as well as dense attention can.

Subquadratic claims to have cracked the problem at last. It pitches SubQ as the first sparse-attention LLM that rivals mainstream dense-attention models in performance.

“Historically, most mechanisms have used fixed patterns, like always comparing the first word to the fifth,” says Whedon. “That’s pretty limiting. Language is too sophisticated for that. And so, one of the things that makes our mechanism unique is that we dynamically select which ones are important.”

The firm won’t say exactly how SubQ chooses which words to focus on, but the selection is calculated on the fly and differs for each piece of text the model is given. “That’s kind of where the secret sauce is,” says Whedon.

Testing, testing

The upshot is that for certain tasks, SubQ may be faster and cheaper to run than most other models. Appen evaluated SubQ on a handful of standard tests. In a straight-up speed test, which sets a baseline for how fast a model can operate in theory rather than assessing what a model can actually do, Appen found that SubQ was 56 times faster than models using FlashAttention, a previous sparse-attention technique. 

On LiveCodeBench, a test that looks at how well models perform on competitive coding problems taken from real contests, SubQ scored 89.7%, putting it in the same ballpark as other top coding models. “This model continues to provide frontier-level performance in coding,” says Appen’s Sinanan-Singh.

Subquadratic’s claims about cost are harder to verify because SubQ is not yet widely available. According to Dangel, it costs $2,600 to run Anthropic’s LLM Opus 4.6 through RULER 128, a test developed by Nvidia to assess a model’s ability to retrieve information from large data sets. And SubQ? “It cost us eight dollars,” he says.

SubQ does seem to be able to handle a lot of text at once. The model has a context window (roughly akin to a working memory) up to 12 million tokens long. Most top models today have context windows one million tokens long. In a demo that Whedon ran for me, he asked SubQ to perform a task that required it to reason about information contained in 400 documents. It responded in seconds. When he gave Perplexity—a popular LLM-powered search engine—the same task, it failed to load all 400 documents. 

Appen put SubQ through the Needle-in-a-Haystack test, which, like RULER, assesses how well a model retrieves specific information buried in a large data set. In its report, Appen states that Subquadratic’s model scored 98% with context windows six million and 12 million tokens long, “sustaining near-perfect long-context retrieval at scales few models are tested at.”

Too good to be true?

Despite the high scores, benchmarks paint an incomplete picture of what a model can and cannot do. Testing under very specific conditions is not a substitute for running a model on a wide range of real tasks.

Subquadratic is offering SubQ as a model tailored to coding and to searching very large data sets. It says that tens of thousands of potential users have already signed up for early access, including more than 500 enterprise customers. But there’s a long waitlist, and the firm has given very few people access so far. Subquadratic’s response is that it is a new, small company with limited resources and cannot serve too many people at once.

Until more people get their hands on the model and try it out for themselves, some skepticism is justified. One nagging issue is that Subquadratic reused the weights (values set within a model during training that determine how it will behave) from a version of the Chinese open-source model Qwen to bootstrap SubQ, rather than training it from scratch. That’s a common approach for model makers to take, but it cuts across Subquadratic’s claim that it has fully reinvented how LLMs work.  

“They may have built something real and useful,” says Depue. “But the public evidence does not yet justify the stronger claim that they have solved the quadratic attention bottleneck.”

In the meantime, Subquadratic cofounder Whedon insists that making something different was his only option. If you want to build a competitive model, you have to have new ideas, he says: “We’re more up against it than OpenAI is.”

text:
🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Days 267 to 273 (Week 39): Phase Three: Full Term
📚 Source: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. General pregnancy education only, not medical advice. Always talk with your doctor or midwife.
🔊 Your baby reaches full term this week. Every organ is formed, the reflexes are ready, and your baby already knows your voice. Which song will you sing first, and how have lullabies, nursery rhymes, and phonic songs been preparing that moment? Read on.

🗓️ Week 39 at a Glance
  Week 39 is pregnancy days 267 to 273, counted from the first day of your last period, the same way your doctor, midwife, and pregnancy calculator count. If conception happened around day 14, your baby is between 253 and 259 days old. In longer or shorter cycles, these days shift a little.
This is the week of full term. Your baby is ready to live outside the womb. The brain and lungs keep maturing up to birth. Fat makes up a bigger part of your baby's weight, helping with warmth and energy. The fingernails may reach past the fingertips.
  Your baby is about 20 inches from head to heel and weighs about 7 1/4 pounds, about the size of a small pumpkin. Your due date is next week, but your baby may come any day.

🗓️ The Week, Day by Day
  Here is the week counted in days after conception. In a 28-day cycle, add 14 to find your pregnancy day. Your baby will choose the day, so treat this as a guide.
Days 253 and 254 (pregnancy days 267 and 268): Your baby reaches full term.
Days 255 and 256 (days 269 and 270): The lungs keep making surfactant, and the brain keeps adding connections.
Day 257 (day 271): Fat keeps building, giving your baby round cheeks and soft creases.
Day 258 (day 272): The fingernails may reach past the tips of the fingers.
Day 259 (day 273): Your baby weighs about 7 1/4 pounds and is about 20 inches from head to heel.

🎉 Full Term
  Doctors call babies born from 39 weeks through 40 weeks and 6 days full term. Babies born in this window generally have the best health outcomes, with the fewest problems with breathing, feeding, and staying warm.
  Your baby is ready. Every organ is formed and working. The lungs are prepared for the first breath. The brain is ready to learn. The reflexes for sucking, swallowing, and gripping are strong.
But being ready does not mean labor will start today. Many first-time mothers give birth after their due date. Your baby will come in God's time.

🗣️ What Your Baby Knows
Your baby will not understand a single word at birth. But your baby is not a stranger to your home. Your baby knows the sound of your voice. Your baby has heard Dad's voice, the voices of brothers and sisters, and the songs your family sang every week.
  Studies show newborns pay special attention to their mother's voice and to sounds they heard often before birth. The GLAL method teaches more than that too. From conception, your baby has received your songs spirit to spirit. Now the spirit, the ears, and the voice of home will meet face to face.

🫶 Teaching Begins at Home
  From the first day, your home is your child's first school. God told His people to teach their children in the house, on the road, when lying down, and when rising up.
Your baby will learn by being held, by hearing your voice, by watching your face, and by hearing the same songs and words again and again. This is God's Home Schooling. You do not need a classroom. You need love, time, and the habits you have already built.
“And you shall explain them to your sons. And you shall meditate upon them sitting in your house, and walking on a journey, when lying down and when rising up.” (Deuteronomy 6:7, CPDV)
“Gregory Peck was born April 5, 1916. In the 1962 film To Kill a Mockingbird he played a gentle father who taught his children honesty and kindness at home, a role he called one of his favorites.”

🏥 If Labor Does Not Start
  Most women go into labor on their own between 37 and 42 weeks. If labor does not start, your doctor will talk with you about the next steps.
  Some doctors offer an induction at 39 weeks for healthy pregnancies, after talking it through with you. Others wait longer, often until 41 weeks, with extra checks of your baby. If there is a medical reason, such as high blood pressure, your doctor may recommend an earlier induction.
An induction means using medicine or other methods to help labor begin. Ask your doctor what they recommend for you and why, what methods they use, and how long it may take. Write the answers in your journal.
“I know it at first light; great is your faithfulness.” (Lamentations 3:23, CPDV)
“Lou Gehrig was born June 19, 1903. He showed up and played in 2,130 baseball games in a row, faithful day after day, and he was remembered as a gentle and humble man.”

📝 Phase Three: Sing the Whole List
For 20 weeks, Phase Three has helped you join sounds into words. Look at your Word List now. You have family words, food words, face words, sound words, praise words, light words, action words, rhymes, direction words, sense words, number words, lullaby words, thank-you words, welcome words, comfort words, and Bible names.
  This week, sing through the whole list. Take one group each day. Sing every word on the melody of the weekly song, clap the beats, and remember the week you added it.
Then circle the words you will sing first after birth. Perhaps "Hello," "Mama," "Dada," "I love you," and your baby's name. This list will become your baby's first reading list. One day, your child will see these words in print and read the very words you sang before birth. That is God's plan: sounds first, then words, then reading.
  Every word on your list is a phonic song. Together they make your family's own collection of lullabies, nursery rhymes, baby music, and kids music, built one sound at a time.
  “Write the vision and explain it on tablets.” (Habakkuk 2:2, CPDV)
  “William Howard Taft was born September 15, 1857. After serving as president of the United States, he became chief justice of the Supreme Court, the only person ever to hold both offices.”

🤰 Your Body at Thirty-Nine Weeks
  Your body is ready for birth. Your cervix may be softening and starting to thin. You may feel a lot of pressure low in the pelvis, more frequent tightenings, a low backache, and sometimes loose stools or nausea as labor gets close.
Rest as much as you can, and eat and drink to keep your strength up. Walking can feel good if your doctor says it is safe.
If you have tightenings, time them from the start of one to the start of the next. Follow your doctor's instructions for when to call and when to come in.

🏥 Arriving at the Hospital

Bring your headphones and the weekly songs. Familiar music can help you stay calm between tightenings.

  Before you leave the hospital, your baby will usually have several checks. A few drops of blood from the heel are tested for rare but serious conditions. A small sensor on the hand and foot checks oxygen levels to screen for some heart problems. And your baby's hearing is screened with a quick, painless test while your baby sleeps.

🔧 How Labor Can Be Started
  If your doctor recommends an induction, there are several ways it can be done. A membrane sweep is when the doctor gently separates the bag of waters from the cervix during an exam, which may help labor start. Medicines placed near the cervix or taken by mouth can help soften and open it. A small balloon may be placed in the cervix to help it open.

  Labor usually happens in stages. In early labor, the cervix slowly softens and opens, and tightenings start mild and irregular, then become more regular. This stage can last many hours. In active labor, tightenings get stronger and closer together, and the cervix opens more quickly.

  Moving and changing positions can help you cope with labor and may help your baby move down. Try walking, swaying, rocking on a birthing ball, leaning forward over a bed or counter, kneeling on hands and knees, or sitting backward on a chair. A warm shower can bring relief.

This is the start of many visits in the first year. Write each date and what the doctor said. These notes will help you see how your baby grows and learns.

💙 Dads Can Struggle Too
  Mothers are not the only ones who can feel low after a baby is born. Some fathers feel anxious, sad, or overwhelmed in the weeks and months after birth. Lack of sleep, new responsibilities, and money worries can all play a part.
  Dad, if you feel this way, tell your wife, a friend, your pastor, or your doctor. Asking for help is a sign of strength. A healthy father is a gift to his whole family.

  In early labor at home, light snacks and drinks can help keep up your strength, if your doctor agrees: toast, crackers, fruit, broth, juice, or water. text:
Club Kid (🌟🌟🌟🌟) hit me right between the eyes. This is the kind of film that reminds me why I love going to the movies - why I even started this account in the first place. There’s no other way I can describe this movie. Writer/director/leading man Jordan Firstman? This his moment. It’s his time. Club Kid is the perfect mixture of uproarious comedy and heartfelt introspection that is so appropriate for the year 2026, as a man stuck in a state of arrested development is forced to reconcile his inability to grow up for his own sake with the necessity that he do so for the sake of someone else. This tried and true arc of sudden parenthood thrusting responsibility upon the irresponsible is elevated by the world that colors this film. The underground queer nightlife of New York City and the community that surrounds it and holds it up adds a uniqueness to this story, which refuses to condemn any one type of life style, but instead demands life be lived with intention rather than reckless abandon. 

The story here follows Peter Green, a decade after a drunken threesome that will soon come back to his doorstep. Peter’s uproarious drug-fueled lifestyle of clubbing and party management where days bleed into nights endlessly, gets promptly flipped on its head with the arrival of Arlo. Arlo, the surprise son of this gay man’s sole sexual encounter with a woman, is essentially left on Peter’s doorstep from London after his mother’s death. With a heart of gold and a desire to explore his new home in NYC, Arlo turns out to be exactly what Peter needs at this juncture in life, just as Peter is exactly what Arlo needs as well. But of course, bringing these worlds together is hardly seamless, and the fairytale of a family united inevitably crashes back down to reality. 

I can’t determine if Firstman’s best work here is as a writer, a director, or an actor, as he puts in strong work under each of these three hats. The script tells the story of a man in turmoil who gets offered a lifeline disguised as a burden, and the way Peter and Arlo are written to be the perfect puzzle pieces to each other’s fractured lives provides the heart of the entire story. You instantly believe how badly each of them needs the other. The script perfectly serves the entire ensemble; from Peter’s relocated roommate Nicky, to his business partner turned adversary Sophie, to Arlo’s transgender DJ mentor Saffron, the whole cast feels authentically ripped from New York City streets and the underground nightlife. The camera work also serves as a window into Peter’s mind and an extension of his mental state, often dropping us into the intoxicating strobe lights of a club, the frenetic energy of an empty apartment stormed by pregamers, or the intense close ups of a soul-bearing conversation. The audience cannot help but be immersed in this world. 

But Firstman’s performance deserves the most praise, as he delicately walks the line of a man dripping in self-loathing who has long-since relinquished any care for his own life suddenly given a new life to be responsible for. This movie serves as the literal and metaphorical trial of this man’s soul, as he must reckon with his past decisions and how he got to this point, and decide what he can do to change course, or if he even wants to. His salvation comes not from learning self-love, but from discovering that even someone who struggles to see the value in his own life can be invaluable to someone else’s. Of course, this performance is matched by Reggie Absolom’s work as Arlo, a child who smiles despite going through hell. Absolom plays the layers of Arlo brilliantly, as he navigates a new world amidst his grief and confusion. He’s the delicate plate that Peter must keep spinning as the audience watches with bated breath. We worry any wrong move could break him. Their unabashed love for one another is the essence of the whole film….

text:
As with most issues with scripture it's a language translation issue. So much meaning is lost in the translations over time into English.

Let's take a look at where this verse comes from, 1 Thessalonians 4.

1 Thessalonians 4:13 “But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.”

Asleep – dead. Paul doesn’t want you to be ignorant about where the dead are, those that have gone before. You shouldn’t be sad for to be absent from this body is to be with our Father. Your loved ones are not in a grave somewhere. They are with our Heavenly Father.

Others which have no hope – heathen. Below I reference again the story of Lazarus and the Rich Man from Luke 16…all are in heaven waiting to be judged. No one is burning in hell. There is a gulf that separates the good from the, let’s just call them not so good. And Paul is very loving in that he doesn’t want people to be biblically illiterate. It can cause unnecessary anxiety and worry.

1 Thessalonians 4:14 “For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him.”

If you believe Christ rose from the dead, then you must believe we all do. Remember Lazarus and the Rich Man in Luke 16. The Rich Man was also taken to heaven to be held for judgment and was conscious to the fact that he was on the wrong side of the gulf and he felt the embarrassment and disappointment that he had acted as he had on Earth.

Luke 16:26 Context
23. And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom. 24. And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame. 25. But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. 26. And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence. 27. Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father's house: 28. For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment. 29. Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

1 Thessalonians 4:15 “For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep.”

By the Word of the Lord, not by the doing of man. We can’t prevent them from going to the Lord because they are already there.

1 Peter Chapter 3:18 Christ went back to the beginning to offer all that came before salvation…

Peter 3:18 “For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:”

Peter 3:19 “By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison;”

Peter 3:20 “Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.”

Peter 3:21 “The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ:”

1 Thessalonians 4:16 “For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump (7th trump) of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:”

There’s a colon after God: to separate the thought…
**Grammar rule: Use a colon between 'independent clauses' if the second summarizes, explains or amplifies the first.

Understand from earlier that the dead that rose first are already with Him. And when we are done with these flesh bodies, they return to the dust from which they came. Some Christians believe our bodies will be raised out of the graves.

Further Documentation:
Ecclesiastes 12:6 “Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.”Ecclesiastes 12:7 “Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

1 Thessalonians 4:17 “Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.”

and to just close out the 4th chapter…
1 Thessalonians 4:18 Wherefore comfort one another with these words.

This is the verse that causes the most confusion. In fact, Paul later realized that this was a confusing statement and attempts to correct it and better explain this in 2 Thessalonians Chapter 2.

“We which are alive and remain…” Remember 1 Corinthians 15:51-52 where Paul said “we shall not all sleep but be changed” in the “twinkling of an eye…”

Another thing that confuses people again comes back to translation. Paul also spoke colloquial Greek, basically informal slang. Let’s look at two words: clouds and air.

STRONGS NUMBER G109
Word Summary
aēr: air
Original Word: ἀήρ
Transliteration: aēr
Phonetic Spelling: (ah-ayr')
Part of Speech: Noun, Masculine
Short Definition: air
Meaning: airStrong's Concordance
air.From aemi (to breathe unconsciously, i.e. Respire; by analogy, to blow); "air" (as naturally circumambient) -- air. Compare psucho.

So, it’s nothing to do with the sky. It’s breath, or basically the breath of life, our spirit body. Nothing about atmosphere, nothing about wind.

Further Documentation:
Ezekiel 37:5 “Thus saith the Lord GOD unto these bones; Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live:”

Ezekiel 37:6 “And I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and ye shall live; and ye shall know that I am the LORD.” Ezekiel 37:7 “So I prophesied as I was commanded: and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone.” Ezekiel 37:8 “And when I beheld, lo, the sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above: but there was no breath in them.” Ezekiel 37:9 “Then said he unto me, Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live.” Ezekiel 37:10 “So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.”God breathed life (spriit) into these old, dry bones and flesh bodies.

Job 33:4 “The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.”Genesis 7:15 “And they went in unto Noah into the ark, two and two of all flesh, wherein is the breath of life.”

Ok, let’s talk about the word cloud now.

This is where it’s important to bring up Paul’s use of “street” Greek. The word “cloud.”

First let’s look at an example in scripture of when Paul has used that word before.

Hebrews 12:1 “Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,”

The word “cloud” is the same word in the Greek as in 1 Thessalonians – and here it’s talking about a large crowd of people. Also the English definition can also have the same meaning: c: a great cloud or multitude.

So, for clarities sake and a different perspective, let’s rewrite that verse using the meanings instead of the translated word:

1 Thessalonians 4:17 “Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in great crowds, to meet the Lord in our spiritual bodies: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.”

Starting to mean something different now, isn’t it? And again, remember the subject is “where are the dead?” And at the end we all will be changed into that “breath of life” spiritual body. Not up flying up in the air or dead bodies rising from the grave.

text:
AWESOME MOVIES THAT DESERVE MORE LOVE
Dracula Untold (2014)

The movie is supposed to be an origin story for the titular Dracula, and follows Vlad Dracula the Prince of Wallachia and Transylvania as he becomes tired of all of as part of the Ottoman Sultan's elite janissary corps, where he was known as "Vlad the Impaler, Son of the Dragon." At some point him and his men find a cave populated by a mysterious figure, a hermit vampire (the ever-excellent Charles Dance), who slaughters Vlad's men but leaves Vlad alive. Vlad returns and later learns that his family and his territory is being threatened by Ottoman forces, with his son being kidnapped. 

Desperate to save his son, Vlad returns to Broken Tooth Mountain to seek help from the Master Vampire. The vampire offers Vlad blood that temporarily gives him its powers. If he resists the intense urge to drink human blood for the next three days, he will turn back into a human. Otherwise, he will remain a vampire forever, and the ancient vampire will be freed. Vlad drinks its blood and is given superhuman strength and supernatural abilities, including the ability to transform into a cloud of bats. A story of revenge ensues. 

Although the movie did pretty well at the box office, earning $220.2 million on about an $80 million budget, it was mostly savaged by critics and earned itself a woeful 26% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. I think this has given people the impression that it's not good, bt this couldn't be further from the truth. While it shares very little in common with Bram Stoker's Dracula, the focus here is on epic action and watching this guy use his awesome powers to enact his revenge, all while struggling to maintain his humanity. There is an epic feel to it all, like you're watching a grand fantasy film with vampires, the sets and costumes are awesome, and we get lots of creative displays of Dracula's powers, as well as a human story underlying it all. It's a damn good time, and deserves more love. Check it out if you can! A 100,000-ton U.S. aircraft carrier is built for war. On July 27, 2018, the USS Carl Vinson went to work for a 35-foot boat.

That morning the Carl Vinson was off Hawaii for RIMPAC, the largest naval exercise on Earth. Twenty-five nations. About 25,000 people.

Then a distress call came over the radio.

A small boat had run aground in the shallows off Niihau, the westernmost inhabited island in Hawaii. Five people were on board.

Niihau is remote. The nearest Coast Guard station was on another island.

The sailors standing watch on the carrier's bridge heard the call.

The carrier was seven miles away.

Nobody on that bridge decided it was somebody else's problem. The Carl Vinson offered help and launched two MH-60S Seahawk helicopters from the Black Knights of Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron 4.

All five people were lifted off.

Four were flown to Coast Guard Station Kauai. The fifth went to a hospital to be checked.

Then the Coast Guard came in to deal with the grounded boat.

The carrier's captain, Matt Paradise, kept it short:

"When nearby mariners needed assistance, we stepped up immediately and helped. That is what we are trained to do, and I'm proud of our team."

Five strangers on a stranded boat. One nuclear aircraft carrier. Seven miles.

That was the whole decision.

text:
Sun Tzu 8.3: 

There are roads which must not be followed, armies which must be not attacked, towns which must be besieged, positions which must not be contested, commands of the sovereign which must not be obeyed.

***

This line from Sun Tzu relates to the idea of “commander’s intent.” 

It is not practical to always rely on checking with your commander before taking action. For this reason, militaries have realized the need for a concept called the “commander’s intent.”

The idea is that leaders should empower those under their command to understand the purpose behind an order and then to work to achieve the objective according to their own best judgment. 

They should not be passive or wait to get permission for every decision.

A highly similar military doctrine was created by the Royal Prussian Army (1701–1919). 

It is called Auftragstaktik (“mission-type tactics” or “military tactics”).

You might recognize the idea from the 2000 novel Shadow of the Hegemon, by Orson Scott Card (part of the Ender’s Game series).

The Prussian Army was known for an emphasis on independent initiative and the willingness to take risks in order to bring about a decisive battle.

The job of a leader is to use his own judgment and take advantage of the opportunities that come up.

As you decide your actions, use your own eyes and your own mind to decide what is and is not possible.

You were not made to be a robot or a clone of someone else. There are moments in which you are the only one in a position to do what is needed.

Be willing to take your stand, even when no one else understands.

If you are leading others, consider using a decentralized command structure in which you give clear directions about your intent and rationale, while leaving the manner of execution to the judgment of the one closer to the situation.

In Auftragstaktik: The Basis For Modern Military Command, Major Michael J. Gunther offers a memorial account to summarize the concept:

//Gen. Helmuth von Moltke, Chief of the German General Staff from 1857 until his retirement in 1888, often related a story to junior members of his staff that described the essence of the German system of command. Following a battle, Prince Frederick Karl took a major aside and proceeded to reprimand the young officer for a tactical mistake. The major responded that he was following an order issued to him from a superior officer, which constituted the word of the king himself. The prince responded in kind, “His Majesty made you a major because he believed you would know when not to obey his orders.”//

The idea of following commander’s intent also applies for Christians executing God’s mission to be salt and light in the world.

We do not have the ability to converse with God the way Moses or Abraham did, so we need to understand God’s intent based on his written instructions. 

And we need to take initiative and apply independent judgment and a spirit of enterprise.

Since Ukraine struck Russian Wildberries warehouses in July, Russia has hit 570 Ukrainian warehouses, according to military analyst Clement Molin. Molin argues the exchange exposed Ukraine's civilian logistics as Russian strikes on Black Sea ports intensified during the harvest.

THE WAREHOUSE CAMPAIGN

Molin's summer assessment is severe. Kyiv made decisions its defences and economy could not absorb. Ukraine also struck Black Sea commercial vessels. Russia hit supermarkets and ports. Civilian supply chains and trade were disrupted.

Russia was already striking Ukraine's ports and needed no excuse. Responsibility for its attacks rests with Moscow. Molin's narrower point: Kyiv was unprepared. Black Sea ports were cut off and repeatedly bombarded. Damage to storage and retail squeezed an economy reliant on moving goods.

A warehouse hit in Russia and one in Ukraine have different consequences for a civilian economy under invasion. Kyiv has every right to strike Russia. It must calculate what it can protect when Russia responds.

THE AIR-DEFENCE SQUEEZE

Russia's growing supply of deep-strike weapons, including Geran-4 and Banderol systems and munitions for Iskander and S-400, met a shortage of Ukrainian interceptors. Near-daily attacks on Kyiv strained defence production and civilian economic activity.

Molin points to decisions inside Ukraine's control. Two warehouses hit near Kyiv this summer held substantial ammunition stocks, including air-defence missiles. Keeping them in vulnerable facilities magnified losses when interceptors were scarce. An attack on a publicly announced military exhibition killed Ukrainian drone-industry workers. Molin argues the toll among specialists and defence-industry personnel far exceeded the official figure. Lost expertise, capacity and missiles will matter in the months ahead.

POLITICS AND COMMAND

The military strain coincided with a political rupture. Zelensky's sudden dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov drew criticism, as did corruption affairs around Kyrylo Budanov and his refusal to speak with Ukrainian journalists despite foreign interviews. Fedorov then called for an election and accepted work abroad, hurting his standing despite popular support.

Mykhailo Drapatyi's appointment as commander-in-chief offered hope, not instant repair. His task was to stabilise the Donbas after its sharp deterioration in August. Russian gains demanded attention, though Molin cautioned against declaring a return to an offensive on the scale of 2024 or 2025. Ukraine's position in the south improved, and its drone strikes continued.

A HARD WINTER TO PREPARE FOR

Molin warned of a difficult winter in the rear if attacks caused widespread electricity and heating shortages, and raised the possibility of hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians leaving for Poland and the wider EU. Winter could hinder Russian infiltration at the front, but offers little comfort to families without heat or power. Protecting homes, industry and supply routes sustains the army.

Russia has vulnerabilities too. Its strained economy and damaged refineries have brought fuel shortages to parts of the country. Both sides' deep strikes reach beyond their targets. Ukraine must impose costs on Russia without exposing essential systems to damage it cannot quickly replace.

Molin says he has faced criticism from Ukrainians over his earlier account of these decisions and from Russians over his more recent coverage of Russian losses. He describes his work as OSINT-based monitoring that returns to a subject repeatedly, rather than treating one set of strikes or losses as the whole war. This difference is important here. The warehouse tally, the port campaign, the interceptor shortage and the worsening Donbas position belong in the same assessment, even when the findings make different audiences angry.

Source: @clement_molin

She became the Mad Queen the moment the bells rang and she kept burning anyway.

Surrender was offered. The Lannister army was broken. The city had no more fight left in it. She still ordered Drogon to incinerate streets full of civilians who had nothing to do with the wars in Essos or her claim to the Iron Throne. That wasn’t “strategic” or “the only logical end.” That was the point where she chose terror over victory. She later admitted as much to Jon: she knew people would only follow her out of fear after that.

The Targaryen coin-flip was always the subtext. Aerys burned people alive and talked to flames. Dany spent seasons building a pattern of escalating violence justified by “liberation” (crucifying the masters, burning the Tarlys, threatening to burn cities that didn’t kneel). The final act just stopped pretending the justification still mattered. You can argue the show compressed the descent badly (it did), but the destination was written on the wall once she decided a surrendered population still needed to burn to prove her destiny.

The tragedy wasn’t only the pacing. It was watching someone who once saw herself as a breaker of chains become the very thing she claimed to hate, and then convince herself it was necessary. That’s the Mad Queen.

text:
The General’s Dispatch — Tuesday, November 10

Commanders: The $SPX retreated 0.71% to 7,496.63, the $IXIC fell 0.90% to 25,025.83, and the $DJI lost 0.57% to 52,087.13. After Monday’s grand charge, Wall Street found inflation waiting at the next hill, armed with fresh data and no interest in surrender.

October consumer prices rose 0.4%, above the 0.3% expected, while core inflation also came in hotter than forecast. The report strengthened bets on another Fed rate hike—and raised talk of a larger move. Technology shares faced added pressure as traders weighed the cost of money and the uncertain price of the AI campaign; investors also watched $NVDA amid the company’s inquiry involving CEO Jensen Huang. October inflation data managed to steal the day’s dispatch from the earnings scouts.

Across the intermarket battlefield, the formations disagreed:

Treasuries retreated: the 2-year yield jumped to about 4.74%, and the 10-year approached 5.0% as rate expectations reset.

Oil fell: Brent slipped to about $90.69 a barrel, with hopes of reduced Iran-related supply risk weighing on prices.

Gold retreated: spot gold dropped roughly 2.3% to about $4,044 an ounce as higher yields and a firmer dollar pressed on the metal.

Breadth weakened: the major indexes all closed lower, with technology among the pressure points.

The dollar strengthened about 0.6%, adding another headwind for gold.

The General’s assessment: Today’s cross-asset picture reflected a market recalibrating to stickier inflation: yields and the dollar advanced, while stocks and gold gave ground. Cheaper oil offered some relief on the energy front, but the inflation report kept the Fed’s next move in focus. Monday’s rally gained ground; Tuesday’s data reminded the army that the campaign still has several hills to cross.

text:
for pre-readers, there's something special about a book series with a consistent look and theme. each new book offers something familiar and something new. i've watched that combination draw my oldest back to books again and again.

it makes sense through a montessori lens: a sense of order helps children explore independently. a recognizable series gives them a familiar starting point, with something new to discover.

Even if that series isn't the most stellar or expected choice...

In my experience, Chris Ferrie's "Baby University" series. Over 10 board books that any montessorian or charlotte masonite would, with good reason, sneer at. 

But because of their size, predictable format, and use of novel language and concepts, my daughters quickly took to them. "Another "for babies" book, mommy?".

Other notables that achieve the same effect:
Dr. Seuss
Brambly hedge
Frog & toad
Tales for Once & Ever
Bendon Publishing fairy tale collections
The Lang Fairy books
Little Golden Books

They will literally want me to go through the -whole- series simply because they enjoy finishing a set. 

Children are drawn to order.

text:
VISTRA $VST GETS A TEXAS TEST FROM NRG BY YEAR-END:

Vistra (VST) at $131.18, -$2.74 / -2.05% on Tuesday.

Vistra stays off every Len5 we weigh, with debt still more than three times the owners' stake on its September balance sheet. The next dated test of whether data centers still sign for Texas power belongs to NRG Energy (NRG) at $97.11, -$0.29 / -0.30% on Tuesday. Robert Gaudette, NRG's president and chief executive, expects approved agreements on a Texas data-center project by year-end, and Vistra has given no timing for selling the second part of Comanche Peak, its Texas nuclear plant. Vistra is up 5.1% since our post, all of it gained on Monday, when NRG reported and Vistra had nothing to report. NRG has won back its whole election-week loss, and Vistra about two-thirds. After Monday's close Vistra registered for resale the 5,000,000 shares it paid Q-Generation Holdings, the seller of Cogentrix, a gas-plant owner Vistra bought on October 30.

Vistra is on none of the Momentum, Quality-Value, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es, and it fails the Quality Len5 on debt. Quality wants a profitable business with debt under the owners' stake, and Vistra's debt was 3.4 times that stake on its September 30 balance sheet. Our post gave the June 30 figures.
- Long-term debt: $21.1B in September, $19.6B in June.
- Owners' equity, what is left for shareholders after every debt: $6.3B in September, $5.5B in June.
Since then Vistra took on $1.7B of debt with Cogentrix and repaid it on November 5, partly with short-term borrowing that is not counted in long-term debt. What would put it on the Quality Len5: debt cut below the owners' stake, a $14.8B gap on September 30.

We said Friday's buyers took Vistra's answers on Texas as NRG's too. On Monday NRG gave its own, with a date. Gina Hinojosa, Texas's governor-elect, has promised a moratorium on new data-center approvals. Gaudette said of NRG's plan to build power plants for a Texas data center, "The project is on track, and I fully expect approved agreements and an announcement by year-end." He also said, "I've actually talked to our customer since the elections, this project is going to happen." Stacey Dore, president of Vistra Retail, said on November 6 that Vistra does not comment on the timing of new deals. Jim Burke, Vistra's president and chief executive, said the state's hold on new data-center permits, part of an audit ordered by Governor Greg Abbott, had been expected to lift around mid-December. NRG is on none of the Momentum, Quality-Value, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es; at 48.9% under its February 25 high, it lacks the climb Momentum wants.

Vistra's whole gain since our post came on Monday, when it rose 7.31%.
- Since our post: +$6.38 / +5.1% from the $124.80 we quoted.
Constellation Energy (CEG) at $267.76, -$8.33 / -3.02% on Tuesday.
Constellation, which sells nuclear and gas power, raised its 2026 profit forecast before Monday's open. Our read: Vistra rose on Monday with NRG's and Constellation's reports and a broad rally in stocks. From the November 3 close, the last before the election results:
- NRG: +0.9%.
- Constellation: +1.7%.
- Vistra: -6.0%, with 69% of its two-day loss won back.
Constellation is on none of the Momentum, Quality-Value, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es; at about 21 times the middle of its 2026 profit forecast, it offers the value Len5es no discount.

The 5,000,000 shares were part of the price for Cogentrix, and the two sides counted each at $185. The purchase agreement required the registration, which is not itself a sale. The shares are about 1.5% of Vistra's stock, and Q-Generation agreed not to sell them through January 30 without Vistra's consent, with limited exceptions.

Vistra's debt keeps it off the Quality Len5, and its next Texas contract has no date. The dated tests, in order: mid-December, when Burke expected the permit hold to lift; year-end, for NRG's agreements; January 19, Hinojosa's first day as governor; and February 25, tentatively, Vistra's next report.

text:
ALIBABA $BABA CALLS ITS CHIP SPIN-OFF INSIGNIFICANT:

Alibaba Group (BABA) at $102.72, -$2.66 / -2.52% on Tuesday.

Alibaba passes the Quality Len5 and is on no other Len5 we weigh, and the go-ahead it announced Tuesday to list T-Head, its chip unit, adds nothing to that case yet. Taipei and Tokyo gained at midday Wednesday while Hong Kong's technology index fell. Alibaba's announcement keeps T-Head a subsidiary, sets no size or date, and calls the spin-off "insignificant" beside Alibaba's total assets, revenue and net income, in winning a waiver from offering its shareholders the new shares. Alibaba's shares fell in New York and Hong Kong before the announcement and lost under 1% more after it. Nasdaq-100 futures point to a higher open for US technology stocks, with Dow futures far behind.

Alibaba is on none of the Momentum, Quality-Value, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es. Quality wants a profitable business with debt below the owners' stake; Alibaba earned $1.55B for shareholders in the June quarter, and its borrowings are about a quarter of their equity. That profit was 76% below a year earlier. What would knock it off the Quality Len5: a year that ends in a loss. Deep-Value and Special-Situations wants a sound business priced under a cautious value of the cash it produces, and Alibaba's free cash flow, the cash left after running the business and paying for data centers, was an outflow of $6.6B in the June quarter. What would put it on the Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5: free cash flow turning positive in the September quarter, which Alibaba reports November 19 before the US open.

Asia's chip-heavy markets rose, and Hong Kong went the other way. At about 10:45pm ET, so far in Wednesday's sessions:
- Taiex (Taiwan): 43,762.51, +1,050.59 pts / +2.46%.
- Nikkei 225 (Japan): 61,118, +658 pts / +1.09%.
- Hang Seng (Hong Kong): 24,339, -218 pts / -0.89%.
- Hang Seng Tech index: 4,026.71, -57.74 pts / -1.41%.
- Shanghai Composite: 3,654.95, -8.77 pts / -0.24%, at its midday break.
Reuters's Tankan poll for November, out Wednesday in Tokyo, showed Japanese manufacturers at their most upbeat since August 2021, on demand for chips. The Standard, a Hong Kong newspaper, put Hong Kong's fall on technology shares and on property companies, hurt by worry about higher US interest rates after the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday that consumer prices rose 0.4% in October from September. Hong Kong reached its midday break at 11:00pm ET without once trading above Tuesday's close.

Alibaba said Tuesday evening in Hong Kong that the stock exchange there had confirmed it may go ahead with spinning off T-Head, meaning listing the unit as a separate company. T-Head, which Alibaba owns outright, designs data-center chips, including its Zhenwu AI chips.
- T-Head is expected to remain an Alibaba subsidiary, and the size of the share sale is not final.
- The exchange waived its requirement that Alibaba's shareholders be offered an assured entitlement, a guaranteed claim on T-Head's shares. One ground in the announcement: the spin-off is "insignificant to the Company and its Shareholders" measured against Alibaba's total assets, revenue and net income.
IFR, a capital-markets news service, reported the sale could raise $2B to $3B. That is about 1% of Alibaba's market value.

Alibaba's shares fell before the announcement, on no reported cause, and little after it.
- Monday: -3.72% in New York, to $105.38.
- Tuesday, before the announcement: -2.87% in Hong Kong, to HK$101.60, on a day the Hang Seng Tech index rose 1.08%.
- Wednesday, at the midday break: -0.79% in Hong Kong, to HK$100.80.
About two-thirds of Tuesday's fall in New York only matched Hong Kong's drop hours earlier. Measured from Hong Kong's close and converted to the same currency, New York took off about 0.9% more, and Wednesday's Hong Kong price matches New York's. Our read: neither city has paid more for Alibaba since the announcement, which fits how small Alibaba says the spin-off is.

Nasdaq-100 futures point to a higher open for US technology stocks, and Dow futures have gained less than a quarter as much in percent. At about 10:45pm ET, since Tuesday's close:
- Nasdaq-100 futures: 28,169.25, +334 pts / +1.20%.
- S&P 500 futures: 7,586.25, +42.00 pts / +0.56%.
- Dow futures: 52,458.00, +143 pts / +0.27%.
VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) at $483.63, -$3.78 / -0.78% on Tuesday. From Friday's close through Tuesday's: the chip fund +4.2%, Alibaba -6.1%. Overnight moves can fade before New York's 9:30am ET open, and Hong Kong trades again from midnight to 3:00am ET.

T-Head's listing has the exchange's go-ahead, with no size and no date. It still needs approval from the exchange's Listing Committee, the panel that admits new listings, and has to be put on record with the China Securities Regulatory Commission. Alibaba's own date is November 19, when the September quarter shows whether cash is still flowing out.

According to a rumor shared by Hong Kong boot insider @boot_meister, Nike is planning to revive its fan-favorite Tech Craft series in 2027. The popular concept, which has been shelved since around 2020-21, was renowned for giving Nike's modern speed and control silos a premium leather treatment.

First launched in 2015, the Nike Tech Craft collection originally blended high-tech Flyknit and synthetic uppers with thin, premium kangaroo leather layers across silos such as the Mercurial, Hypervenom, Magista, and Phantom. Traditionally crafted at Nike's famed Montebelluna factory in Italy, the hybrid boots offered players the lightweight responsiveness of modern boots alongside the classic padded touch of leather.

The collection was eventually discontinued after Nike committed to phasing out kangaroo leather across its football boot lineup. text:
A Deeper Framework for Understanding Conservatism, Jacobinism, and Trumpism

After reading Wang Jianxun’s essay once again, I have come to believe that its significance lies not merely in introducing one of Wang’s political perspectives, but in encouraging readers to develop a deeper and more comprehensive framework for analyzing political ideas.

I would like to highlight five particularly important intellectual foundations in his essay that deserve closer examination.

1. Edmund Burke: Conservatism Is Not Opposition to Change, but Opposition to Radicalism

Edmund Burke opposed Jacobinism during the French Revolution not because he rejected all reform, but because he opposed the destruction of a social order shaped by centuries of historical experience in the name of abstract reason and utopian ideals.

What Burke cherished were tradition, religion, property rights, social responsibility, and the continuity of civilization across generations.

There is an important distinction here:

Conservatism recognizes civilization as the accumulated achievement of generations.
Jacobinism tends to believe that society can be redesigned according to abstract ideological principles.
The former respects institutions and customs shaped by history; the latter is inclined to regard history as an obstacle that must be swept away.

This raises a fundamental question: Does humanity truly possess the capacity, through reason alone, to completely redesign society?

2. Jacobinism: More Than a French Revolution, It Is an Evolving Political Ideology

One of the most valuable aspects of Wang’s argument is that he does not confine Jacobinism to eighteenth-century France.

Rather, he identifies the continuation and evolution of an intellectual tradition.

From the radical egalitarianism of the French Revolution, through various revolutionary ideologies that emerged later, to certain contemporary progressive political movements, we can observe recurring patterns of thought.

Of course, not every left-wing ideology should be equated with Jacobinism. Nevertheless, these movements can be examined through certain shared political tendencies:

Redistributing power in the name of equality, rejecting tradition in the name of progress, and expanding political authority in the name of remaking society.

This is also an important key to understanding America’s contemporary culture wars.

3. Alexis de Tocqueville: The True Foundation of a Republic Is Its National Character and Social Mores

The insights of Alexis de Tocqueville are particularly important.

Wang draws upon one of Tocqueville’s central observations: American liberty depends not only on laws and the Constitution, but also on the mores of the American people and their habits of heart and mind.

I believe this insight can be expressed even more directly:

A constitution can establish the framework for liberty, but only a people who possess the spirit of liberty can sustain a free republic.

When a society loses its religious faith, moral restraints, capacity for self-government, and respect for personal responsibility, even an excellent Constitution may gradually lose its substance and effectiveness.

This is deeply connected to the Founding Fathers’ understanding of republican government.

4. Niccolò Machiavelli: The Fate of a Republic Depends on the Virtue of Its Citizens

In Discourses on Livy, Niccolò Machiavelli offers profound insights into the relationship between civic virtue and political institutions as he examines the rise and decline of the Roman Republic.

One point deserves particular attention:

A republic is not a machine that can function independently of the character of its citizens.

When citizens possess civic spirit, a sense of responsibility, and virtue, they are capable of choosing leaders who serve the republic. When these qualities deteriorate, their political choices change accordingly.

This observation resonates deeply with Tocqueville’s analysis.

1/2

#佳作选读

王建勋｜川普主义是雅各宾主义的克星（结束语）

2021年推荐，值得一读！

在柏克及其追随者看来，雅各宾主义是保守主义的头号敌人。源于法国大革命和欧陆启蒙运动的雅各宾主义，鼓吹理性至上，信奉进步主义，迷恋平等观念，倡导激进变化，嘲笑传统道德，蔑视私有财产，敌视宗教信仰等。

雅各宾主义并未随着法国大革命的结束而烟消云散，相反，其基本主张为后来出现的各种左翼意识形态和激进思潮所继承，在欧美成为批判、解构和瓦解西方文明的主要力量。

在过去半个世纪中，挟持了新闻界、教育界以及科技界等领域精英人士的雅各宾主义咄咄逼人，几乎是无坚不摧，而对抗这种力量的保守主义则显得力不从心，几乎是节节败退。正是在这种背景下，川普和川普主义应运而生，扛起抵御雅各宾主义进攻的大旗。

尽管川普和川普主义未必能击溃雅各宾主义，但至少有助于保守主义者重新集结力量，并思考如何最终战胜雅各宾主义，挽救西方文明。那曾经是柏克的夙愿，他曾经凭借一己之力在一定程度上遏制了雅各宾主义对英国的侵蚀，暂时保守住了英国的传统和自由，如今，这个任务落在了所有柏克的追随者身上。即使川普只是个“一届总统”，他对美国政治和社会的影响已经超出了很多人的想象。

他在短短四年内大刀阔斧般地进行革新，从减税和减少管制，到建墙和限制移民，再到任命三位大法官，以及重塑对外贸易、推动中东和平等，不仅履行了自己的竞选承诺，而且让美国恢复了活力和繁荣。他的政治遗产就是“川普主义”，其基本内涵表现为反对行政国家，捍卫自治传统；反对大政府，捍卫有限政府；反对经济管制，捍卫资本主义；反对世界主义，捍卫国家认同；反对多元文化主义，捍卫犹太-基督教传统。

在很大程度上讲，川普主义意在回归柏克开创的（古典）保守主义，是对当代美国新保守主义的矫正，有助于美国保守主义运动的再次复兴。美国当下的社会政治状况让很多人联想到罗马共和国，尤其是它开始衰败并走向帝国的时候。

在几乎所有的史书中，那是一个世风日下的时代，那是一个民众堕落的时代，那是一个独裁者横空出世的时代。无论这个联想是否有道理，无论美国的现状能否跟罗马共和国末期相提并论，马基雅维利曾敏锐地发现，只要罗马共和国的公民还没有腐化堕落，他们通常就还能选出有德行的统治者―能力出众且兢兢业业服务于共和国；一旦罗马的公民变得腐化堕落了，他们就开始选择那些能够讨好他们而非保障共和国安全的人；当罗马的公民变得更加腐化堕落的时候，他们就不再选那些讨好他们的人而是选那些权力令其恐惧的人了。

在很大程度上讲，这个看法与1831年访问美国的托克维尔不谋而合。在托克维尔看来，与美国的自然条件和法律制度相比，美国的民情、美国人的心智习惯（habits of heart and mind）才是决定美国民主的最重要因素，它决定了美国是一个自由且自治的社会。

一旦美国的民情发生了变化，其共和国的根基便会动摇，再优良的宪法和法律制度也无法有效地发挥作用。也就是说，在最终意义上讲，美国的民情―美国人的宗教信仰、道德观念、思维方式等，决定着美利坚合众国的未来，决定着美国国父们缔造的自由共和国还能否存续下去。这一点儿，没有人比托克维尔认识得更加深刻－更加清楚了。其天才般的洞见和智慧迄今值得每一个热爱自由的人细细品味和认真思考。

——王建勋 于2021年

DEMOCRAT MOB THUGGERY

Asymmetric Warfare in Politics, or Why it’s So Tough to Find Conservatives to Run for Office

Nov. 10, 2026

By rushbabe49 

Our State of Washington has been ruled for decades by Democrats, mostly elected by the voters (or non-voters) of Seattle, whose population outnumbers the rest of the state.  In the last 20 or so years, a new phenomenon has arisen that has basically consigned conservatives in Western Washington to minority status, and that is the rise of social media, and search engines like Google, which enabled the average person to look up previously hard-to-find information on just about anyone.

Social media also allowed users to come together in groups, and all concentrate on one user or organization, and mass-report or respond to their “tweets” on Twitter or posts on social sites like Facebook, Instagram, or MySpace.  Those sites and other similar places tended to be owned and staffed by young techies, who by affinity were mostly on the Left in political orientation (the taking over of public education by leftist teachers unions contributed to this uniformity of thought).  So many conditions happening all at the same time led to those young techies becoming much more powerful than they had ever been, with the newfound ability to direct their ire at specific people and organizations and affect those entities in real life.

I am a member of https://t.co/Rc1YRdCZUF, and I remember hearing from multiple other members that their Facebook posts were often “flamed” by many other members (flaming is an angry response to a simple post, often by many others), and flagged by “trust and safety” moderators.  People reported that even their own family members responded angrily and profanely to their posts and messages.  I used to subscribe to Kim Komando’s newsletters, and was mildly alarmed to hear of the continual Facebook scams that she reported on daily.  This ensured that I never joined Facebook, and that turned out to be a good decision. And this kind of leftist online thuggery has even invaded sites and groups that should have little to no reason for political attacks, including gamer sites, knitting sites, and even gardening sites. No corner of the internet is safe from invasion any longer.

I also remember, in my years of listening to Rush Limbaugh, how many times he spoke about the internet mobs that made whatever online presence he had miserable.  One thing he did that was put his investigative team on it, and they found that the majority of so-called members of leftist organizations were actually “bots” and behind them were just a few people.  The internet, then, has enabled a few people to control the online (and real) lives of many.

The first instance that I can remember of a hostile internet mob was the case of Brendan Eich, who was offered the CEO position at Mozilla Corp, who are responsible for the Firefox browser.  He donated to a ballot measure in California that was against homosexual “marriage”, and the Internet Mob doxed him (released all his personal information like home address) and, eventually, led Mozilla to rescind its CEO offer.  The Mob flexed its newfound power to, literally, destroy its “enemies”.  This sort of online rioting has now become almost routine on the Left, with very little pushback from victims.

Nvidia’s probe into reports that Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang—who engaged in an intimate relationship with a former executive identified as a Chinese asset—demonstrates why Washington cannot rely on chipmakers to police their own sales to China.

The revelation has ignited swift bipartisan scrutiny on Capitol Hill, prompting House committee chairs to demand a closed-door briefing with Huang while the administration prepares to brief the congressional Gang of Eight.

Lawmakers have spent the current Congress documenting how Beijing circumvents controls through intermediary smuggling, overseas cloud data centers, foreign tool suppliers, and distillation techniques used to illicitly train domestic models on American systems.

The upcoming 2027 National Defense Authorization Act offers Congress an immediate mechanism to plug these gaps by restricting advanced processor sales, penalizing unauthorized model distillation, and shutting down remote access to American compute abroad.

Sustaining America's competitive edge in artificial intelligence requires decisive intervention; allowing these evasion avenues to persist risks letting Beijing dominate core global platforms built on American private investment.

Chinese industry leaders openly admit that U.S. export restrictions remain their primary roadblock, underscoring that maintaining strict technological embargoes deprives Beijing of the advanced tools needed to close the hardware gap.

The strategic stakes extend directly to national security, as the Chinese Communist Party deploys high-end computing to design naval weaponry, expand domestic surveillance over minority populations, and pursue critical choke points in biotechnology and pharmaceuticals.

While critics claim restrictions merely accelerate Chinese self-reliance, Beijing launched its push for semiconductor independence a decade ago, and state subsidies cannot readily replicate allied chipmaking technology.

Lawmakers have roughly 50 days left in this legislative session to integrate these controls into the annual defense authorization, strengthen America’s negotiating posture against Beijing, and prevent China from closing the computing divide.

text:
There are some great Nats nuggets from Spencer in his story tonight. He is excellent and his work is worth subscribing to The Athletic for.

My thoughts on Dylan Crews' future:

1) The Jacob Young extension felt like a "Crews is available" tell. If the Nats were sold on Crews as the every day CF of the future, retaining JY wouldn't have been a priority. I get that Young didn't break the bank and that both can co-exist in the long-term plans, but Crews' value is at it's highest if he's playing CF.

2) The Nats should absolutely listen to offers for Crews. If a team is willing to give you a young, controllable pitcher for him? That absolutely has to be considered. Washington has a strong core of outfield talent and a dearth of pitching prospects.

3) Crews probably has more trade value than you'd think. He is going to be a very solid major leaguer for a long time. The noise about him among disappointed fans, while understandable because of where he was drafted, is way overblown. 

Clubs covet players like Crews, especially if he ends up hitting a little more than he has. He will have value to teams, including the Nats, because he's an excellent defender (87th percentile range) and an elite base runner (92nd percentile FRV). He also hits the ball very hard (71st percentile XV). Has he lived up to the No. 2 pick hype and expectation? Not even close. Is he a good, helpful player who fans are way too down on? Also, yes. 

4) The only Nationals who should be untouchable in trade talks this offseason are James Wood and Cade Cavalli. There is nobody else on the roster that Paul Toboni should avoid listening to offers on. That doesn't mean you have to trade anybody. But you only have two guys who are off limits. 

5) While not "an untouchable," Daylen Lile is a player the Nationals should be looking to extend rather than shop. He improved immensely on defense last year and has a chance to be a building block for a long time to come. 

6) I'm expecting a CJ Abrams trade. Does the work stoppage make it hard to get done until the deadline? I guess that's possible. But he's coming off a career year and can be sold at a high price and he and the team don't see eye-to-eye on what position he should play.

The personal scandal and the geopolitical claim are two completely different things.
Jensen Huang’s private conduct is for Nvidia and the people involved to address. The allegation that Chinese intelligence targeted him remains entirely unproven — China has already dismissed it as a baseless smear, and no credible evidence has been presented.
Yet in Washington, the two are being deliberately blurred. For critics of Trump, the affair becomes a convenient tool to attack his chip policy and his relationship with Huang. For export hawks in both parties, it offers fresh political cover for restrictions they already wanted. Huang’s long-standing push to sell chips to China is now being reframed as a “security risk” by the same people who opposed it from the start.
Personal failings do not equal foreign interference. Unproven accusations should not be used to settle unrelated policy fights. China is not required to serve as a scapegoat for Washington’s internal battles.

text:
Jensen Huang admits to an affair. Nvidia opens an investigation. And in Washington, an old proposal to tighten chip restrictions on China suddenly gets a new selling point.

The two issues must be separated: his affair is one thing. The claim that Chinese intelligence targeted him remains unproven, and China has rejected it as a groundless smear.

So why blur the two in Washington?

For Trump's critics, the scandal puts his decision to ease some chip restrictions and his ties to Huang under the spotlight. For export hawks in both parties, it gives fresh momentum to restrictions they already wanted. And for Huang, his push to keep selling chips to China is now being cast as a security liability by people who opposed it in the first place.

Huang should answer for his conduct. Washington can fight over Trump's chip policy. China doesn't owe either of them a scapegoat. #MediaUnlocked

The Council of Clermont was a mixed synod of ecclesiastics and laymen of the Catholic Church, called by Pope Urban II and held from 17 to 27 November 1095 at Clermont, Auvergne, at the time part of the Duchy of Aquitaine.[1][2]

While the council is known today primarily for the speech Pope Urban gave on the final day, it was primarily a synod focused on implementing the Cluniac reforms, enacting decrees and settling local and regional issues.[3] This also included the extension of the excommunication of Philip I of France for his adulterous remarriage to Bertrade of Montfort and a declaration of renewal of the Truce of God, an attempt on the part of the church to reduce feuding among Frankish nobles.[4]

Pope Urban's speech on 27 November included the call to arms that would result in the First Crusade,[5] and eventually the capture of Jerusalem and the establishment of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. In this, Urban reacted to the request by Byzantine emperor Alexius I Comnenus who had sent envoys to the Council of Piacenza requesting military assistance against the Seljuk Turks.[6] Several accounts of the speech survive; of these, the one by Fulcher of Chartres, who was present at the council, is generally accepted as the most reliable.

The Knights of Malta (historically known as the Knights Hospitaller or the Order of St. John) have deep historical ties to the areas in and around London’s Square Mile (the City of London).
While their primary medieval English headquarters was located just north of the City walls in Clerkenwell, they took ownership of significant property directly inside and bordering the Square Mile through major historical events.
1. The Temple District & Temple Church
The most prominent footprint of the Order directly bordering the Square Mile is the Temple district (located between Fleet Street and the River Thames).
The Takeover: This land originally belonged to their fierce medieval rivals, the Knights Templar. When the Templars were dissolved and suppressed by the Pope in 1312, a papal bull transferred their vast property portfolio over to the Knights Hospitaller (Knights of Malta).
The Legal Hub: The Hospitallers primarily treated the Temple property as a source of rental income. They leased the land out to professors and practitioners of law. These tenants eventually established the famous Inner Temple and Middle Temple—two of London's four Inns of Court that still dominate the legal landscape of the City today.
The Architecture: The stunning 12th-century Temple Church, famous for its circular nave mimicking Jerusalem's Holy Sepulchre, officially belonged to the Hospitallers for over two centuries until Henry VIII seized it during the Reformation.
2. Clerkenwell Priory (Just Outside the Walls)
Though situated just a short walk north of the Square Mile's formal boundary, the Order's true power center in London was the Clerkenwell Priory.
Established in the 1140s, this massive 10-acre fortified precinct served as the administrative and financial hub for all of England.
From here, the Order managed profits from hundreds of British estates to fund their crusader castles and naval fleets in the Mediterranean (first in Rhodes, and later Malta).
Today, you can still visit the surviving St. John’s Gate and the medieval crypt beneath the Museum of the Order of St John in Clerkenwell.
3. Modern Presence
The modern continuation of the order, the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, remains very active in London. Their primary religious activities and Grand Priory of England chapter room are located today at 23 Golden Square in London's West End, while their main British administrative office operates out of Putney.

The history of the Temple begins soon after the middle of the twelfth century, when a contingent of knights of the Military Order of the Temple of Solomon in Jerusalem moved from the Old Temple in Holborn (later Southampton House) to a larger site between Fleet Street and the banks of the River Thames. The new site originally included much of what is now Lincoln’s Inn, and the knights were probably responsible for establishing New Street (later Chancery Lane), which led from Holborn down to their new quarters. Following their custom, the knights built a round church patterned on the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. An inscription on the Round recorded that it was consecrated by the Patriarch Heraclius on 10 February 1185, in honour of the Blessed Virgin Mary. It is thought that King Henry II was also present on that day, inaugurating a long association between the royal family and the Temple.

Among the other buildings erected by the knights were dormitories, storehouses, stables, chambers, and two dining halls, one of them in the consecrated central portion and connected with the church by a cloister. It was a house fit for kings to stay in, and several did so. During a visit by King John in January 1215 he received a deputation of barons demanding a charter of liberties; and when the Great Charter was signed later in the year, the Master of the Temple was one of the witnesses. The knights took advantage of their special privileges to make their sanctuary a safe place for depositing treasure, and during the thirteenth century the New Temple became a busy financial centre. It was no doubt during this period that the first handful of lawyers came to live in the Temple, not as distinct societies but as legal advisers to a wealthy international organisation. The Templars thrived, adding to their round church a fine nave, which was consecrated in the presence of King Henry III in 1240. Many knights associated with the order were buried in the church, the most distinguished being William Marshal (d. 1219), first Earl of Pembroke and regent of England, the very model of medieval English chivalry, and one of the instigators of Magna Carta. Marshal’s armoured effigy, battered by time and war, may still be seen in the Round.

After losing the Holy Land in the 1290s, the order of the Temple fell into a decline. The knights were dubiously accused of improprieties, and in 1312 their order was dissolved. Although the pope granted their estates to the Knights Hospitaller of St John of Jerusalem, King Edward II seized the New Temple as forfeit to the Crown. Nevertheless, the consecrated portion was conceded to the Hospitallers, and the remainder was sold to them later.

 We are faced here with the question whether claims for losses allegedly suffered at the hands of a Nazi puppet regime during World War II are cognizable in our courts today. Because these claims, at least superficially, touch on foreign relations and potentially controversial political issues, it is tempting to jump to the conclusion that such claims are barred by the political question doctrine. The Supreme Court has counseled, however, that “it is error to suppose that every case or controversy which touches foreign relations lies beyond judicial cognizance.” Baker v. Carr, 369 U.S. 186, 211, 82 S.Ct. 691, 7 L.Ed.2d 663 (1962). The justiciability inquiry is limited to “ ‘political questions,’ not ․ ‘political cases,’ ” id. at 217, 82 S.Ct. 691, and should be made on a “case-by-case” basis, id. at 211, 82 S.Ct. 691.

Although the political question doctrine often lurks in the shadows of cases involving foreign relations, it is infrequently addressed head on. See, e.g., Hwang Geum Joo v. Japan, 332 F.3d 679, 682 (D.C.Cir.2003), vacated and remanded by 542 U.S. 901, 124 S.Ct. 2835, 159 L.Ed.2d 265 (2004) (explaining that because the district court did not have subject matter jurisdiction in case involving World War II-era claims against Japan, “[n]or ․ need we consider whether the political question doctrine would also bar its adjudication”). The procedural posture of this case, however, places the issue squarely before us.

What actually happened: 
Carvajal pleaded guilty in U.S. court in June 2025 to narcoterrorism, drug trafficking, and related charges. In early December 2025, while in federal custody, he wrote a letter (dated Dec. 2) addressed to President Trump and the American public. His attorney shared it with the Dallas Express (and it was covered by outlets including the Miami Herald). In it, he made broad allegations about the Maduro regime, including:That the Venezuelan government (under Chávez and Maduro) operated as a criminal/narco enterprise.
That U.S. diplomats and CIA officers were paid to help keep Chávez and Maduro in power.
Claims involving drug trafficking (Cartel of the Suns), Tren de Aragua, Cuban intelligence, Hezbollah ties, Smartmatic, and efforts to destabilize the U.S.
The letter does not name any specific U.S. senators, members of Congress, or other elected officials, and it does not contain or reference any “Venezuela List” of politicians receiving kickbacks.⁠SnopesOrigin of the viral claim
The specific “list” of senators (mostly Democrats, plus some Republicans such as McConnell, Grassley, Murkowski, etc.) and the framing about them undermining anti-Maduro efforts originated in social media posts (including one by an X user named Joshua Hall in December 2025). Those posts provided no primary documents, court filings, or authenticated evidence. Fact-checkers, including Snopes, found no supporting evidence that Carvajal released or confirmed any such roster.⁠SnopesNo major news organizations, DOJ statements, court records, or other credible sources have corroborated a verified list of senators receiving millions from the Maduro regime.
