A fandom shouldn’t be measured by how many people can repeat the same bullish message.

It should be measured by what its members contribute.

That’s one thing I find interesting about @IPXExchange FAN SZN.

Two people can support the same project in completely different ways. One creates educational content, another brings new people into the community, while someone else contributes through consistent discussions and participation.

FAN SZN gives these contributions a way to be recognized through Aura.

ALFRED adds another interesting layer by evaluating submitted content and awarding randomized Aura based on its assessment. That means simply tagging @IPXExchange isn’t the point. The content itself needs to offer something.

Having managed Web3 communities, I’ve seen how quickly engagement becomes repetitive when everyone feels pressured to post the same talking points.

I’d rather see someone explain a feature in their own words, share a useful observation or introduce a perspective nobody else has considered.

That’s how a community develops its own identity.

The strongest fandoms don’t create an army of people saying the same thing. They create a community of people with different things worth saying.

text:
One distinction I think every @IPXExchange supporter should understand is this: funding and ownership are not the same thing.

A creator can raise funds using their intellectual property without necessarily giving up ownership of the original work.

But if I’m backing that project with USDC or $IPX, I want to know exactly what I’m getting in return.

Let’s use a documentary as an example.

Fans fund its production, then a brand licenses a clip for an advertising campaign. Who receives that revenue? Does the creator keep everything, do supporters receive a defined share, or does the arrangement follow another agreed structure?

That answer should be clear before anyone contributes.

The token alone doesn’t tell me what rights I have. Those rights must be defined in the project’s terms and enforceable agreements.

This is why I think IPX needs to make three things transparent before every raise:

What the creator retains.
What rights or benefits supporters receive.
Whether supporters have any contractual claim to future revenue.

A completed production is valuable, but a transparent agreement showing exactly how its commercial success affects its backers is even more important.

My question for @IPXExchange: how can supporters verify these rights and revenue terms before committing funds?

Because trust in tokenized IP shouldn’t begin after a project makes money. It should begin before the first contribution.

text:
IPX calls itself an operating system for intellectual property. I think that’s one of the most interesting parts of what @IPXExchange is building, but it also raises a question worth exploring.

What’s the actual difference between an IP marketplace and an OS for IP?

A marketplace allows people to discover, buy and sell projects. An operating system should go further by providing infrastructure that other developers and businesses can build on.

Think about what that could mean in practice.

A filmmaker launches a documentary through IPX. The project raises production capital, distributes tokens and progresses through milestone-based funding.

Now imagine an independent developer building a dashboard that tracks the documentary’s entire journey: how much it has raised, which production milestones have been completed, when funding is released and how much revenue it generates after distribution.

That developer shouldn’t have to build an entirely separate system for every documentary.

Or consider a brand looking for licensing opportunities. Instead of manually searching through individual projects, a third-party application could potentially allow the brand to filter available IP by genre, audience, funding status and licensing terms.

Another developer could build a rights dashboard that helps token holders understand the benefits and contractual entitlements attached to their holdings across multiple projects.

These are just three possible applications, but they illustrate the bigger opportunity.

For this to work, however, infrastructure matters.

I’d want to see public APIs, developer documentation, smart-contract interfaces and reliable ways to access project data. Developers also need clear permission boundaries so private contracts and restricted information aren’t exposed.

This is where I think IPX’s four pillars become particularly interesting:

Tokenize, Advertise, Monetize and Distribute.

If these functions are connected at the infrastructure level, independent applications could potentially combine them in ways the original platform never anticipated.

A developer could build a tool that discovers tokenized films, connects them with suitable advertisers and tracks the commercial performance of those projects.

That’s a much bigger opportunity than simply creating another marketplace feature.

But I have one important question for @IPXExchange:

What can an independent developer actually build on top of IPX today?

Are there public APIs, developer tools or smart-contract interfaces that allow external applications to interact with projects across the ecosystem?

Because there’s a difference between a platform that offers many products and an operating system that allows an entire developer ecosystem to emerge around it.

As someone interested in building blockchain applications, that’s the part I’d love to explore.

The real strength of an OS isn’t just what its original developers create.

It’s what they make possible for everyone else.

🔸 November 11 - Saint Menas the Great-Martyr 🗡️🔸

Today, we commemorate the Great-Martyr Saint Menas of Egypt. The holy military officer suffered for Christ during the reign of the Emperor Diocletian (284-305). St Menas was born in Egypt in 285 AD to ascetic Christian parents. His father, a ruler of one of the administrative divisions of Egypt, died when Menas was 14 years old. At the age of 15, Menas joined the army. He was given a high rank because of his father’s reputation, and was stationed in Cotyaeum, Anatolia (today Kütahya, Turkey).

In 298, the Emperor published an edict ordering everyone to worship the pagan idols, or otherwise face persecution, torture and death. After hearing this order, Menas gave up his military position and withdrew to a the seclusion of a mountain where he kept vigil and lived an ascetic life of fasting and prayer. Living as hermit, the Saint purified himself of every passion of the soul and body. Whilst in prayer, he heard a divine voice call to him: “Blessed are you, Abba Menas, because you have been called for the pious life from your childhood. You shall be granted three immortal crowns; one because of your celibacy, the second because of your asceticism, and the third for your martyrdom.”

With his heart aflame with love for God, Menas left the mountain and bravely returned to the city, where the people were celebrating a pagan festival. Standing in the midst of the crowd, Menas triumphantly declared Christ as the One True God, and shouted that the pagan idols were nothing more than inanimate objects made of metal, wood, and stone. Menas was beaten and thrown into prison for this outburst by the Roman authorities, and was brought before Pyrrhus, the city prefect.

Phyrrus offered to restore Menas to his former rank in the Army if he would offer sacrifice to the pagan gods, but St Menas affirmed that he would never deny Christ. After suffering many tortures including being bound to a wooden post and having his skin flayed with sharp metal hooks, he finally received the crown of martyrdom by beheading in the year 304. The valour with which he suffered for Christ converted many pagans to the True Faith.

War and the years taken from veterans

Veterans often speak of lost years. Some lost years to deployments, missing the births of children, the deaths of parents, the ordinary life of home. Some lost years after their return, to post-traumatic stress, depression, addiction, or the slow work of recovering from wounds. Some lost years to the moral injury that comes from having done, seen, or failed to prevent things that violate their conscience. Some lost the person they were before they went to war.

Part 10 treats war, veterans, and moral injury at length. Here it is enough to say that Joel 2:25 belongs to veterans as much as to anyone. The "great army" of locusts in Joel is a military image; the prophet speaks the language soldiers know. And the God who commands armies promises to restore the years that the army took. For the veteran who feels that war has eaten their life, the pastor can offer this word: God knows what was taken, He counts every year, and He is able to restore.

Broken families and the years of division

For many families, the locust years are years of division. A divorce splits a household, and children grow up moving between two homes. A quarrel between siblings over an inheritance leads to decades of silence. A parent's addiction or abuse leaves wounds that shape every family gathering. 
Adult children estranged from their parents, and parents who do not know where their children are, carry a grief that can last a lifetime.

Joel's promise reaches these losses too. God can restore relationships that seemed dead. 

Reconciliations happen, sometimes after many years. 

The Sunday of Forgiveness, when the faithful bow to one another and ask pardon (Part 2), is a liturgical sign of this hope. But the pastor must also be realistic. Reconciliation requires two parties, and sometimes one is unwilling or unable. In such cases, the person who longs for reconciliation can still forgive, can still pray, and can still entrust the broken relationship to God, who will restore all things in the end.

Years that are not given back in this life

Honesty requires one more word. Some losses are not restored in this life. A spouse dies before reconciliation comes. A parent dies after a long illness that no one could cure. A grown child does not come home. The person who has prayed Joel 2:25 over such a loss may feel that the promise has failed.

The Church does not answer this with a forced smile. She answers with the Resurrection. Joel's promise looks beyond the harvest to the day of the Lord, and the Church reads it in the light of the empty tomb. What is not restored here is not lost to God. The last word of Scripture on these years is not the locust but the promise: "And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying" (Revelation 21:4). Meanwhile the Church prays for the departed by name and so keeps the bond of love unbroken.

Alas for the day! 
The Prophet Joel; for the 21st Century 
A Practical Resource for Orthodox Christian Clergy and Laity Alike  

Why this book  
The Book of Joel is short. In the English Bible it has only three chapters, and in the Septuagint four; anyone can read it aloud in under ten minutes. 

Yet the Orthodox Church hears Joel at some of the most important doors of Her year: on the Wednesday of Cheesefare Week, as Great Lent draws near, when the prophet cries "turn to me with all your heart" (Joel 2:12 LXX); at the Vespers of Pentecost, when the Church remembers the promise "I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh" (Joel 3:1 LXX = 2:28 KJV); and on Joel's feast, October 19.  

Joel's people faced locusts that came in waves. Ours have other names: loneliness and despair, addiction and the endless screen, broken families and money worries, illness, war and its wounds, and a steady anxiety about the future. Joel's answer, and the Church's, is not a self-help program but a call to turn to God together, and a promise that God will answer.  

For whom it is written  
Earlier versions of this work were written for Priests and Deacons. This edition is written for the whole Church: for Clergy, and for the Laity with whom they pray, fast, and serve.  

There is a reason for the change, and it is in Joel himself. When the prophet calls the solemn assembly, he does not call the Priests alone. He calls, "gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the infants at the breast" (Joel 2:16 LXX), and he summons even the bridegroom and the bride from their wedding. 

The Priests have their own place: "Between the porch and the altar let the Priests that minister to the Lord weep" (Joel 2:17 LXX). But they weep for a people who are standing with them. A book about Joel that spoke only to Clergy would leave out half of Joel.  

So this book speaks to both. Clergy will still find homily seeds, notes for the confessor, and frank pages on the strain of ministry. Laity will find the same Fathers and the same Scripture in plain English, with practical counsel for prayer, fasting, family, work, grief, and service. Neither is asked to do the other's work. Both are asked to stand where Joel put them, together, before God.  

The book still keeps a special place for wounded veterans and for those who live with lasting illness or disability, who are in our pews, at our altars, and in our homes. Its pastoral sketches are composites, not accounts of real persons; yet real persons were the impetus of the accounts.  

This book also speaks to those who run toward trouble for the rest of us: firefighters and police officers, paramedics and dispatchers, emergency room staff, chaplains, hospice and bereavement workers, and all who minister at deaths and funerals, as well as veterans. 

The toll of that work on their hearts, minds, and bodies can be overwhelming. Part 11 speaks to them directly, and Part 12 to the Parish that receives them. Part 12 also says more about the Orthodox household: why a family should learn Joel together, and how to keep a family altar and a simple daily rule as a little church.  https://t.co/YwtXXB4JwN

But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people: the Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing: which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation. But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: how much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth. Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood. For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these. For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us: nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others; for then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself. And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment: so Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.”

text:
Veterans Day 2026: Free Meals & Deals for Those Who Served

Today is Wednesday, November 11, 2026 — Veterans Day. Across the United States, restaurants are saying thank you with free meals, entrees, sides, drinks, and discounts for active-duty service members, veterans, National Guard, Reserves, and in some cases military families or first responders.

Most offers are dine-in only, require valid military ID, VA card, DD-214, or other proof of service, and can vary by location or franchise. Call ahead, check the restaurant’s site or socials, and expect lines. Offers can change, so confirm before you go.

Here are some of the standout free meals and deals happening today:

 Full Free Meals & Big Entrees
- Golden Corral — Free dinner buffet + beverage (4 p.m. to close) for anyone who has served. Dine-in only.
- Bob Evans — Free entree from a special menu of 11 breakfast/lunch/dinner options + a future-visit coupon for sausage gravy and biscuits.
- Denny’s — Free meal (examples include Original Grand Slam) with valid ID.
- Chili’s — Free item from a special Veterans Day menu (Chicken Crispers, Oldtimer Burger, quesadillas, or soup + salad).
- Cracker Barrel — Free Sunrise Pancake Special + 25% off Military Collection merch (through Nov. 12) and a year-round 10% military discount in the app.
- IHOP — Free “Red, White & Blue(berry)” pancake combo with eggs, hash browns, and bacon or sausage (7 a.m.–7 p.m.).
- Applebee’s — Free full-size entree from a special menu (historically options like steak, bacon cheeseburger, or chicken tenders) + often a bounce-back card.
- Olive Garden — Free entree from a select menu (past options have included spaghetti and meatballs, fettuccine Alfredo, chicken parm, or unlimited soup/salad/breadsticks).
- Red Robin — Free Red’s Big Tavern Burger with Bottomless Steak Fries (no purchase needed).
- Wendy’s — Free Dave’s Single (participating U.S. locations; no purchase needed; excludes digital/delivery/kiosk).

Wings, Burgers & Casual Favorites
- Buffalo Wild Wings — Free order of 10 boneless wings (“Wings for Heroes”).
- Hooters — Free item (10 Original wings, cheeseburger, Buffalo chicken sandwich, or Chicken Caesar salad) with a drink purchase.
- Smashburger — Free All-American Smash burger or American Big Dog.
- Hopdoddy — Free Classic Burger (or with cheese).
- Bad Daddy’s Burger Bar — Free burger with cheese + a side (11 a.m.–3 p.m.).

Breakfast & Coffee
- Dunkin’ — Free donut with in-store purchase.
- Krispy Kreme — Free doughnut + small brewed coffee (one per guest).
- Starbucks — Free tall hot or iced coffee (for veterans, active-duty, and military spouses at participating locations).
- Hy-Vee — Free breakfast (6–10 a.m. at stores with hot food) + 15% off groceries with code VETS2026.
- Keke’s Breakfast Cafe — Free Classic Two Egg Combo.

More Notable Offers 
- Outback Steakhouse — Free Bloomin’ Onion + beverage (Nov. 10–11); also standing 10% Heroes discount.
- Bonefish Grill — Free Bang Bang Shrimp + nonalcoholic beverage.
- Little Caesar's — Free HOT-N-READY Lunch Combo (4 slices + 20-oz Pepsi, 11 a.m.–2 p.m.).
- Qdoba / Chipotle — Free chips and dip (with minimum purchase at Chipotle).
- Firehouse Subs — BOGO free sub (any size, in-store).
- Taziki’s — Free Grilled Chicken Gyro meal (“Gyros for Heroes”).
- Sonny’s BBQ — Free Pork Big Deal (sandwich + side + drink).
- Pilot Flying J — Free breakfast sandwich + coffee or lunch item + fountain drink (via app verification).

This is only a sample — dozens more chains (Blaze Pizza, Capriotti’s, California Pizza Kitchen, Red Lobster, and many regional places) are participating with free entrees, appetizers, discounts, or full meals. Many also offer year-round military discounts.

Quick tips for today:
- Bring proof of service.
- Call your local restaurant first.
- Most are dine-in; some allow takeout.
- Family members may get discounts at certain places.
- Check apps or rewards programs for extra perks.

Thank you to every veteran and service member. Enjoy the free meal — you’ve earned it. Share with fellow vets so more people can take advantage!

Happy Veterans Day. 🇺🇸

[A Little Winter Shopping Detour in Nihonbashi, Tokyo]

What if shopping for children’s winter clothes could also be part of discovering a different side of Tokyo?

“We need a warmer jacket for our child.”
“It’s hard to tell the color and thickness from online photos.”
“If we’re going into central Tokyo, why not explore the neighborhood too?”

Welcome to Kids Bird, a baby and children’s clothing shop in Nihonbashi Yokoyamacho, Tokyo. Our store is filling up with winter fashion: fluffy textures, cozy layers, jackets and sweatshirts. It feels like winter the moment you look around.

Our attached store-tour video runs about 3 minutes and 55 seconds. That’s longer than a typical social media clip, but we wanted to show you the actual shop, not just a few polished seconds. Pause whenever you spot something you like. You might discover an outfit worth looking for on your next trip to Tokyo.

📍 Kids Bird: 6-12 Nihonbashi Yokoyamacho, Chuo-ku, Tokyo
🚃 About 2 minutes on foot from Bakuro-yokoyama, Bakurocho and Higashi-nihombashi stations
👶 Baby to junior clothing, with sizes from around 50 to 160 cm
🛍️ Everyone is welcome to shop on the first floor, even for just one item.

If you’re staying at a hotel in the Bakurocho, Higashi-Nihombashi, Yokoyamacho or Asakusabashi area, this could be an easy neighborhood shopping stop rather than a major trip across the city. And if you’re planning a Tokyo holiday from overseas, read on: we’ve included real nearby hotel names and sightseeing ideas to help you find us.

Save this winter-shopping guide for Tokyo.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
01 | When the fluffy winter clothes arrive, the whole shop changes.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Spring and summer bring light fabrics and bright colors. In winter, our rails fill with fuller jackets, soft-looking sweatshirts and textures you want to examine up close. The same little shop takes on a new personality as the seasons change.

In the video you’ll see racks of winter outerwear, stacks of clothing in different colors, outfits for girls, pants for boys, baby clothes, character designs, umbrellas and other accessories. It’s more than an announcement that winter stock has arrived. It’s a glimpse of what walking through the store actually feels like.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
02 | Did you know there is a children’s clothing shop here in Nihonbashi?
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Many visitors associate Nihonbashi with department stores, traditional shops or the business district. But Yokoyamacho and Bakurocho have another story: generations of clothing and accessory wholesalers working in the heart of Tokyo.

Some wholesale stores in the area do not sell to individual shoppers. Kids Bird is different: our first-floor retail shop welcomes everyone, and you can buy a single piece of clothing. No business account or wholesale purchase is required. If you’ve ever passed by wondering whether you were allowed in, the answer is yes!

━━━━━━━━━━━━
03 | A family of children’s clothing specialists since 1954.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Kids Bird is operated by Toyo Iryo Co., Ltd., a company founded in 1954. We’ve seen fashions change, but the everyday needs behind children’s clothes remain familiar: comfort, practicality, fit and the excitement of finding something a child loves.

There are very different reasons for coming in. A family might need a practical extra layer for nursery, a grandparent might be searching for a thoughtful gift, and a visitor might simply want to see a real Tokyo children’s clothing shop rather than another big shopping mall. We hope each can enjoy browsing at their own pace. Our history belongs to the company; the shop’s present is in the video, on the racks and shelves today.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
04 | Start your winter shopping with a jacket.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before choosing, ask how the jacket will be worn. Is it for school, nursery, weekends or a family holiday? Will your child wear a thick sweatshirt underneath? Are the hood, fastener and length suitable for your routine? The answers matter as much as the design.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
05 | Soft, fluffy, cozy: the textures of winter.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

There’s something irresistible about winter clothing that looks soft to the touch. Fleecy surfaces, plush-looking fabrics and fluffy details make the shop feel warmer even before anyone tries anything on.

Not every soft-looking garment is made the same way. Fleece, brushed interiors, boa-style pile, linings and thickness vary by product. A photo may not reveal these differences, which is one reason visiting a real store can be helpful.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
06 | Winter outfits for girls: style and everyday versatility.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Our store-tour video shows tops, jackets and outfit ideas for girls, from gentle shades to more playful designs. Children’s tastes change quickly. Last year’s favorite color might suddenly be replaced by something completely different!

If you’re travelling with children, let them point out what catches their eye. Maybe it’s the texture of a jacket, a cheerful print or a color they’d never normally choose at home. For families visiting Japan, a practical piece bought on the trip can become part of a memory: the warm top worn on a chilly morning, or the outfit chosen while exploring an unfamiliar neighborhood. Please remember that sizes and designs vary by product, so ask us if you’re searching for something particular.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
07 | Winter clothes for boys: room to move and room for personality.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Running, bending, climbing and sitting: childhood is full of movement. When shopping for boys’ winter clothes, the daily routine matters as much as the print or color. In the video you’ll see jackets, casual tops and racks of pants.

It’s useful to think about the clothes your child already has. A colorful sweatshirt may work best with a simple pair of pants; a patterned top could make a familiar outfit feel new. Winter trips also mean layers: what is comfortable for a long train ride may be different from what works outside on a cold afternoon. Our range changes, but choosing a useful item that fits the child’s ordinary routine is always a good place to start.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
08 | Baby clothes: tiny outfits for big everyday moments.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

There’s a special charm in a rack of baby clothing: tiny sleeves, delicate proportions, gentle colors and soft-looking materials. Our video also visits this part of the store. Whether you’re preparing for a new baby, shopping for your grandchild or looking for a gift, we’d love you to see it.

If you’re visiting with a baby, it’s sensible to plan breaks and check facilities in advance. Our store accepts strollers and has a ramp at the entrance, but it does not have a nursing room or diaper-changing station. We want parents to know that before visiting so they can plan a comfortable outing. There is no pressure to shop quickly; choose a time that suits your family and check our opening hours first.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
09 | From newborn sizes to clothes for older kids.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

You might assume a baby shop stops at toddler sizes. Or you might think a junior clothing shop has nothing for a newborn. Kids Bird brings a wide range together: approximately 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 95, 100, 110, 120, 130, 140, 150 and 160 cm.

That does not mean every design comes in every size. Each product has its own size range, and particular colors or sizes may sell out. If you’re looking for something specific, please ask in store or contact us before making a special trip.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
10 | Character clothing and the magic of “That’s the one!”
━━━━━━━━━━━━

A child’s face can light up when they spot a favorite character or print. The video includes eye-catching character designs and playful graphics. To an adult, two tops may look similar. To a child, one particular design can feel like the most important choice in the world.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
11 | Sometimes all you need is one more everyday piece.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

A full wardrobe refresh isn’t always necessary. Maybe the morning air has turned colder. Maybe you need more clothes between laundry days. Maybe there’s a favorite pair of pants waiting for the right top.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
12 | Don’t forget to look at the accessories.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

The video isn’t just about clothes. You’ll also see areas with bags, umbrellas and other everyday accessories. Sometimes you come for a jacket and discover a useful item you hadn’t planned to look for.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
13 | A good find may be hiding on an ordinary rack.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Alongside everyday clothing, Kids Bird sometimes has special-price items and other budget-friendly finds. Looking carefully through the racks can reveal an unexpected color, size or design you might otherwise miss.

We can’t promise the same bargains every day. Products, prices and available quantities change, and some items sell out. The attached video shows one moment in the life of the store, not a permanent catalog.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
14 | Seeing the real item can change the questions you ask.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

In a physical store you can compare colors, inspect the fabric and think about proportions. You can also explain what you’re looking for and ask us about the available choices. We may not be able to answer every question, but we’ll do our best to help you find a starting point.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
15 | Not a huge department store. A small discovery instead.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Kids Bird is a relatively compact specialty shop, not a multi-level department store. That makes it easy to include in a neighborhood stroll or combine with errands elsewhere in Tokyo.

If you’re expecting a vast flagship store with several floors, this isn’t that kind of experience. You might notice a tightly packed rail, a familiar cartoon design or a little section of everyday items instead. We think that is part of its charm. You can see a real independent-style neighborhood shop at work and decide what suits your family without having to spend a whole afternoon shopping.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
16 | Now, let’s explore Nihonbashi like a travel magazine.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Japanese travel publication Rurubu & more. has featured Amazake Yokocho and the Yokoyamacho wholesale district as places to discover on foot. You don’t need to follow a strict sightseeing itinerary. Visit a children’s clothing shop, enjoy a nearby street and stop for something tasty if you feel like it. You can plan a short loop around your hotel rather than a full day of travel.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
17 | A little detour: Amazake Yokocho in Ningyocho.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Amazake Yokocho is known for its traditional shopping-street atmosphere. Sweet shops, places to eat and long-established businesses make it a lovely area for a relaxed walk. Instead of racing from attraction to attraction, enjoy seeing what each storefront offers.

One idea: take a snack break around Ningyocho, then stroll toward Higashi-nihombashi and Bakuro-yokoyama to look for children’s winter clothes at Kids Bird. It’s a day out with both neighborhood character and a practical shopping stop.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
18 | Another detour: a gentle walk through Hamacho.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Between Ningyocho and Hamacho, you can find quieter streets and a different pace from Tokyo’s busiest districts. Hamacho Park is one possible place to include if you’d like a little greenery or a break before continuing your shopping day.

Please note that parts of Hamacho Park may have temporary access restrictions related to local construction. If the park is a main reason for your trip, check the latest information from Chuo City before setting off.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
19 | Look around the Yokoyamacho and Bakurocho wholesale streets.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

For a different kind of Tokyo experience, explore the streets around Yokoyamacho and Bakurocho. This area has long been connected to the trade in clothes, textiles and accessories. It has the atmosphere of a place where people have worked with products and customers for generations.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
20 | Staying in a hotel nearby? Kids Bird may be just around the corner.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Some Tokyo visitors choose hotels near the famous tourist centers. Others discover how convenient the Bakurocho and Higashi-Nihombashi station area can be. This neighborhood has rail connections, places to eat, practical everyday shops and a quieter atmosphere than some major nightlife districts. It can be a useful base for visitors who want to explore different parts of Tokyo rather than stay in a single sightseeing zone.

If your hotel address includes “Nihonbashi Bakurocho,” “Nihonbashi Yokoyamacho,” “Higashi-Nihombashi” or “Asakusabashi,” look up Kids Bird on your map. We may be close enough to add to your morning walk, your afternoon return to the hotel or a short outing between other plans. You don’t need to set aside a whole day simply to visit us.

We aren’t affiliated with the hotels mentioned below, and we aren’t offering hotel bookings. We’re naming them to help visitors recognize the area. Walking routes and times depend on your particular hotel entrance, luggage, children and the route you choose.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
21 | Hotel neighbors: some names you may recognize from your booking.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

One especially close landmark is APA Hotel Nihombashi Bakuroyokoyama Ekimae at 5-6 Nihonbashi Yokoyamacho. Kids Bird is at 6-12 in the same Yokoyamacho neighborhood. If that is where you are staying, you can plan a short local stroll to our shop rather than a cross-city shopping trip.

Other nearby accommodation names include Comfort Hotel Tokyo Higashi Nihombashi (in Nihonbashi Bakurocho), DDD HOTEL (also in Nihonbashi Bakurocho), and Toyoko Inn Tokyo Nihombashi Bakurocho (in the Odenmacho area). Their official access guides place them around Bakurocho or nearby stations. If you are staying at one of these properties, check a walking route from the lobby to our address; you may find it makes sense to stop in while exploring the streets around your hotel.

The useful message is simple: you don’t have to be staying in a famous shopping district to find children’s clothes. Sometimes there is a small specialty shop in the neighborhood where you are already spending the night. Save our address so you can find it when your itinerary allows.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
22 | Explore Ningyocho, Amazake Yokocho and Suitengu Shrine.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Ningyocho is a lovely place to slow down and notice details. Around Amazake Yokocho you’ll find the atmosphere of an old Tokyo shopping street: traditional snacks, sweets, places for a meal and businesses with stories that go back generations. It’s the sort of neighborhood that rewards curiosity. You don’t have to buy anything to enjoy peeking into the windows and noticing how different it feels from Tokyo’s busiest shopping avenues.

Suitengu Shrine is another well-known point of interest in the Ningyocho area, traditionally associated with safe childbirth and family blessings. If cultural history interests you, it can be an addition to a neighborhood walk. Please observe the usual manners around places of worship, and check the shrine’s own visitor information if you plan to visit for a specific service or ceremony.

A gentle idea for a family day: enjoy Ningyocho’s streets, choose somewhere suitable for lunch, then head toward Bakuro-yokoyama to visit Kids Bird. Don’t turn it into a race. With children, the moments between planned stops are often the most memorable ones.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
23 | Asakusabashi: a different kind of shopping street.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Asakusabashi is worth remembering if you enjoy crafts, accessories and traditional Japanese details. The area has long been associated with dolls, beads, hobby materials and small wholesale businesses. Some stores sell to the general public, while others focus on trade customers; checking the individual store’s rules is part of the adventure.

For visitors who have already explored Tokyo’s large department stores, a walk through Asakusabashi can offer another perspective. Here, the pleasure is less about a giant shopping center and more about noticing a doll display, a collection of craft supplies or a tiny shop that specializes in one category. It’s also a neighborhood with stations that make it convenient to travel onward.

Kids Bird sits in the neighboring Yokoyamacho/Bakurocho area, so you can combine an Asakusabashi stroll with a children’s clothing stop. If you are staying near Asakusabashi Station, look up our address and choose a suitable route. This is an especially nice plan for travelers who appreciate local shops rather than crowded malls.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
24 | Visiting Asakusa and Senso-ji? Add a local shopping stop.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Asakusa is a classic Tokyo destination, especially for visitors who want to see Senso-ji Temple and the atmosphere of Nakamise shopping street. It can be a wonderful day for visitors of different ages, but it’s also a popular area. After taking in the sights, some families appreciate a quieter shopping stop away from the busiest sightseeing streets.

Higashi-Nihombashi Station, close to Kids Bird, is served by the Toei Asakusa Line, which connects with the Asakusa area. That makes it possible to include our neighborhood in a wider day of sightseeing without treating it as a separate distant destination. Check your travel planner for the service and station exit that suit your route.

Here’s an idea: explore Asakusa, enjoy the temple district and a snack, then travel toward Higashi-Nihombashi and browse children’s winter clothes if we’re still open. Or shop with us first and continue to Asakusa. We recommend planning around our closing time, not assuming that a neighborhood shop stays open late like a large shopping center.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
25 | Akihabara and Tokyo Station are useful reference points too.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Akihabara may be on your itinerary for electronics, anime, games or pop culture. Tokyo Station may be where you arrive, change trains or start a journey to another city. The Bakurocho/Yokoyamacho district sits within the wider central/eastern Tokyo transport network, so it can be an approachable extra stop if you plan your train route.

From JR Bakurocho Station you can use the Sobu Rapid Line toward Tokyo Station. Akihabara is accessible via nearby rail connections, including the Asakusabashi area. Rather than guessing an exact journey time, look at your travel planner with your starting station and the time of day. The important point is that Kids Bird is close to several train lines, not hidden far from public transport.

You may be visiting Tokyo for fashion, history, museums or anime. A little children’s clothing shop might not have been on the original list, but that’s sometimes where an unexpectedly useful souvenir or a favorite everyday outfit is found. Our aim isn’t to replace the famous sights. It’s to make a small, easy detour worth considering.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
26 | Three gentle travel ideas for families and hotel guests.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

PLAN A — A relaxed neighborhood morning: Begin around Ningyocho, walk past the traditional shops at Amazake Yokocho, have a snack or an early lunch, then visit Kids Bird during opening hours. This works well when you want to experience a real Tokyo neighborhood without spending most of the day in transit.

PLAN B — A hotel-neighborhood shopping break: If you’re staying in Bakurocho, Yokoyamacho, Higashi-Nihombashi or near Asakusabashi, look up the route to Kids Bird. Stop in to see winter jackets, baby clothes and casual pieces before continuing with the rest of your sightseeing. Keep the stop flexible, especially when traveling with small children.

PLAN C — Big sights, small shop: Spend part of the day in Asakusa or around Tokyo Skytree, then return toward the Higashi-Nihombashi/Bakurocho area. If it’s before closing and the family still has energy, take a look around our store. If not, save the address for the next suitable weekday. A pleasant trip is better than an overpacked schedule.

These are suggestions, not timed tours. Walking routes, accessibility, train services, opening hours and children’s energy levels all matter. Adjust the day to your own needs, and remember that the shop’s selection may change between the time you watch the video and your visit.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
27 | Come for the clothes, the walk, or a bit of both.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

There’s no single perfect way to visit. Perhaps you’re eating lunch in Ningyocho, exploring Hamacho, heading toward Asakusabashi or changing trains at Bakuro-yokoyama. A stop for children’s clothes can fit naturally into your plans.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
28 | A few helpful things to know before you visit.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

The public retail area of Kids Bird is on the FIRST FLOOR (ground level in US English). Our company also has a wholesale business, but individual shoppers are welcome downstairs. You can enter with a stroller, and there is a ramp at the entrance. Because the store is compact, moving around may be difficult at busy times.

Sizes, colors and styles change as stock sells. The video does not guarantee future availability. If you need one particular item, contact us before visiting. Opening hours can change too, especially on Saturdays, so please check the latest notice.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
29 | Easy to reach by train: remember these three stations.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

The company access guide lists roughly a two-minute walk from Bakuro-yokoyama Exit A1, Higashi-nihombashi Exit B4 and Bakurocho Exit C2. Kodenmacho Exit 1 is about eight minutes away, and JR Asakusabashi East Exit about nine minutes away.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
30 | When should you remember Kids Bird?
━━━━━━━━━━━━

When last year’s sleeves look a little short. When the morning air makes you wish your child had a warmer coat. When the right top is missing from an otherwise useful outfit. When you’re shopping for siblings or looking for a gift for a new baby.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
31 | Why did we leave the store-tour video so long?
━━━━━━━━━━━━

Short clips are convenient, but this time we wanted to keep a more complete sense of the store. The rails, stacks of clothing, colors, playful designs and extra volume of winter layers all help tell the story of what the shop looks like today.

━━━━━━━━━━━━
32 | Make a small children’s clothing shop part of your Tokyo story.
━━━━━━━━━━━━

When people imagine shopping in Tokyo, huge stations and famous department stores often come to mind. Those places are wonderful. But stepping into a small clothing specialist in a historic wholesale neighborhood offers a different experience.

We’re a small store, but we care about the clothes that children wear in their everyday lives. Whether you’ve shopped with us before or are discovering Kids Bird for the first time, we’d love to welcome you. Our fluffy winter collection is waiting. 🐥🧸❄️

[VISIT KIDS BIRD]
Kids Bird — Baby & Children’s Clothing
1F, Toyo Iryo Co., Ltd.
6-12 Nihonbashi Yokoyamacho, Chuo-ku, Tokyo 103-0003, Japan
Phone: +81-3-3661-4859
Access: Approx. 2 minutes’ walk from Bakuro-yokoyama Exit A1, Bakurocho Exit C2 or Higashi-nihombashi Exit B4
Hours: Mon-Fri 9:00 AM-4:30 PM / Sat 9:30 AM-3:00 PM / Closed Sundays and Japanese public holidays (hours may change; check before visiting)
Sizes: Mainly 50-160 cm, from baby clothes to junior styles; availability and sizes vary by product
Everyone can shop on the first floor. Strollers are welcome. No nursing or diaper-changing facilities inside.

Watch the attached 3-minute-55-second video for a look at the current winter display. Save this post if you’d like to visit, and share it with anyone planning a Tokyo trip or looking for children’s clothing in Japan.

text:
The conversion of Hagia Sophia into a mosque and Muslims praying in a building that does not belong to their historical or civilizational heritage, is the clearest proof that Islam is a barbaric religion that does not create, but only conquers and destroys. Also we all know that nobody visits Turkey for their "culture". You visit Turkey to see Greek-Byzantine heritage and Asia Minor to admire the Ancient Greek archaeological sites. 

I almost forgot it. Many people are visiting Turkey just to do a hair transplant. Oh, and of course the food. Which is Turkish only by name and of course you can find every single recipe in the Byzantine books and in the ancient Greek work of Athenaeus (Deipnosophists). Does anyone seriously believe that the "Turks" that supposedly came from the Steppes and they were nomads, were making wine and desserts? You have to be completely uneducated if you don't know that the real Turks were nomads living in tents moving all the time. But I don't really care about those things. I care about heritage and our lands that are occupied.

Both Constantinople & Istanbul are Greek words.

Istanbul comes from the Greek phrase "εἰς τὴν Πόλιν" (pronounced "is tim ˈbolin"), meaning "to the City" & is how it was referred to by the Greeks. Turks started using that word the last 50-70 years.

Constantinople comes from the Greek Konstantinoúpolis meaning City of Constantine. The name Constantine derives from the Latin word constantia, which means stability. The mother of Constantine, Helena, was a Greek and Christian from Bithynia who played an important role as Augusta and subsequently as the mother of Constantine in the shaping of the Roman Empire, with New Rome, known as Constantinople, as its capital.

Helena and her son Constantine were the first archeologists in the history. She was responsible for the construction of the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem, and the Church of Eleona on the Mount of Olives; sites of Christ's birth. She is most famous for the discovery of the True Cross. According to Eusebius, Constantine and Helena destroyed the temple of Venus and discovered the burial site of Jesus in the spot that Emperor Hadrian had built during the 130s over the site of Jesus' tomb near Calvary.

She went to Cyprus where she found pieces of the holy cross, and pieces of the rope with which Jesus was tied on the Cross.

Helena left Jerusalem and the eastern provinces in 327 to return to Rome, her place of residence. Later legends depict her as bringing with her large parts of the True Cross and other relics, which were then stored in her palace's private chapel, now the Basilica of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, where they can be still seen today.

Both Constantine and his mother Helena are commemorated annually as saints in Greece on the 21st of May, and it is a huge celebration.

The third name of Constantinople (the oldest chronologically) was known as Byzantium is Greek (ancient Greek: Βυζάντιον, Byzántion), was the name given to it at its foundation by Megarians and their King Byzas, around 657 BC. "Byzantium" is not a made up term like Turks want you to believe. It was the first and original name of the city. But of course this is something they don't know because they have the poorest education system in the world.

We read in the geographical/topographical encyclopedic-dictionary of Stephanus of Byzantium (6th century AD) :

"Byzantion" : Byzantion, the royal city in Thrace, a most renowned city, situated by the Propontis, on the European side. An oracle was given to the Megarians who inquired at Delphi, as follows: "Blessed are the men who will inhabit that city, by the narrow mouth of the Thracian shore, where fish and deer graze the same pasture; set out as quickly as possible, taking all this to heart." And so it was founded by Byzantas, son of Keroessa, daughter of Io and Poseidon, or because Byzas was the leader of the fleet. It is also said that the sea urchins there are highly sensitive to the winds. The city was later renamed Constantinople and New Rome. The ethnic term is Konstantinopolitis, without the "u." The ethnic term for Byzas is Byzantios with an "i," while the possessive form uses a diphthong. The ethnic term Byzantios is of three genders. The possessive form is Byzantiakos. It is also called Byzantias and Byzantis. There is also Byzanteia with a diphthong referring to the region. From Byzantios comes Byzantia and Byzantianos, and Byzanteianos with a diphthong, like Herakleianos. There is also another Byzantion in India.

It is very important to understand what I wrote in the beginning of my post. One more time.

The conversion of Hagia Sophia into a mosque and Muslims praying in a building that does not belong to their historical or civilizational heritage, is the clearest proof that Islam is a barbaric religion that does not create, but only conquers and destroys, and the clearest proof that Turkey has nothing to offer to the world except problems and terrorism.

I write about the ancient, medieval, and modern history of Greece and what Christians went through because of Islam. Always with primary sources and historical facts. Thanks for reading me and for all the support.

- Homer Pavlos

Lord krishna say  -

In the 4th chapter:

Bhagavan Krishna says that there are various Yajnas. Whoever performs Yajnas with the right Vidhi and guidance mentioned in the Vedas or scriptures attains the fulfilment of their desires.

In the Sri Mahabhagavata Purana, the worship of different deities for different purposes is well mentioned. Whether it is fame, name, health, wealth, youthfulness, sexual potency, or anything else, everything is explained, guided, and worked upon for 10,000 years. And because that is the only truth, that is why I am saying this to you.

So, there are only three ways prescribed by Hari-Hara: Daan, Tapa, and Adhyayan.

There is no need to search for the right woman. Just sit somewhere in a temple in front of a Shivling and chant Stotrams daily in front of Shiva. This will attract the energy of Shiva within you, and everything will become attainable. This is the most superior, best, safest, and easiest way...

To be honest, depending on your devotion and Tapas, the doors and pathways will open. But it is very clear in the Skanda Purana that only through Shiva's grace does a man attain a loyal, chaste, and pious wife.

Several Stotrams and methods are given to attain a good wife, and all these work towards building your wisdom and strengthening your faith.

Now, coming back to the point, just start chanting Shiva Stotrams along with Kaal Bhairav Stotrams, because that is the fastest way according to my knowledge. Except for this, there is no faster way to change the trajectory of your life and transform your karma in fast-forward mode.

text:
𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗔𝗕𝗟𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗨𝗕𝗧 𝗥𝗘𝗚𝗔𝗥𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗖𝗛𝗥𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗔𝗡𝗜𝗧𝗬

There are many reasons a person could 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗯𝗹𝘆 𝗿𝗲𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗲 without claiming to have proved Christianity false. The key distinction is:

𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘂𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗳𝗮𝗹𝘀𝗲—but it can be sufficient reason to withhold belief.

Some of the strongest grounds for reasonable doubt are:

𝗖𝗛𝗥𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗔𝗡𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗗𝗘𝗣𝗘𝗡𝗗𝗦 𝗢𝗡 𝗘𝗫𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗢𝗥𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗥𝗬 𝗦𝗨𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗔𝗟 𝗖𝗟𝗔𝗜𝗠𝗦.

Its central doctrines involve 𝗱𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝗺𝗶𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗹𝗲𝘀, 𝘃𝗶𝗿𝗴𝗶𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗽𝗿𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿, 𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗹𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗳𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗳𝗲. These aren't merely ordinary historical claims; they assert events or realities outside what can presently be independently demonstrated.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗥𝗥𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗖𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗕𝗘 𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗕𝗟𝗜𝗦𝗛𝗘𝗗 𝗜𝗡 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗔𝗠𝗘 𝗪𝗔𝗬 𝗔𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗢𝗥𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗥𝗬 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗡𝗧.

Historical methods can investigate that Jesus was crucified and that some early Christians believed he had risen. But establishing 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗽𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝗯𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗱 𝗮 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗱 is not equivalent to establishing 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗮 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗼𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗱.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗨𝗥𝗩𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗚𝗢𝗦𝗣𝗘𝗟 𝗔𝗖𝗖𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗧𝗦 𝗪𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗪𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗡 𝗗𝗘𝗖𝗔𝗗𝗘𝗦 𝗔𝗙𝗧𝗘𝗥 𝗝𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗦.

They are 𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗻𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲𝘀 rather than contemporary recordings or modern eyewitness documentation. Scholars can use them as historical sources, but reconstructing precisely what Jesus said and did involves substantial historical uncertainty.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗚𝗢𝗦𝗣𝗘𝗟𝗦 𝗗𝗜𝗙𝗙𝗘𝗥 𝗜𝗡 𝗦𝗜𝗚𝗡𝗜𝗙𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗡𝗧 𝗗𝗘𝗧𝗔𝗜𝗟𝗦.

The resurrection narratives, genealogies, chronology, sayings, and other episodes contain differences that require interpretation and harmonization. Christians propose various reconciliations, but their existence provides 𝗹𝗲𝗴𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 claims of straightforward historical or textual inerrancy.

𝗠𝗜𝗥𝗔𝗖𝗟𝗘 𝗖𝗟𝗔𝗜𝗠𝗦 𝗢𝗖𝗖𝗨𝗥 𝗜𝗡 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗬 𝗥𝗘𝗟𝗜𝗚𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦.

Christianity isn't unique in possessing testimony concerning miracles, visions, healings, apparitions, divine revelations, and supernatural experiences. Since 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 can generate sincere testimony of this kind, 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘆 𝗮𝗹𝗼𝗻𝗲 creates a difficult epistemological problem.

𝗔𝗟𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗘 𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗔𝗟 𝗘𝗫𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦 𝗘𝗫𝗜𝗦𝗧 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗔𝗧 𝗟𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗧 𝗦𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗥𝗘𝗟𝗜𝗚𝗜𝗢𝗨𝗦 𝗘𝗫𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗜𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗘𝗦.

Psychology and neuroscience document visions, hallucinations, altered states, expectation effects, memory reconstruction, social influence, confirmation bias, grief experiences, and other mechanisms capable of producing powerful experiences interpreted religiously. This doesn't prove every religious experience has a natural explanation, but it weakens the inference 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗶𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 → 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗲.

𝗗𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗡𝗘 𝗛𝗜𝗗𝗗𝗘𝗡𝗡𝗘𝗦𝗦 𝗖𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗔 𝗣𝗛𝗜𝗟𝗢𝗦𝗢𝗣𝗛𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗕𝗟𝗘𝗠.

If a perfectly loving personal God wants humans to know him and regards that relationship as enormously important, 𝘄𝗵𝘆 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗻𝗼𝗻𝗯𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗳 𝗲𝘅𝗶𝘀𝘁? Philosophers of religion disagree about how strong this objection is, but it is a serious argument rather than simply an absence of belief.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗕𝗟𝗘𝗠 𝗢𝗙 𝗦𝗨𝗙𝗙𝗘𝗥𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗥𝗘𝗠𝗔𝗜𝗡𝗦 𝗨𝗡𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗢𝗟𝗩𝗘𝗗.

Christianity traditionally maintains that an 𝗮𝗹𝗹-𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿𝗳𝘂𝗹, 𝗮𝗹𝗹-𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗴𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗚𝗼𝗱 created and governs reality. Yet reality contains enormous amounts of apparently gratuitous suffering—including disease, natural disasters, childhood suffering, predation and suffering that existed long before humans. Christian theodicies offer possible explanations, but their adequacy remains philosophically disputed.

𝗣𝗥𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗣𝗥𝗢𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗘 𝗔𝗡 𝗨𝗡𝗔𝗠𝗕𝗜𝗚𝗨𝗢𝗨𝗦 𝗗𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗡𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗢𝗙 𝗖𝗛𝗥𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗔𝗡𝗜𝗧𝗬.

Believers report answered prayers, but unanswered prayers are also common, and people belonging to mutually incompatible religions likewise report answered prayers. This makes personal prayer experiences difficult to use as 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 identifying Christianity specifically as true.

𝗖𝗛𝗥𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗔𝗡𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗗 𝗪𝗜𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗡 𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗟𝗜𝗘𝗥 𝗥𝗘𝗟𝗜𝗚𝗜𝗢𝗨𝗦 𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗗𝗜𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦.

Christianity emerged from Second Temple Judaism; Judaism developed from earlier Israelite religion; and ancient Israelite religion existed within the broader ancient Near Eastern cultural environment. Historical development does not itself prove Christianity false, but it provides a 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗵𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 for how its concepts developed rather than requiring supernatural revelation as the only explanation.

𝗥𝗘𝗟𝗜𝗚𝗜𝗢𝗨𝗦 𝗕𝗘𝗟𝗜𝗘𝗙 𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗡𝗚𝗟𝗬 𝗖𝗢𝗥𝗥𝗘𝗟𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗪𝗜𝗧𝗛 𝗛𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗖𝗨𝗟𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗔𝗟 𝗖𝗜𝗥𝗖𝗨𝗠𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗘𝗦.

People overwhelmingly encounter religions through families, societies and traditions. A person's birthplace and upbringing substantially affect which religious claims they initially encounter as credible. That doesn't establish that those beliefs are false, but it gives a reasonable basis for questioning whether 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗶𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘃𝗶𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗯𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸𝘀 𝗼𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗶𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘁𝗵.

𝗖𝗛𝗥𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗔𝗡𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗔𝗜𝗡𝗦 𝗦𝗨𝗕𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗡𝗧𝗜𝗔𝗟 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗡𝗔𝗟 𝗗𝗜𝗦𝗔𝗚𝗥𝗘𝗘𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧.

Christians disagree about salvation, baptism, Eucharist, biblical authority, hell, predestination, free will, homosexuality, abortion, creation, evolution, miracles, charismatic gifts, church authority and even how particular biblical passages should be interpreted. Disagreement doesn't establish falsity, but it complicates the claim that 𝗱𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗵𝗮𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝘂𝗻𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗮𝗯𝗹𝘆 𝗰𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗿 𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗼𝗳 𝗱𝗼𝗰𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗲.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗖𝗨𝗠𝗨𝗟𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗘 𝗔𝗥𝗚𝗨𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧

The cumulative argument is stronger when stated modestly. None of these points individually proves “𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝗳𝗮𝗹𝘀𝗲.” Christians have sophisticated responses to essentially all of them. But 𝗮 𝘀𝗸𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀𝗻'𝘁 𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝗖𝗵𝗿𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗳𝗮𝗹𝘀𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝗼𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗼 𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗵𝗼𝗹𝗱 𝗯𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗳.

The defensible conclusion is therefore:

text:
That's because yahweh is the devil and a rewrite of sumerian Enlil and not the real loving father Christ spoke of, known as source or "The One" which is mentioned in the Bible in the NT but warped by OT torah teachings, as God does not have a name, only fake gods get names, God simply exists. We can call him God or source or creator to describe God, but never a name, especially something gay like HaShem

Examples:

John 10:30: “I and the Father are one.”

John 14:9–11: “Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father… Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me.”

John 17:21–23 (the high-priestly prayer): Jesus prays that his followers “may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you… that they may be one even as we are one… that they may become perfectly one.”

John 8:58 — “Before Abraham was, I am.”

John 14:6 — “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”

John 11:25 — “I am the resurrection and the life.”

The two layers
Yahweh / Enlil side (the figure of the Torah and much of the Old Testament): the jealous commander, the one who issues the laws, demands blood, flood, and obedience, and sets the dualistic frame (fear the authorized god or be punished). 

“The One” / true Father (the language Jesus uses in John): the source of the oneness he claims (“I and the Father are one”) and the oneness he offers others (“that they may be one even as we are one”).

 This is treated as prior to, or above, the dualistic management system.

Where the New Testament supplies the contrast:

The strongest material for the differentiation sits in John’s Gospel and a few related places:
Jesus repeatedly speaks of the Father in terms of mutual indwelling and shared reality (John 10:30, 14:9–11, 17:21–23) rather than as a distant lawgiver who requires sacrifice.

In John 8 he tells certain religious authorities who claim the God of the Old Testament (YAHWEH): “You are of your father the devil… he was a murderer from the beginning” (John 8:44).

The “I AM” statements and the prayer in John 17 move the center from external obedience to an internal, participatory oneness.

The kingdom language (“the kingdom of God is within you,” the body as temple, forgiveness clearing the mind) is used to shift the focus away from the sacrificial and hierarchical system.

How the differentiation is usually phrased in this framework:

Yahweh/Enlil = the jealous operator of the dualistic contract (the one who says “I am the Lord your God… you shall have no other”).

The Father / The One that Jesus speaks of = the source behind or beyond that contract; the awareness or light in which the dualism itself appears.

Christ is read as the one who points past the operator YAHWEH/ENLIL to that source/ TRUE LIGHT, which is why the institutions later re-attached the New Testament back onto the Old Testament framework.

text:
🧭 TEMPLE OF POSEIDON | TRAVEL ESSENTIALS

📍 Getting There
Cape Sounion lies southeast of Athens, approximately 65–75 minutes away by car. A rental car, taxi, or organized excursion offers flexibility.

Important: The coastal KTEL bus service to Sounion has been suspended since October 4, 2026, until further notice. Confirm any resumption before relying on public transport.

🏛️ What to Explore
Walk around the surviving Doric columns, explore the sanctuary's remains, and enjoy sweeping Aegean views. For a longer outing, combine the temple with nearby Legrena beaches or Lavrio's archaeological museum.

⏱️ Time Needed
Allow 60–90 minutes at the site, or approximately 4–5 hours for a round trip from Athens. A full day works better for coastal stops and a relaxed meal.

🌅 When to Visit
The site opens daily from 9:30 AM until sunset, except on designated holidays. Last admission is 20 minutes before closing.

Late afternoon offers beautiful light, while mornings are a good alternative for exploring the ruins.

💰 Costs & Booking
Official admission, checked November 2026: €20 full price or €10 reduced. Online tickets are available through Hellenic Heritage.

For sunset visits, arrange return transportation in advance, particularly while public bus services remain suspended.

text:
Affordability isn't a psy-op, it's a real experience that most Americans wrestle with daily. 

Democrats leveraged that in the midterms because Republicans offered no pathway to ease this pain. In fact, we made it worse. 

Here are some steps that the GOP should be pushing both Nationally and locally. 

A large share of what we pay is a cost government stacks on top of the price, and what government stacks on, government can take off.

1. Tariffs are taxes, and Congress has to own them.

In February, the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that the emergency tariffs were illegal because the power to tax belongs to Congress. That should have been a win for the Constitution. Instead, the tariffs moved to a different statute, and in July a new tariff of 10-12.5% took effect on 60 countries covering more than 99% of what we import, with no expiration date.

I want to be tough on China, and targeted, security-based trade measures make sense. But a blanket tax on nearly everything we import is paid at the checkout line by American families. Article I gives the taxing power to Congress for a reason. Congress should take it back and vote on it in the open.

2. Housing: get government out of the way of building.

Washington passed the ROAD to Housing Act this summer. It's a start, but even its supporters say the near-term effect will be modest. The real barriers are closer to home:

Tariffs on lumber, steel, and copper go straight into the price of every house.

Local zoning makes it illegal to build a duplex, a small-lot starter home, or a backyard cottage for Grandma.
Permits sit for months, and impact fees pile thousands onto the price before a shovel hits dirt.

Subsidies bid prices up. We need to enable property owners to build.

3. Food: stop taxing the dinner table.

Beef is the big one. USDA projects beef prices up over 9% this year. Some of that is a tight cattle herd, but policy makes it worse:

The sugar program keeps American sugar prices above world prices.
The ethanol mandate burns corn that would otherwise feed cattle.

Stacked tariffs make imported beef more expensive.

Federal rules make it hard for a local rancher to sell to his neighbor through a small processor.

At the state level, let's keep phasing out the grocery tax and expand farm-to-family sales. No family should pay sales tax on bread and milk.

4. Energy: build more, and make the big users pay their own way.

Energy prices were up over 16% year over year in August, and gasoline was up over 27%. Electricity keeps climbing as the grid strains under new demand. 

The answer is supply:

Permitting reform, so power plants, pipelines, and transmission lines get built in years instead of decades.
New nuclear plants licensed on a reasonable timeline.

Data centers paying their own grid costs, or generating their own power, instead of shifting those costs onto your bill.

Here in Alabama, that means a Public Service Commission that asks hard questions about every dollar going into your rates.

5. Stop borrowing like there's no tomorrow.

Every dollar of federal deficit puts pressure on interest rates. That shows up in your mortgage, your car loan, and your credit card. Fiscal discipline is an affordability policy.

A word on local control:

Some of these reforms are uncomfortable for conservatives, especially on zoning. I don't want Montgomery or Washington dictating to our city councils. But there's a principled middle path:

protect the property owner's right to build modest housing on their own land, and let families, not planning boards, decide.

Conservatives have always known that affordability never comes from another federal program. It only ever  comes from removing the barriers we built ourselves, one level of government at a time.

The populist experiment has failed. It's time to revive, retake, and restore actual conservatism.

text:
DEVELOPING: 11 Democrats Miss Vote on Pete Hegseth Impeachment Effort

Eleven Democratic members of the United States House of Representatives did not participate in Tuesday’s crucial vote on an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, raising questions about their absence as Republicans succeeded in blocking the impeachment push.

The lawmakers are Representatives Julia Brownley, Lou Correa and Nancy Pelosi of California; Laura Gillen of New York; Steven Horsford of Nevada; Jonathan Jackson of Illinois; Brittany Pettersen of Colorado; Melanie Stansbury of New Mexico; Haley Stevens of Michigan; Marilyn Strickland of Washington; and Frederica Wilson of Florida.

The vote took place on November 10, 2026, following the introduction of eight articles of impeachment by Republican Congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky. The articles accused Hegseth of serious misconduct, including allegedly authorising military operations without congressional approval and other alleged violations of law.

Rather than voting directly on whether to impeach Hegseth, lawmakers voted on a procedural motion to refer the impeachment resolution to the House Judiciary Committee, effectively halting the immediate impeachment effort.

The motion passed 211–204, with 210 Republicans and one independent voting in favour, while 203 Democrats and Massie voted against it. Eleven Democrats and seven Republicans did not vote.

Some of the absent Democrats have subsequently offered explanations. Representatives Melanie Stansbury, Laura Gillen, Jonathan Jackson, Marilyn Strickland and Brittany Pettersen cited traffic delays that prevented them from reaching the House chamber before voting closed. Stansbury and Jackson subsequently registered their opposition to the procedural motion in the Congressional Record.

Pelosi was attending a Veterans Day event in San Francisco, while Correa’s office cited a medical procedure. Horsford’s office attributed his absence to a personal emergency and indicated that he supported the impeachment effort.

The absence of the 11 Democrats proved politically significant because their number exceeded the seven-vote margin by which the Republican-backed procedural motion passed.

The outcome has intensified scrutiny of Democratic lawmakers who missed the vote, particularly as the party prepares to assume control of Congress in January 2027.

AfrikTimes is monitoring developments.
