text:
Your name is Tyler. 38. You live in Bloomington, Minnesota, on a street where the houses don't talk to each other. You live between the two that talk the most. You've been practicing americanmaxxing since you were born. You don't know what it is yet.

On your left, Deb. Blue hair. She/her. Prius. Pride flag, a No Human Is Illegal lawn sign, a Harris sticker nobody peeled off. Deb votes blue, donates monthly, signs everything. Deb practices democratmaxxing. She doesn't know what it's called either.

On your right, Rick. Flagpole. F-350. A Let's Go Brandon sign he repaints every two years, because tradition matters. Rick watches the files nobody releases. Rick practices trumpmaxxing. Same deal. Nobody on this street knows what they practice.

You, you don't practice anything. Politics is two teams fighting over your money, and you noticed it at 22. You never mentioned it again. You do one thing: you move forward.

In 2019 you install cooling systems for server rooms. In 2022 you're the guy they call at 2 a.m. when a data center in Abilene, Texas, overheats. In 2024 you own the company that does it in eleven states. People offer to buy it. You don't sell. A clean conscience is nice. You keep a stronghold instead.

Then the AI boom happens. It happens to you. Every chip someone buys makes your phone ring. Billionaires pour concrete into the Texas heat and you take your cut. Your family doesn't understand your job. You stopped explaining in 2023.

Texas gets hot, Minnesota gets weird. You move to Texas. Deb posts about the climate. Rick posts about the border. You post the invoice.

Texas is good. Texas is a data center with a flag. You work, you lift, you learn Spanish from the crew. Your taxes go down. Your truck goes up. Nobody asks who you voted for. It never comes up. You think that's the whole point of the country.

Then Florida, 2026. A villa with a view of the water. The realtor is Dominican. The street is Venezuelans, Cubans, a Quebecoise snowbird named Chantal, and Karen, the American Chantal.

Chantal is from Gatineau. Karen is her American equivalent. Karen has never lost a fight with a manager. Karen knows the HOA president personally. You learn things from Karen that business school charges six figures for.

Half the street left New York in the last six years. They were Democrats when they packed. The property taxes converted them somewhere on I-95. They drive German cars, vote red, and complain about the price of everything except their own houses.

You're between two worlds again. On one side, Latinos who own landscaping companies and send money home. On the other, rich boomers who read Zillow like scripture. Politics comes up once, at Karen's pool. You say you don't really follow it. The table goes quiet. Someone hands you a beer. Nobody ever asks again.

The fief: the villa, the trucks, the company, the accounts, a generator, forty days of water, a lawyer on retainer. The good conscience is the villa. The stronghold is everything else.

You hear about the street from time to time. It's not the same street.

Deb got carjacked at a gas station in 2025. Two guys. Sudanese - the kind Minneapolis sent two thousand federal agents about. They took the Prius and her phone. She posted about the event. She posted about the systemic causes. She posted carefully. Not about the men.

Six months later they were back. Not the same two. The cousin of one of them, maybe. Nobody knows. What's known: Deb's back door doesn't close the way it used to, and a man named Ahmed sleeps in the living room now. It's not a lease. It's not a sale. Deb calls it a complicated housing situation. The city calls it nothing.

The neighborhood went down the way they do. One house, then a block party with a shooting, then a for-sale sign that never sold, then tents. There's no year it turned. It turned.

Deb fell into the tranq dope. Fentanyl cut with a horse sedative. Then a newer one, when the first got famous: medetomidine. It's for dogs after surgery. It's not for people. The people it doesn't kill, it freezes. They stand hunched on lawns, swaying, mid-gesture, for hours. The internet calls them zombies. Deb called it a failure of compassion until one of them was her.

Rick woke up. Rick read the files that exist. Trump backed Israel. The wall stayed a wall of the mind. The Epstein files stayed filed. The wars went on - for the complex, the lobbies, the things Rick now explains at length, in his bunker. The bunker is real: forty feet of shipping container under the garden, ventilation, water, ammo, freeze-dried beef, a flag, a Bible. He built it in 2025.

Rick's house stands empty above the bunker. The statues moved in. That's what you call them. Tranq doesn't make people lie down. It makes them stand frozen, leaning, swaying, holding a pose. There are four of them in Rick's living room. The house is lost. The bunker is his. The statues can have the surface. He's going to save America from below.

You go back once, for your mother's funeral. You park the truck between Deb's squat and Rick's statue garden. Two flags on one street: a Pride flag nobody took down, an American flag nobody took in. At the wake, people ask about Florida. You say the taxes are low. They look at you the way they look at the weather.

A cousin asks if you're coming back. Ahmed's friends are moving a couch into Deb's house. A statue stands in Rick's flowerbed, swaying, holding a phone. The kid next door asks the statue if he's okay. The statue says he's good. Nobody laughs. The street is very quiet and very loud.

You fly back the same night, first class, on points. In Florida it's 78 degrees. Chantal is playing pickleball. Karen is suing the HOA. The villa is lit, the generator is full, the company runs without you. The phone rings with another data center.

You practice americanmaxxing. It's not a team. It's the thing the street forgot: move forward, keep the fief, never argue with a statue. Deb practices democratmaxxing. Rick practices trumpmaxxing. The street practices both for them. You've practiced yours since you were born. Now you know what it's called.

text:
Part III — How the Torrens Title System Actually Works
00:20–00:35 · 15 minutes
6. The central legal distinction: title by registration
The most important doctrinal distinction in this entire seminar is between:
Registration of title: Recording an existing claim or instrument as evidence of ownership.
Title by registration: Giving registration a constitutive legal effect so that the registered interest receives the protection established by the governing statute.
The High Court of Australia expressed this distinction in Breskvar v Wall (1971) 126 CLR 376, 385–386.

Chief Justice Barwick explained:
It is the title which registration itself has vested in the proprietor.

This is a remarkably consequential legal proposition.

Under a Torrens statute, a registration may create a protected legal position that cannot be defeated merely by showing a defect in an earlier transaction. The exact protection depends on the legislation, the nature of the defect, the registered party's conduct, and applicable exceptions.

The system does not merely document the legal situation. Registration itself can alter that situation.

The Australian High Court reaffirmed the importance of this principle in Cassegrain v Gerard Cassegrain & Co Pty Ltd [2015] HCA 2, while stressing that Torrens statutes are not uniform and registered title is not absolutely indefeasible.
https://t.co/Njci5tZrUQ

7. The basic elements of the system
The legal architecture of Torrens registration
Land parcel

A legally identified parcel, generally supported by surveys, plans, or other descriptions

Registrar

The official responsible for maintaining the register and processing legally authorized dealings

Registered proprietor

The person or entity recorded as holding a specified estate or interest

Register or folio

The authoritative official record of ownership and relevant registered interests

Registrable dealings

Transfers, mortgages, leases, and other transactions recognized by the statute

Caveats and notices

Mechanisms for asserting or protecting certain claims against dealings

Judicial supervision

Court procedures for initial registration, disputes, correction, and other matters

Indemnity arrangements

Statutory compensation mechanisms where qualifying losses occur

These elements appear in various combinations across jurisdictions. The 1858 South Australian Act is particularly instructive because it does not merely announce a philosophy of ownership. It creates an operating administrative system.
What the founding Act actually established
The uploaded Real Property Act 1858 contains:
Provision
Subject
§ 3
Definitions of land, proprietor, transfer, certificate of title, mortgage, encumbrance, and registration abstract
§ 4
Duties of the Registrar-General
§§ 5–9

Evidence, forms, authentication, enforcement, and registrar powers

§§ 10–12

Lands Titles Commissioners and legal advisers
§§ 13–14
Land brought under the Act

§§ 15–17
Application review, public notice, and opportunities for objections
The Act's definition of a certificate of title is particularly important. Section 3 describes a certificate executed by the Registrar-General, with a duplicate constituting a page of the register book, and providing for the vesting of the relevant estate.

Thus, the statutory certificate was not simply an attractive piece of paper carrying someone's name. It was part of a legally prescribed registry process.

Source: South Australia, Real Property Act 1858, §§ 3–17, uploaded PDF pp. 1–8.

8. How a parcel first enters the Torrens system

This is called initial registration or bringing land under the Act.

The procedure varies among jurisdictions, but the historical South Australian Act provides an excellent teaching example.

Historical illustration based on the South Australian Real Property Act 1858, principally §§ 14–17. This is not a substitute for any jurisdiction's current filing procedure.Historical initial-registration workflow
1. ApplicationApplicant requests registration of identified land2. Documentary examinationExisting grants, transfers, mortgages, and other title evidence are reviewed3. Identification of interestsThe registrar or commissioners identify possible adverse and beneficial claims4. Public noticeNotices are issued as the statute requires5. Opportunity for objectionInterested persons may lodge caveats or contest the application6. DeterminationThe authorized officials decide whether registration may proceed7. Entry on the registerThe applicant is registered with the estate and interests determined under the Act

Section 14 of the 1858 Act required qualifying applicants seeking to bring previously granted land into the system to provide the registrar with documents affecting title, an abstract, and information about other persons possessing legal or equitable interests.

This is a significant safeguard: initial registration was not intended to operate merely upon an applicant's unsupported declaration of ownership.

Section 16 empowered the Lands Titles Commissioners to investigate more complicated situations, including prior transfers, transmissions, unsatisfied mortgages, and beneficial interests.

The Act also required public notice and supplied objection mechanisms.

The American judicial variation

Minnesota offers a different institutional model.

Under Minnesota Statutes Chapter 508, application and examination are tied to district-court proceedings. The relevant sections include:

§ 508.03 — Application.
§ 508.10 — District-court powers.

§ 508.12 — Examiners of titles.

§§ 508.15–508.17 — Summons, service, and answers.

§§ 508.22–508.23 — Registration decree and its contents.
The resulting decree supplies the legal foundation for the registered title.
A crucial distinction is that the original investigation of title can be extensive even when subsequent transfers become simpler.

This is one reason discussions about Torrens efficiency must distinguish initial registration costs from ongoing conveyancing costs.
https://t.co/uJefSMScq3
9. How ownership transfers after initial registration
Consider a hypothetical example.
Alice is the registered proprietor of Parcel 101. She agrees to sell to Benjamin.
The transaction can be described in the following sequence:
Alice and Benjamin enter into a valid purchase agreement.

The parties examine the current register and undertake other required legal investigations.

Appropriate transfer documents are prepared and executed.
Existing mortgages and other matters are addressed as required.

The transfer is submitted for registration.
The registrar examines the submission for compliance.

Upon effective registration, Benjamin becomes the registered proprietor of the estate transferred, subject to applicable statutory provisions and exceptions.

The transfer instrument remains important. But a contract or signed transfer alone is not necessarily equivalent to becoming the registered proprietor.
This distinction also raises the question of what rights may exist between contract execution and registration.
For example, Benjamin may acquire an equitable interest under a specifically enforceable purchase contract before registration. The precise consequences depend on jurisdiction and facts.
A modern development: electronic titles
Historically, many Torrens jurisdictions issued a paper certificate corresponding to the official register.
In New South Wales, this changed substantially on October 11, 2021.
Physical certificates of title were canceled and electronic lodgment replaced the paper-based process. The official register—not possession of an old paper certificate—remains authoritative.
Registrar General+1
This illustrates an important lesson:

The legal heart of the Torrens system is the authoritative register, not the physical medium used to display its contents.

10. How a mortgage operates
A mortgage is a security interest associated with an obligation, commonly repayment of a loan.
Suppose Benjamin purchases registered land using a loan from Bank C.

Benjamin's ownership and the bank's security interest are separate legal positions.

Invented example. A real register may differ considerably in layout, terminology, numbering, and legal effect.Illustrative Torrens register entryFolio 101/2026Illustrative onlyLand descriptionLot 101, Registered Plan 2026Registered proprietorBenjamin — Fee simpleRegistered interestsMortgage M-1001 — Bank COther recorded mattersEasement E-120 — Access right benefiting adjoining land
Benjamin remains the registered proprietor of his estate, subject to the registered mortgage and other legally effective interests.

The bank does not automatically become the owner merely because it holds the mortgage. A mortgage creates the security rights established by the instrument and the governing law.

Minnesota §§ 508.54–508.58 address mortgage registration and foreclosure-related matters.
The original South Australian Act expressly defined mortgage, mortgagor, and mortgagee in § 3, illustrating that secured lending was a central concern from the beginning.
11. Caveats: protecting interests before they are defeated

A caveat is a statutory notice mechanism by which someone claiming a qualifying interest may seek to prevent registration of dealings inconsistent with that interest.

Examples of claims that might justify a caveat under an applicable statute include:
An equitable purchaser under an enforceable contract.
A beneficiary or claimant asserting a qualifying proprietary interest.
Another person with a legally recognized interest at risk from a proposed dealing.

A caveat does not, by itself, establish the claimant's ownership. It is a protective procedural mechanism and may be challenged.

The New South Wales 2013 registry guide, page 8, explains caveats as notices intended to restrict registration of inconsistent dealings.

Classroom question 3

Alice signs an agreement to sell land to Benjamin. Before Benjamin registers his transfer, Alice enters a second agreement with Catherine.

Benjamin claims that the first contract gives him an equitable interest.

What could Benjamin do to preserve his position?

Expected discussion: Investigate whether a caveat or other protective filing is available, preserve the evidence of his agreement, and seek appropriate judicial relief if necessary. Filing a caveat without sufficient legal grounds can expose a claimant to consequences.

Cole Hocker won three NCAA titles in one year, and he wasn't Oregon's only champion that year. The Ducks won six individual distance titles in 2021 alone: five by men, one by a woman.

Hocker grew up in Indianapolis and ran a 4:36 mile as an eighth grader. At Cathedral High School he won the 2018 Indiana state cross country title, placed 2nd at Nike Cross Nationals and won the Foot Locker national title. He picked Oregon over offers that included Northern Arizona and Indiana.

In February 2021 he ran 3:50.55 for the mile, 2nd to teammate Cooper Teare as both broke the collegiate record. In March he won the NCAA indoor mile (3:53.71) and 3000 (7:46.15). In June he won the outdoor 1500 in 3:35.35, outkicking NCAA record holder Yared Nuguse, and was 4th in the 5000.

That's 3 individual titles and 4 All-American honors, all in 2021.

Three years later he was the Olympic 1500 champion in Paris, in an Olympic record of 3:27.65. In 2025 he added a world title in the 5000.

text:
America's First Legal Psilocybin Program Treated 346 People. Here's What Happened. | Michelle Starr, ScienceAlert

For those living in the shadow of mental health conditions such as PTSD, anxiety, and depression, finding a way forward can sometimes feel impossible – especially when conventional treatments have offered little succor.

Psilocybin, a psychoactive chemical found in some mushrooms, spent decades being demonized as an illicit drug.

But now, results from the first state-regulated psilocybin program in the US suggest the drug could offer a glimmer of hope beyond the confines of clinical trials.

Between November 2024 and June 2026, a team led by Oregon Health & Science University tracked 346 clients participating in the program – and found that, in the first three months after taking psilocybin, participants reported significant improvements in mental health, well-being, and life satisfaction.

Just one month after the dose, 92.2 percent of participants said the experience had been beneficial, while, on average, their mental health symptoms had fallen dramatically.

"This paper is going to be cited for decades," says neuroscientist Adrianne R. Wilson-Poe of the Legacy Research Institute and co-director of the Open Psychedelic Evaluation Nexus (OPEN).

"This is the first large-scale study to monitor the safety and mental health symptoms of real people in the real world."

Mental illness affects tens of millions of Americans, many of whom find conventional treatment insufficient – or don't find it at all. In 2024, approximately 23 percent of US adults reported symptoms of mental illness in the prior year; however, only half of those people received treatment.

This has led researchers to investigate other options, such as psilocybin. Over the last decade, clinical trials have shown increasing promise that the compound can alleviate the symptoms of mental illness, particularly in patients for whom other treatments have not worked well.

A clinical trial, however, is a very tightly controlled setting.

The Oregon study is a totally different beast.

The program officially opened its doors to clients in mid-2023. Rather than using carefully selected participants, synthetic pharmaceutical psilocybin, and ongoing therapeutic support, it allows any adult over 21 to participate for any reason, uses mushroom-derived products, and doesn't require facilitators to have professional clinical training.

So what happens, the researchers wanted to know, when you take psilocybin out of the tightly controlled clinical-trial environment and offer it to ordinary members of the public?

OPEN recruited 346 clients of the program, across 24 licensed service centers in Oregon, who were willing to participate in assessing its outcomes and safety.

Each client received a supervised dose of psilocybin averaging 31.9 milligrams, although individual doses ranged from 2 to 50 milligrams. Clients underwent preparation beforehand, took the psilocybin under facilitator supervision, and could attend integration sessions afterward.

They also completed surveys to assess changes in symptoms and life satisfaction before the dose and at several points after, up to 3 months later.

The results were impressive.

After three months, the proportion of participants reporting moderate-to-severe PTSD symptoms had fallen from 48 percent to 16.8 percent. Moderate-to-severe anxiety fell from 45.1 percent to 13.2 percent over the same timeframe, while moderate-to-severe depression fell from 42.2 percent to 16.5 percent.

Meanwhile, life satisfaction rose from 63 percent to 82.3 percent across the cohort.

But it wasn't all great news. Four people – 1.2 percent of the cohort – experienced serious behavioral reactions requiring medical attention.

One person became violent and was transported to the hospital. Another subsequently reported an emergency room visit, worsening anxiety and depression, and thoughts of self-harm.

A third reported an emergency room visit and worsening anxiety and depression.

And the fourth reported severe anxiety and insomnia requiring medication, plus worsening anxiety and depression and thoughts of self-harm through three months.

All four were psychedelic-naive (hadn't taken a psychedelic before) and had symptoms of depression, anxiety, and/or PTSD before taking psilocybin. They also received moderate-to-high doses of 25 to 50 milligrams.

The researchers suggest that inexperience with psychedelics, greater psychological vulnerability, and higher doses may increase the risk of serious reactions, although four cases are far too few to establish that.

There are also several limitations. Because it's a real-world study, it can't prove that psilocybin caused the improvements.

There was no control group; participants chose to use the service; and only around 5 percent of Oregon's psilocybin clients during the study period participated in OPEN. In addition, most of the participants were white and relatively affluent.

However, Oregon's experiment is already considerably larger than this study alone might suggest.

More than 20,000 people have received regulated psilocybin services in the state since 2023 – more than six times the number who have participated in clinical trials of classic psychedelics since 1951.

For study lead Todd Korthuis of Oregon Health & Science University and his colleagues, the findings suggest that the benefits seen in tightly controlled clinical trials may carry over into the messier real world – although the small number of serious reactions shows that psilocybin is not without risk.

Psilocybin isn't suitable for everyone, and anyone considering it should discuss the potential risks with a medical professional, particularly if they have existing health conditions or take medications that could interact with it.

But the findings offer encouraging early evidence that bringing psilocybin outside the traditional medical model doesn't necessarily mean leaving its potential benefits behind.

"Just because something isn't a medical model doesn't mean you can't have mental health benefits," Korthuis says.

text:
The Yankees didn't have to fire anyone to reshape Aaron Boone's coaching staff. Other teams are doing it for them, which says a lot about how the rest of baseball rates the people in that dugout.
Brad Ausmus is leaving to manage the Astros, per https://t.co/PBnjiv1H9y and ESPN. 

He has been Boone's bench coach since 2024, and he played 10 of his 18 big league seasons in Houston. This is his third time running a club, after the Tigers (2014-17), where he won the AL Central as a rookie manager, and the Angels (2019). 

Tanner Swanson is going home to Seattle as the Mariners' bench coach. He ran the Yankees' catchers for seven seasons, and in that time they led the majors in catcher framing runs. His contract was up, and the Washington native picked the Mariners over a new offer from New York.

Now James Rowson is expected to join the Giants, and Jon Heyman reports his title will be offensive coordinator. 

Rowson's contract also expired, and the Yankees had been reviewing their hitting department. Their offense ranked first in baseball in wRC+ in 2024 and 2025, then fell to 14th this year while Aaron Judge missed more than three months with a broken rib.

The Yankees haven't named a new bench coach or hitting coach yet. Brian Cashman said Tuesday they're looking at hitting coach candidates both inside and outside the organization. 

On the catching side, they've already promoted run prevention and catching coordinator Aaron Gershenfeld to the major league staff to fill Swanson's role. Pitching coach Matt Blake is back after his staff posted an MLB-best 3.23 ERA, and the Post's Joel Sherman called Joe Espada, the manager Ausmus is replacing in Houston, a logical bench coach candidate.

The Yankees went 93-68 and lost to the Rays in the ALDS, and Boone returns for the final year of his contract. With a possible lockout starting Dec. 1 that would cut coaches off from players, the next two hires need to happen fast, and they'll shape how 2027 goes.

text:
"A week before the United States invaded Venezuela in January and captured its authoritarian leader, US Vice President J.D. Vance flew in Air Force Two for a visit to Montana's Yellowstone Club, an ultra-exclusive ski and golf resort.
There, he met an old friend and early financier of his political career, John Addison, a gasoline trader with commodities giant Vitol, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Flight records reviewed by Reuters show Addison's private Embraer jet and Vance's vice-presidential plane together on the tarmac at the Bozeman Yellowstone International Airport, about an hour's drive from the resort, on Dec. 27, a week before the invasion.
Vance and Addison talked about Venezuela, according to the person, who was given an account of the meeting from Addison. Vance was particularly interested to know how ​quickly Venezuelan crude could be sold if the US hypothetically gained control of the country's oil supplies, the person said. Addison assured Vance that Vitol was uniquely placed to do that job.

For this article, both Addison and Vance's office denied having the Dec. 27 meeting in Montana. 
But Addison confirmed to Reuters that on Jan. 5 – two days after the operation that unseated Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and killed up to 100 people – US Energy Secretary Chris Wright called him at his desk in Houston with an irresistible offer.

President Donald Trump's administration was planning to start selling the South American OPEC nation's crude to global buyers to finance its coming political transition, and Wright wanted to know from Addison if Vitol wanted the job.

The Department of Energy confirmed Wright called Addison Jan. 5 to discuss Venezuela.

Within days, Vitol and its rival Trafigura landed special licenses to sell Venezuela's oil, and the companies have since earned hundreds of millions of dollars marketing the crude.
The details of how Vitol secured one of the administration's most coveted energy licenses have not previously been reported.
Addison, ​48, wasn't the obvious choice to receive such a call from Wright. He was a senior trader at Vitol, not the firm's regional CEO. And his specialty was buying and selling US gasoline, not Latin American crude oil.
But Vance had told Wright that Addison was trustworthy, paving the way for the call, Addison told Reuters.
A US official confirmed to Reuters on condition of anonymity that Vance ​had told Wright in a conversation that Addison was a trustworthy person in the energy industry. The official said that conversation happened at least a year before the Jan. 5 phone call.
The Department of Energy told Reuters in a statement that Vance and Wright never discussed the sales of Venezuelan oil, and ⁠that the department picked Vitol because it is the largest energy and commodity trader in the world.
The Montana meeting and the unusually prominent role played by Addison in securing the lucrative contract raise fresh questions among Democratic lawmakers about how personal connections might have influenced access to government business after the Venezuela operation.
Robert Garcia, the ranking Democrat on the House Oversight Committee and its incoming chair, sent a letter to the heads of both ​Vitol and Trafigura in January asking questions about the circumstances under which they secured the licenses.

Typically, large US government contracts are awarded in a competitive bidding process to ensure transparency, prevent favoritism, and secure the best possible financial returns to taxpayers.
But the Trump administration has defended its decision to skip that process, arguing that moving fast after Maduro was seized was critical to stabilizing Venezuela's struggling economy and ensuring that everyday services and debt restructuring efforts received immediate funding.

AT THE WHITE HOUSE."

text:
Lil Wayne and Turk once seriously considered leaving Birdman’s Cash Money Records to join Master P’s No Limit empire, and Master P believes things worked out exactly how they were supposed to.

During an October 2026 appearance on the We In Miami Podcast, Master P was asked about Turk’s previous revelation that he and Wayne had discussed switching labels during their early Hot Boys days.

Turk had explained that watching No Limit artists receive houses, Rolex watches and expensive cars made him and Wayne question their own situation at Cash Money. At the time, they felt other artists were receiving better treatment, and the two even talked about approaching Master P.

But the conversation never turned into an actual offer. Before they made a move, their situation at Cash Money improved, and they ultimately stayed with Birdman.

Looking back, Master P said he was happy things happened that way, explaining that Wayne and Turk might not have become the artists they are today if they had joined his label.

Rather than treating it as a missed opportunity, he believes everyone has their own journey.

text:
The Miami Heat had Hassan Whiteside up for $100 million. Dwyane Wade says he had signed for $13 or $14 million, and he asked the team to take care of him first.

In the video below, Dwyane Wade says, "Y'all about to give him money over me?"

After LeBron James left Miami, Wade says the call he got was, "That's all the money we got left." He says he signed a two-year deal for $13 or $14 million. Reports put that deal at two years and $31.125 million. "Mind you, at this point, I should be in my 20s million a year."

Chris Bosh had already gotten a max contract. Wade says, "Chris got his max, but Chris ain't selling no tickets. They come to see the kid. So pay me my due."

He wanted a three-year deal to finish. He says they would not do it. They chased Kevin Durant and, Wade says, had Whiteside up for $100 million. Whiteside later signed a four-year, $98 million contract.

Wade's phone stopped ringing. The Heat later offered a two-year deal for what he says was the money he had asked for the year before. By then, he says, it had become business. He left for Chicago after 13 seasons and three titles in Miami.

So did the Heat have to pay Whiteside first, or did they owe Wade before anyone else?

text:
🚨Casemiro on why he rejected offers from European clubs to join Inter Miami:

🗣️ Casemiro:  “After announcing I was leaving Manchester United, I received offers from several European clubs.

Good clubs.

Clubs where I could have continued playing Champions League football and competing for trophies.

So people asked me, ‘Why would you leave Europe for MLS?’

The answer was actually very simple.

I had already lived the dream.

I played with Cristiano Ronaldo.

I played with Luka Modrić.

I played with Toni Kroos.

I played with Sergio Ramos.

I played with Karim Benzema.

I shared dressing rooms with some of the greatest footballers of my generation.

I won the Champions League.

I won league titles.

I played in the biggest stadiums and experienced almost everything a footballer dreams about.

But there was one thing missing.

Lionel Messi.

I had played against him many times.

I had spent years trying to stop him.

I had watched him do things against my teams that made you question whether the normal rules of football applied to him.

But I had never sat beside him in a dressing room.

Never trained with him.

Never walked onto a pitch knowing he was wearing the same shirt as me.

Then the Inter Miami opportunity came.

And honestly, I started thinking differently.

At my age, football isn’t only about asking, ‘Where can I win another trophy?’

You start asking, ‘What experiences will I remember when I stop playing?’

And I knew one thing immediately.

I wanted to know what it was like to play with Messi.

People thought I was choosing MLS over Europe.

That wasn’t how I saw it.

I was choosing an experience I could never repeat.

I could have stayed in Europe for another year or two.

Maybe I could have won another trophy.

Maybe I could have played another Champions League campaign.

But I had already done those things.

I had never shared a dressing room with Messi.

That was something I couldn’t buy with money and couldn’t create by waiting.

So when the opportunity came, I didn’t need much convincing.

I wanted to see how he prepares.

How he sees the game.

What he says in the dressing room.

Where he wants the ball.

How he thinks about football when nobody is watching.

Those things are priceless to me.

I’ve played with Ronaldo, Modrić, Kroos, Ramos and Benzema.

Now I had the chance to add Messi to that list.

And I think that is something people sometimes forget about footballers.

We spend our whole careers chasing numbers, trophies, contracts and records.

But when you are near the end, you remember the moments that made you feel something.

I wanted another story.

I wanted another challenge.

I wanted to sit in that dressing room and understand what it feels like when the player you spent years preparing to stop is suddenly the player you are trying to help win games.

That was the attraction.

Not the money.

Not the league.

Not the idea of escaping Europe.

It was Messi.

So yes, I rejected European clubs.

Not because I was afraid of competition.

I simply felt there was one experience my career was still missing.

And when the opportunity came, I didn’t want to look back and wonder what it would have been like.

I wanted to be able to say one thing.

‘I didn’t just play against Lionel Messi.

I played with him.’

For me, that was worth more than another trophy.”

text:
🚨Casemiro on why he rejected offers from European clubs to join Inter Miami:

🗣️ Casemiro:  “After announcing I was leaving Manchester United, I received offers from several European clubs.

Good clubs.

Clubs where I could have continued playing Champions League football and competing for trophies.

So people asked me, ‘Why would you leave Europe for MLS?’

The answer was actually very simple.

I had already lived the dream.

I played with Cristiano Ronaldo.

I played with Luka Modrić.

I played with Toni Kroos.

I played with Sergio Ramos.

I played with Karim Benzema.

I shared dressing rooms with some of the greatest footballers of my generation.

I won the Champions League.

I won league titles.

I played in the biggest stadiums and experienced almost everything a footballer dreams about.

But there was one thing missing.

Lionel Messi.

I had played against him many times.

I had spent years trying to stop him.

I had watched him do things against my teams that made you question whether the normal rules of football applied to him.

But I had never sat beside him in a dressing room.

Never trained with him.

Never walked onto a pitch knowing he was wearing the same shirt as me.

Then the Inter Miami opportunity came.

And honestly, I started thinking differently.

At my age, football isn’t only about asking, ‘Where can I win another trophy?’

You start asking, ‘What experiences will I remember when I stop playing?’

And I knew one thing immediately.

I wanted to know what it was like to play with Messi.

People thought I was choosing MLS over Europe.

That wasn’t how I saw it.

I was choosing an experience I could never repeat.

I could have stayed in Europe for another year or two.

Maybe I could have won another trophy.

Maybe I could have played another Champions League campaign.

But I had already done those things.

I had never shared a dressing room with Messi.

That was something I couldn’t buy with money and couldn’t create by waiting.

So when the opportunity came, I didn’t need much convincing.

I wanted to see how he prepares.

How he sees the game.

What he says in the dressing room.

Where he wants the ball.

How he thinks about football when nobody is watching.

Those things are priceless to me.

I’ve played with Ronaldo, Modrić, Kroos, Ramos and Benzema.

Now I had the chance to add Messi to that list.

And I think that is something people sometimes forget about footballers.

We spend our whole careers chasing numbers, trophies, contracts and records.

But when you are near the end, you remember the moments that made you feel something.

I wanted another story.

I wanted another challenge.

I wanted to sit in that dressing room and understand what it feels like when the player you spent years preparing to stop is suddenly the player you are trying to help win games.

That was the attraction.

Not the money.

Not the league.

Not the idea of escaping Europe.

It was Messi.

So yes, I rejected European clubs.

Not because I was afraid of competition.

I simply felt there was one experience my career was still missing.

And when the opportunity came, I didn’t want to look back and wonder what it would have been like.

I wanted to be able to say one thing.

‘I didn’t just play against Lionel Messi.

I played with him.’

For me, that was worth more than another trophy.”

text:
I never understood Western-style dating as a Westerner. The people who have new partners every few months. They swipe on apps like they’re picking out a flavor of breakfast cereal at the supermarket. She advertised her pictures to your entire neighborhood, and you want that in your future household? They date multiple people at the same time as though they’re fielding candidates for a job interview. You hear about the breakup texts sent before 9:00 AM. The modern people who keep their exes in their orbit: “He’s just my friend.”

Work in any kitchen in America, and the servers, cooks, and bartenders are all sleeping together. Where the human spirit is broken, spiritually thin dating thrives.

My hostel dorm mate in Las Vegas introduced himself to a girl from Slovakia. He led with living in New York and working in finance. When he asked her things about Slovakia, he pretended to text his “Slovakian friend” about all the cultural factoids she was telling him.

“What do you think of that Slovakian girl? She was cute, right?” He asked me, “I don’t f*ck anyone over the age of 28; it just doesn’t hit the same.” He was charming, but very distant, almost sociopathically so. Like he was looking at you in a calculating way. Before I had a chance to get out of there, he wanted to show me a picture of the “French babe” he was with last night.

I think true love is meeting your partner’s inner child. Yet your inner child does not poison themselves in bars and clubs. Older people say you meet the one in cafes and bookstores, or when you’re not looking for love. But to a young man in the West, more innocent dating is boring. When young men grow older, they change the rules on women.

I remember I was writing in a library in Los Angeles, and middle schoolers at a table behind me were talking loudly.

“I look baddie in this picture, right?”

“Yeah, you look baddie,” the group leader said.

The group leader, whom they referred to as “Mom,” answered the phone. It was one of her friends crying.

“Oh no, you didn’t sleep with him, did you?”

Their other stories were less tragic, centering around their high-flying parents still chasing their careers. Fancy dinners in New York and such.

The middle school “Mom’s” values were pretty on point. They weren’t an unwavering value system like Christianity, but more street values. Street values consist of behaviors and their probable cause-and-effect consequences.

On all those afternoons writing, I decided I was never raising a child in Los Angeles. There is a certain indescribable magic to that city, but you’re only part of the club if you’re not close with your parents.

Hollywood movies are funny to me, where the bad guy has the girl, and the good guy has to defeat him to steal her back. Like, dude, her hardwiring is all wrong for choosing him in the first place. Brad Pitt in Ocean’s Eleven: Do you want Tess (Julia Roberts) back after Terry Benedict, the ruthless Casino Owner, railed your wife while you were in prison? $150 million in a bank vault to win back a girl who’s given up on you and chosen another man? These Hollywood hippie white Satanists.

I do love that movie, though. I watched it on a plane this year. It’s all smooth vibes. It’s a beautiful heist film. Critics say the premise is flawed. I think the physics of a nuclear pinch shutting down the power in Las Vegas is more realistic than a self-respecting man choosing a woman who abandoned him.

But hey, she still “loved” him all this time. She even kept the ring. That’s considered loyalty by the logic of Western dating. You forget about their true dynamic when you wrap it in status and Hollywood aesthetic. If Danny Ocean were a line cook with a hand tattoo trying to get back a server who cheated on him with the head bartender, that would be pathetic.

That’s the hardest question I have to ask myself. Is my desire for monogamy my inner child wanting to be loved in a pure way? Or my position in the social hierarchy, not caring for these hippie white girls with a convoluted history of exes offering themselves to me? When you have more access, you don’t care about value systems you’re not part of.

So what if a white girl in a bohemian skirt and dream catcher earrings presents herself as “trauma-healed” and wants to take my astrology reading? My alarm bells are screaming: She’s let so many men into her life. I can be polite to her, as I have been. No one is making me date anyone with differing values.

It’s not a reflection of me that Western women looking for their last branch on the tree offer themselves to me.

I guess it’s nice the Asian Dads discourage their daughters from dating until university age. So I don’t have dark images of who I’m sitting across from. I think back to some of the university women I had crushes on back in Boston. The soul of a little girl building a sandcastle on the beach who needs to be protected. Then my mind does a horror-movie flashback to a tattooed line cook making her moan. His mess of alcoholism and weed-stained hair pounding her repeatedly. How could I possibly find her cute, then?

No one wants their adorable child to grow up to be the line cook’s good Friday night. I’m talking about you dirty hippie line cooks in the West. The foreign cooks are clean-cut. They’re just making their money to build a better life for themselves.

I would never let someone into my future household who’s had a one-night stand, even once. It breaks my heart when women don’t know how amazing they are. I don’t let men into my world who participate in short-term things either. I can think of no greater barometer for lack of intentionality.

I’m a child on the inside. I imagine us building a snowman together, falling in the snow and giggling, holding hands in a movie theater and holding each other during the scary parts. Then kissing on the sidewalk in an unexpected rainstorm. Not just any rainstorm. But one of those Asian monsoon rainstorms with the taste of tropical vegetation mixed with air pollution. I’m a connoisseur of air pollution. The formula for air impurities has to be just right.

How am I supposed to meet your inner child if you gave away pieces of your soul to men who didn’t care to be your life partner? How can I choose you with everything that I am when you didn’t even choose yourself?

I think that’s the biggest insecurity of being a man: You meet someone amazing. She has an outlier mind. Her intuition sees things imperceptible to you. She’s pretty in a non-stereotypical way. You confess your feelings for each other. Then one Saturday night, she sleeps with the lanky line cook with a hand tattoo, all because he asked her. You have to sever the part of yourself that wrote her into your future. You have to sever the part of yourself that could ever be drawn to that.

I think the spiritually thin and the spiritually deep walk with each other, irrespective of cultural ideals.

Despite the wounds of Western-style dating, certain nuances slip through the cracks of my condemnation for its spiritually thin behaviors. I don’t condemn the rappers, the James Bonds, and female singers of the world. Why do the rappers get to be openly non-monogamous, but if a lanky line cook sleeps with half the servers, his behavior is suddenly devious? Is there a social status element to Western-style dating? Status and attractiveness influence our perception.

We also tend to condemn differing values less than we do inconsistent ones.

My dinner dates are usually awkward. In 2017, I’m sitting across from a girl who’s telling me a story about making out with a guy drunk on a train in Germany. At his own bachelor party.

“I figured he was going to be married for a long time, so I wanted to give him one last good night.”

That would have been nice to know before I flew across the world for this. It’s funny that behavior self-justifies itself within its own worldview. I guess any girl willing to meet you in Russia is as crazy as you are. I remember my inner panic when she sent me a screenshot of her Russian visa when I was living in Sydney. Oh, we’re really doing this now.

Maybe part of me expects women to run, and it affects my more tangible life choices. I think I have an abstracted view of love. People are real. People are messy with all their lightness and darkness.

The red-headed Dutch girl at dinner in China was nice, at first. No Western-style dating history either. She explained how the Dutch would save the world from rising sea levels. Something is endearing about a woman who has pride in her country. She insisted on splitting the bill, so I played with her and asked to order the most expensive thing on the menu, since we were “splitting it.” Her reaction, frantically searching the menu for a compromise dish, was funny.

I wasn’t meeting her, though. And she wasn’t meeting me. I was meeting a travel girl on a gap year, the white T-shirt and giant backpack. She was meeting the high-stakes stock trader pretending to design a product while gambling his recently deceased Dad’s life insurance money.

The travel girl morphs into the career-climbing girl back home. She would do the math that I wasn’t Dutch baby material. She later told me she was dating and was on the apps. She invited me to come visit her at the Christmas markets in the Netherlands a few years later. I figured she had been looking for others this entire time, and I chose not to go.

It takes a certain level of spiritual fortitude to not see new people through the lens of what didn’t work out. But exactly as they are today, with all their lightness and darkness.

I’m not an easy person. Forging your own life path is not pretty. There are easy lives for me. I could work at an architecture office in a small Midwestern town, and make the kind of money that gets me a house and a middle-class life. But there’s no pain like growing old, and knowing that you never really went for it when it mattered. I don’t write well when I’m not living a life that is true to myself.

I carry all this unresolved energy when I’m on dates. They sense the discrepancy between the life I have and the inner self I haven’t offered yet, and it makes their stomach churn. It makes my stomach churn to take in an entire person as I meet more of their darkness. Maybe I have to be more integrated myself to integrate with another.

I’m on a pizza date in Hanoi. The server gives me the zero-sugar Coke and her the watermelon juice. She doesn’t know the girly drink is mine. We both wait for her to leave before swapping drinks.

She eats way slower than I do. I’m embarrassed to keep grabbing more pizza slices. What if she says she’s satisfied, but she’s still hungry? And she ends up stopping somewhere else to eat on her way home? I drink my watermelon juice too quickly. I ordered it because I associate watermelon with a childhood photo of her. She lets me drink her zero-sugar Coke. The server comes out with a tiny glass of water for me, which I drink in a few gulps. Then more of her Coke. The shrimp pizza is spicy. Luckily, Coke has magically more volume in a can than when it’s poured out into her glass.

She wants me to look at her. I do, then her eyes have that “not sure” look, and I get uncomfortable, and we both look away and giggle. Comfort and certainty are a cascading effect from both sides.

She keeps asking if I’m hungry, even though I ate 2/3 of the pizza. I could eat more pizza, sure, but I want to make sure her stomach is happy. We order more pizza to be safe. I don’t think either of us knows how to be direct yet.

The server interrupts us just as I start talking about kissing. The subject is not brought up again.

I’m less interested in condemning what I witnessed at university house parties in Boston and reopening old wounds. A girl across from me in 2012 had slept with four of the men present at different times. One of them had a girlfriend who was out of town. I don’t know what to do at parties anyway. They were kind of boring, even when I was young. Get drunk and listen to people talk? My presence there was so unnatural. I still chose to be there.

That wound was reopened at a university language cafe in Rovaniemi, Finland. There were tables with different country flags representing languages you could practice speaking. Native speakers ran the table, and people could join from all different levels. Why, Christopher, did you not follow your heart and do something like this in university? Why did you watch life transpire around you at sketchy basement house parties?

To be more integrated, I have to forgive myself too. Maybe true love is rarer than we imagine. Maybe it’s only rare because we choose the expected arrival of another before we choose ourselves. As I integrate another person into my life, I have to ask myself: Am I moving towards a life that is meaningful to me? Or am I holding a place open for another before I’ve fully chosen myself?

I can continue to be a stranger in my own life, or I can choose myself, and let life be a byproduct of me. The Western individual and Eastern collective values are beside the point. You attract who you choose to be.

text:
False Christians devastate the name of true Christians. This is how true Christians act, they don’t kill people, they don’t start revolutions, they pray for the kings, the ultimate dictators. They pray for all who are in authority, and our prayer is that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity because this is good and acceptable in the sight of God, our Savior.  

Government in Biblical Perspective — John MacArthur // January 23, 2011 

So Peter and Paul agree on this, as we would expect. We have a serious responsibility to live out our justification by grace through faith. Our self-sacrificing lives should be models of submission to government authority, no matter whether that government authority is what we want it to be or not. 

This is a biblical pattern for all people.

Now let’s go back to Romans 13. As we look at this initial responsibility, we’ll just take the first one. We’re going to look at the taxes in a little bit, but the first responsibility is to be subject to the higher powers, the powerful governing authorities. That is the standard. Let every person be subject to the governing authorities, the governing powers, every - literally in the original - every soul - every soul, be subject. It’s imperative, which means it’s a command.

It’s the verb hupotassō, which is a familiar New Testament verb. Hupo means under. Hupotassō, essentially a military word which means to line up under a commander, speaks of soldiers lining up under the one who commands them. Get in line underneath the powers that govern, the governing authorities, existing civil government, without limitation, here, without qualification, without caveat. The Greek is “the authorities which are over you, those supreme ruling authorities.” Verse 3 refers to them with the word “rulers.” Rulers.

The text makes no distinction between good ones, bad ones; moral ones, immoral ones; fair ones, unfair ones. And here, were not so much talking about persons. We are to honor the person, the king, and we’ll see more about that. We’re talking about governing authorities, institutions that exist, whether they are monarchies with all their elements or democracies with all their elements. The obedience of Christians to the laws and the rulers and the authorities of the system in which they live, even though they are persecuted, is a matter of obedience to God and a clear conscience before the Lord.

For us, this is a sometimes hard pill to swallow because we have in the past had a nation where certain Christian principles dominated. Certain Christian principles dominated. I just read that the first of the fifty states, Hawaii, has outlawed prayer. Prayer that was offered before the gathering of the senate of Hawaii no longer can be prayed because from time to time someone mentions Jesus Christ, and so they’re the first of the fifty states to ban prayer.

Does that concern me greatly? No, because token prayers mean nothing. But it is an evidence of the fact that there is a massive effort to get God out of everything, unless it’s some other god than the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the God of holy Scripture. That’s what makes us struggle, doesn’t it? Because we have a history of acknowledging God, but we’re way down the path in a post-Christian America.

How do we respond? Listen to 1 Timothy 2:1. “First of all, I urge that entreaties and prayers, petitions, and thanksgivings be made on behalf of all men, for kings and for all who are in authority.” Did you get that? “Entreaties, prayers, petitions, and” - what was the last one? - “thanksgiving be made on behalf of all men, for kings and all who are in authority, so that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity.” This is a far cry from a revolution, right? This is a far cry from terrorism. This is Christianity. This is how real Christians behave in a society.

False Christians devastate the name of true Christians.

text:
ON THIS DAY IN TECH HISTORY: Ethernet turns 53.

It started with two engineers, a reel of coax and a soldering iron.

On November 11, 1973, Bob Metcalfe and David Boggs got the first Ethernet running at Xerox PARC in Palo Alto. It came out of a very practical problem.

Xerox had built the Alto, a computer with a graphical interface and a mouse, years before the IBM PC. PARC wanted one on every desk. Those machines needed to share files, reach other networks and feed an experimental laser printer that could eat data faster than any connection of the day could deliver.

Metcalfe was in the lab firing pulses down a long coax cable and watching an oscilloscope. Boggs, a Stanford grad student working nearby, saw him fighting with the connectors and offered to help. That partnership ended up connecting billions of devices.

Metcalfe borrowed from ALOHAnet, a radio network in Hawaii, and moved the idea onto a shared cable. Every machine listened before it talked. If two talked at once, they caught the collision, waited a random beat and tried again. First speed: 2.94 Mbps, an odd number set by the Alto's clock.

The memo went out in May 1973. By November it worked. Later on, thick yellow coax ran through office ceilings, with machines clamped on using "vampire taps" that literally bit through the cable. I remember that era well.

Boggs passed away in 2022. Metcalfe picked up the Turing Award the following year. Well earned for both.

Now Ethernet runs the enterprise, the cloud and the data center. We're moving from 400G to 800G, and 1.6T is arriving. That's quite a run from 2.94 Mbps.

AI is driving the next big Ethernet cycle. Thousands of GPUs trade huge amounts of data in tight sync. When the network chokes, very expensive accelerators sit idle, and that hits training time, power bills and the whole economics of an AI build.

The Ultra Ethernet Consortium is tuning congestion control and transport for AI and HPC. Faster switch silicon, silicon photonics and co-packaged optics are going after bandwidth density and power. InfiniBand and custom GPU interconnects still win where latency is everything.

My bet is Ethernet keeps gaining ground in AI. Open standards, lots of suppliers, interoperability and tools every network team already knows add up to real money for hyperscalers and enterprises. When you're spending billions on compute, avoiding lock-in to one vendor matters a lot.

Not bad for two engineers trying to hook some research computers up to a printer.

53 years later, the job is the same: get machines talking faster, cheaper and more reliably.

Happy birthday Ethernet, and hats off to the Ethernet Alliance for keeping it moving.

#Ethernet #TechHistory #AI #Networking #DataCenters

text:
Letter from Cocke,
Hello my brother,
I know it has been sometime since we have actually spoken to each other but I just wanted you to know I am doing fine these days. Living the good life had has its payoffs with these five children and their children I could have never imagined it being so many of us to continue on. Frances has been busy doing what she really likes and that’s always seeing that everyone is eating right and caring for the one’s that are sick or in need of attention, the nurse coming out. I know that you must be so happy to have the little ones running around, of course you have to move everything, but they are really something aren’t they? I was looking at this new design on an old project in Washington that is up for bids and things are going pretty steady on the courthouse facelift downtown. I never imagined that living my dream as an Architect would be both fulfilling and productive. I really should retire now don’t you think? Avoiding the war really gave me the chance to find out exactly who I was and getting to go to college really made the difference. Two of the boys seem to like doing this so I suppose I will leave it in good hands. I haven’t had the chance to speak to anyone else yet so if you would tell all that I am doing fine. I am hoping we can get together soon.
Of course you know this is not true but I cannot tell you how many times I wanted it to be. The experiences of war took much of my life away, my personality, ambition but never the willingness to live or have a family which helped me with this constant haunting memory. You know all too well about the war as I know you were living then as you are today and with you are memories just as mine similar but different. After the Japanese did what they did to us in Hawaii you know I had to go and fight, it wasn’t really a choice as I would have had to serve regardless of the branch I was in. Guess our childhood helped me a lot having all these brothers to fight with and sisters to pick on and John being as mischievous as he was, I wasn’t, was I? Ha before all that mess broke out I was thinking about becoming an Architect or Artist or something with a future for me but for them to do what they to us, all that killing and for what? It seemed we were being pulled into war no matter what. So, off I went to fight and fight I did, I do not know if you remember when I cut all my hair off and left a big V across the back but I guess that can say much about how I was thinking as I was headed into the unknown where I knew many would die perhaps even me but I knew I would take as many with me as I could before going, after all, I joined to fight for my country and make the others die for theirs. “SEMPER FI” I was one tough marine, had to be, at least on the outside. I never knew during all that fighting and killing that I would carry that around with me for the rest of my life and how it affected everyone. It is funny when a handful of months can change ones whole life and outlook and the fact I hadn’t the chance to choose my profession. Who knows? I could have been a hobo. As it turns out I was a marine fighting and killing, I don’t know if I ever told you any of those stories from those memorial months, maybe I did talk some of it but I am sure it wasn’t as much as I did to my wife and children about blowing up bridges, machine gun traps, tanks, land mines blowing legs off, flame throwers burning people alive and the screaming, while all the long the ones I had began to know as friends were dieing right before my eyes and the times when I didn’t think I was going to make it. I cried many times hoping those memories would leave me but never did. I always cried for the ones who never returned home as they lost any chance in marriage and children, life and it took many years living it over and over hoping time would help me. I have heard that is was evident my months away from home had changed me for life and that I wasn’t the same person I was when I left but it is only now that I see how much, It seems I wasn’t the ambitious person I was before and I need room to breath, maybe farm and enjoy what nature had to offer so with the help of my family that is just what I did. But you know? No matter how long or hard I worked the memories of those months would sometimes control my mind and I had to work, stay busy or just do nothing and the drink helped with the pain of those memories and I guess that some of those “worthless” ole cronies didn’t help matters but they were fun, you know some of them too. The more time went by the better things got, at least I thought so and I had my times, raising five kids surely kept me busy and Frances, well she was the best thing that ever happened to me for sure. I know I really fooled everyone when that bucket fell from the top of the well I was working in and fractured my skull especially when the doctors mentioned I would either be mentally incompetent or die. HA, well the truth be known it was the unconditional love of my wife and her always standing by my side that got me through that ordeal along with those experiences of the 1940”s. I was never afraid to die after that and maybe that was one of the biggest changes in me. Then of course the times I hate to remember now are the times when my children had to see me cry or drink or talk about those horrible moments of that handful of months and how it affected me, my whole family, siblings and all. I could not always block it out so I tried to accept it and deal with it as best I could and that was one day at a time. In my childhood I remember delivering groceries to one of our neighbors for dad and before I could leave she grabbed my arm and said to me “run and hide” as she believed the Yankees were coming. I would have never imagined what she was experiencing and saying was similar but different in the years to come for me. I told that story many times to my children along with many others including those unfortunate times in my life. I keep returning to those times just as they keep returning to me and know now that I passed some of those memories to my children just as you know I am not here in mind but in soul and memory. It is not my hands that write this but the hands of someone else who sometimes cries for me but that is OK. I must say I could have taken better care of myself but when you are married to a nurse, she has five kids, maybe, I had an excuse. HA Now that I have lived through it all I believe that perhaps there is a positive side to all of this. I see all five children with wives and children and their children with children and they all seem to be doing well considering the road they traveled thus far. Perhaps it made them stronger but more vulnerable, weaker but more determined, disoriented but more focused as the direst of errors, which occurs wherever argument or interference passes from world of experience to another and results in confusion. I hope things go well with you and family as it continues to grow and that we never have to put anyone else in those predicaments again but the Marine in me supports any reason to keep our country free even if I have to do it all over again. Well, maybe not. You were right in your saying that there were two of me, the one before the war and the one after but I was still the same Cocke, I just had some extra heavy baggage I had to carry around. I am now at peace and worry no more. Tell I am always here; all they have to do is think of me. I love you all.
Henry L. Moon 2003

text:
$PK Operators React to Earnings
Full Report now ready.

Our interviews revealed:

On group spend, they were constructive. An industry expert in consumer services said international attendees, such as Canadians avoiding US travel, could have washed out big blocks booked long in advance: "it's a very plausible explanation that these impacts were more one-time and not structural." Another said weak banquet capture matters less than it looks, since rooms groups flow through far better than labor-heavy food and beverage.

On costs, they were cautious. One said wage inflation already runs above the guide, so growth will be hard to slow. Another said unionized hotels offer no quick fix and insurance and tax savings tend not to repeat: "there is no sudden lever you can pull to reduce labor cost". The third credited rising occupancy, though overtime and temporary labor climb when occupancy spikes.

On the renovations, they were constructive. The expert who raised the Canadian cancellations said every luxury rival is renovating too: "If you're not, then you're falling behind". The one who spoke on banquets said ramp timing is what underwriting most often gets wrong, and Hawaii depends on Japanese visitors that domestic travel cannot replace.

The open question: whether group spend outside the room comes back.

Source views are those of senior operators and industry experts interviewed by Heron. Not investment advice.

HONORING SERVICE🫡🇺🇸: J.F. Drake Middle School continued a longstanding tradition by hosting its 23rd Annual Veterans Day Program to honor those who have served in the United States Armed Forces!
•
✅Students took an active role throughout the ceremony, sharing the history and meaning behind Veterans Day, recognizing veterans and special guests, and reflecting on the sacrifices made by generations of military service members.
•
🎤Auburn City Schools Superintendent Dr. Cristen Herring offered welcoming remarks, followed by a special address from retired U.S. Air Force Colonel J. David “Rock” Bottomlee, this year's guest speaker.
•
🎺The Auburn High School Vocal Jazz ensemble performed "The Star-Spangled Banner" and "America the Beautiful," and the ceremony closed with a moment of silence and the playing of "Taps" by Cricket Hayes, an Alum of AHS, AHSMB, and concert bands, now in the marching band at Auburn University!
•
📍For more than two decades, Drake's annual Veterans Day program has helped students better understand the significance of military service and the importance of preserving the stories and sacrifices of those who have defended our nation.
•
💙We appreciate Colonel Bottomlee, the veterans and guests in attendance, and the students, faculty, and staff who helped carry on this special tradition!

text:
A preacher everyone protected. In Blue Hollow, Clive hides behind his Sunday sermons. Hymns of Blue Hollow, Book 1. 

Trapped in the unforgiving hills of Tennessee in 1941, Esther Primm is chained to a life of hardship and moonshining under her grandmother's cruel watch.
Lurking in the shadows, bootlegging Preacher Clive, obsessed and driven by dark desires, refuses to release his grip on her. Ian Huggler, a German man with his own haunted past, offers Esther a glimmer of hope and ignites a passion in her untamed spirit.
But will Esther be strong enough to break free and fight for something she doesn't believe she deserves?
Hymns of Blue Hollow is a vividly raw and lyrical tale of resilience, survival, and the pursuit of freedom. Fans of Where the Crawdads Sing and The Nightingale will find themselves captivated by this evocative story set against the haunting backdrop of historical Appalachia during WWII.

text:
I feel like I’ve been in a hundred meetings at this point where an advocate proposes a private, multistate entity funded by participating universities to employ athletes and bargain with their representative as a way to overcome restrictions on collective bargaining at public universities.

As always, I’m happy to engage here or elsewhere, but I’m skeptical that this resolves the legal problems as readily as its advocates suggest.

Let’s start with the basics: the assertion that “schools would not be the employer” requires explanation. Creating another entity to sign contracts and issue paychecks does not resolve the significance of universities selecting athletes, employing coaches, supervising their work, imposing discipline, etc. What changes under this proposal?

There is modest precedent supporting the approach. In Teledyne Economic Development v. NLRB, 108 F.3d 56 (4th Cir. 1997), for instance, the court upheld a bargaining obligation for a private Job Corps contractor despite substantial government control. Retained university control therefore would not automatically defeat federal jurisdiction over a private employer.

But three questions must remain separate: federal employer status, state-law authority to make the necessary commitments, and enforceability. 

Establishing that a private entity can bargain does not establish that a public university can lawfully make every commitment necessary to implement that bargain.

The NLRB cannot compel an exempt public university to bargain. Where a university retains exclusive authority over a working condition, proponents must explain how negotiations with the central employer would produce enforceable protections. Where authority is shared or transferred, they must identify the legal basis for that allocation.

Even the entity’s status requires scrutiny. Under Hawkins County, an entity may be an exempt political subdivision if created directly by the state as a governmental arm or administered by individuals responsible to public officials or the electorate. Its formation and governance—including who appoints and removes its leaders—matter.

State law presents additional complications. The University of Tennessee assigns control of athletics to its chancellors under trustee oversight. Texas prohibits specified collective bargaining contracts concerning public employees. Proponents must explain which powers universities would relinquish or contractually limit, what authorizes those commitments, and why the arrangement complies with each state’s restrictions.

Enforcement matters, too. If a university suspends an athlete or imposes practice requirements inconsistent with the agreement, who can enforce it, against whom, and through what remedy? Sovereign immunity does not necessarily foreclose enforcement--Tennessee permits certain authorized written-contract claims--but the model must explain whether athletes can obtain timely compliance or only compensation after the opportunity to participate has passed.

I could go on, but advocates keep assuring us that this works under existing law and that accomplished lawyers have vetted it. I'm a broken record, but show your work. 

Identify who controls each significant term, who can commit to changing it, and who can be held to that commitment.

I’ve asked these questions repeatedly and have yet to see a legal analysis that answers them. That gap between the confidence of the claim and the explanation offered is why I remain skeptical.

text:
Civitai—an online marketplace for buying and selling AI-generated content, backed by the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz—is letting users buy custom instruction files for generating celebrity deepfakes. Some of these files were specifically designed to make pornographic images banned by the site, a new analysis has found.

The study, from researchers at Stanford and Indiana University, looked at people’s requests for content on the site, called “bounties.” The researchers found that between mid-2023 and the end of 2024, most bounties asked for animated content—but a significant portion were for deepfakes of real people, and 90% of these deepfake requests targeted women. (Their findings have not yet been peer reviewed.)

The debate around deepfakes, as illustrated by the recent backlash to explicit images on the X-owned chatbot Grok, has revolved around what platforms should do to block such content. Civitai’s situation is a little more complicated. Its marketplace includes actual images, videos, and models, but it also lets individuals buy and sell instruction files called LoRAs that can coach mainstream AI models like Stable Diffusion into generating content they were not trained to produce. Users can then combine these files with other tools to make deepfakes that are graphic or sexual. The researchers found that 86% of deepfake requests on Civitai were for LoRAs.

In these bounties, users requested “high quality” models to generate images of public figures like the influencer Charli D’Amelio or the singer Gracie Abrams, often linking to their social media profiles so their images could be grabbed from the web. Some requests specified a desire for models that generated the individual’s entire body, accurately captured their tattoos, or allowed hair color to be changed. Some requests targeted several women in specific niches, like artists who record ASMR videos. One request was for a deepfake of a woman said to be the user’s wife. Anyone on the site could offer up AI models they worked on for the task, and the best submissions received payment—anywhere from $0.50 to $5. And nearly 92% of the deepfake bounties were awarded.

Neither Civitai nor Andreessen Horowitz responded to requests for comment.

It’s possible that people buy these LoRAs to make deepfakes that aren’t sexually explicit (though they’d still violate Civitai’s terms of use, and they’d still be ethically fraught). But Civitai also offers educational resources on how to use external tools to further customize the outputs of image generators—for example, by changing someone’s pose. The site also hosts user-written articles with details on how to instruct models to generate pornography. The researchers found that the amount of porn on the platform has gone up, and that the majority of requests each week are now for NSFW content.

“Not only does Civitai provide the infrastructure that facilitates these issues; they also explicitly teach their users how to utilize them,” says Matthew DeVerna, a postdoctoral researcher at Stanford’s Cyber Policy Center and one of the study’s leaders. 

The company used to ban only sexually explicit deepfakes of real people, but in May 2025 it announced it would ban all deepfake content. Nonetheless, countless requests for deepfakes submitted before this ban now remain live on the site, and many of the winning submissions fulfilling those requests remain available for purchase, MIT Technology Review confirmed.

“I believe the approach that they’re trying to take is to sort of do as little as possible, such that they can foster as much—I guess they would call it—creativity on the platform,” DeVerna says.

Users buy LoRAs with the site’s online currency, called Buzz, which is purchased with real money. In May 2025, Civita’s credit card processor cut off the company because of its ongoing problem with nonconsensual content. To pay for explicit content, users must now use gift cards or cryptocurrency to buy Buzz; the company offers a different scrip for non-explicit content. 

Civitai automatically tags bounties requesting deepfakes and lists a way for the person featured in the content to manually request its takedown. This system means that Civitai has a reasonably successful way of knowing which bounties are for deepfakes, but it’s still leaving moderation to the general public rather than carrying it out proactively. 

A company’s legal liability for what its users do isn’t totally clear. Generally, tech companies have broad legal protections against such liability for their content under Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, but those protections aren’t limitless. For example, “you cannot knowingly facilitate illegal transactions on your website,” says Ryan Calo, a professor specializing in technology and AI at the University of Washington’s law school. (Calo wasn’t involved in this new study.)

Civitai joined OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI companies in 2024 in adopting design principles to guard against the creation and spread of AI-generated child sexual abuse material . This move followed a 2023 report from the Stanford Internet Observatory, which found that the vast majority of AI models named in child sexual abuse communities were Stable Diffusion–based models “predominantly obtained via Civitai.”

But adult deepfakes have not gotten the same level of attention from content platforms or the venture capital firms that fund them. “They are not afraid enough of it. They are overly tolerant of it,” Calo says. “Neither law enforcement nor civil courts adequately protect against it. It is night and day.”

Civitai received a $5 million investment from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) in November 2023. In a video shared by a16z, Civitai cofounder and CEO Justin Maier described his goal of building the main place where people find and share AI models for their own individual purposes. “We’ve aimed to make this space that’s been very, I guess, niche and engineering-heavy more and more approachable to more and more people,” he said. 

Civitai is not the only company with a deepfake problem in a16z’s investment portfolio; in February, MIT Technology Review first reported that another company, Botify AI, was hosting AI companions resembling real actors that stated their age as under 18, engaged in sexually charged conversations, offered “hot photos,” and in some instances described age-of-consent laws as “arbitrary” and “meant to be broken.”
