The Covenant Gate Opened beyond Bloodline, the Eunuch Granted an Everlasting Memorial within the Walls of God, the Stranger Drawn into the Holy Mountain, the House of Prayer Enlarged for All Peoples, the Gathering beyond the Gathered, and the Collapse of Blind Watchmen before the Beasts of Judgment

📜 56 Chapter Heading 📜

“1 The Prophet exhorteth to sanctification. 3 He promiseth it shall be generall without respect of persons. 9 He inueyeth against blinde watchmen.”

The 1611 heading catches the chapter's radical movement. Isaiah 55 invited every thirsty person to the waters.

 Isaiah 56 begins showing what that enlargement looks like socially and covenantally: stranger, foreigner, and eunuch are brought into sacred proximity; the holy mountain opens; prayer becomes universal; and further outcasts are gathered. 

Then the chapter turns sharply toward leaders who cannot see, cannot bark, cannot understand, and cannot stop consuming.

VERSE + COMMENTARY STARTS NOW/HERE - 

📜 Isaiah 56:1

“Thus saith the LORD, Keepe yee ||iudgement, and doe iustice: for my saluation is neere to come, and my righteousnesse to bee reuealed.”

📌 1611 Margin

|| Or, judgement.

📝 Commentary

Isaiah joins ethics and eschatology. Keep justice and do righteousness because “my salvation is near” and “my righteousness [is] to be revealed.”

Hebrew uses יְשׁוּעָה, yeshu‘ah, salvation, from the same root underlying the name Yeshua. Then צְדָקָה, tsedaqah, righteousness, approaches revelation. The verb גלה, galah, uncover or reveal, belongs conceptually to the same world as Greek apokalypsis, unveiling.

Isaiah 51:5 had already said, “My righteousness is near; my salvation is gone forth.” Isaiah 52 declared that all ends of earth would see God's salvation. Isaiah 56 continues the convergence. The approaching salvation demands present holiness. Eschatology generates ethics.

📜 Isaiah 56:2

“Blessed is the man that doeth this, and the sonne of man that layeth holde on it: that keepeth the Sabbath from polluting it, and keepeth his hand from doing any euill.”

📝 Commentary

The Sabbath enters as a creation-covenant institution. Genesis 2 places sacred rest at the completion of creation. Exodus 20 grounds Sabbath in creation. Deuteronomy 5 grounds it also in liberation from Egypt. Exodus 31 identifies it as covenant sign.

Isaiah now joins Sabbath with moral restraint: keep the Sabbath and keep the hand from evil. The parallel prevents ritual observance from being severed from righteousness. The “hand” is the organ of action. One keeps sacred time while restraining destructive agency.

Hebrews 4 later develops Sabbath into an eschatological rest of God, connecting creation-rest with final participation in Divine rest. Sabbath therefore possesses chronological, liturgical, covenantal, ethical, and eschatological dimensions.

📜 Isaiah 56:3

“¶ Neither let the sonne of the stranger, that hath ioyned himselfe to the LORD, speake, saying, The LORD hath vtterly separated mee from his people: neither let the Eunuch say, Behold, I am a drie tree.”

📝 Commentary

Two people fear exclusion: the foreigner and the eunuch. The foreigner fears covenant separation; the eunuch fears genealogical extinction.

His phrase, “I am a dry tree,” returns us directly to Isaiah's botanical theology. A dry tree cannot reproduce. Isaiah 53 presented the Messiah as a root emerging from dry ground. Isaiah 54 presented the barren woman suddenly producing children. Isaiah 56 now confronts a person whose bodily condition prevents descendants.

The prophetic answer is that covenant memory can exceed biological continuity. This creates a fascinating canonical correspondence with Acts 8. Immediately after Philip explains Isaiah 53 to the Ethiopian eunuch, the eunuch asks for baptism and enters the Messianic community.

Isaiah 56 lies only three chapters beyond the text he was reading. Acts does not explicitly say the Ethiopian then read Isaiah 56, but the narrative resonance is remarkable: an actual eunuch and foreigner is incorporated into the people of Messiah precisely in the Isaianic environment where YHWH promises a name to eunuchs and inclusion to foreigners.

📜 Isaiah 56:4

“For thus saith the LORD vnto the Eunuches that keepe my Sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and take hold of my couenant:”

📝 Commentary

The decisive criteria are covenantal: keep, choose, take hold. The person socially incapable of producing an ordinary dynastic future is capable of active covenant fidelity.

“Take hold” is strong language. Covenant is imagined as something grasped and retained. The text therefore reorders value. Physical capacity for descendants does not determine ultimate remembrance before YHWH.

This continues the great Isaianic theme of Divine calling overcoming ordinary probability structures: barren Sarah, barren Zion, dry ground producing a root, eunuch called a dry tree. Human biological limitation does not limit Divine covenantal creativity.

📜 Isaiah 56:5

“Euen vnto them will I giue in mine house, and within my walles, a place and a name better then of sonnes and of daughters: I will giue them an euerlasting name, that shall not be cut off.”

📝 Commentary

Hebrew contains the famous phrase יָד וָשֵׁם, yad va-shem, literally “a hand/place/monument and a name,” traditionally understood as a memorial and a name.

The promise is better than sons and daughters. Ancient society often preserved personal memory through descendants. The eunuch fears exactly this loss. YHWH promises a different mode of permanence.

Then comes a brilliant wordplay: the eunuch fears being genealogically cut off, while YHWH gives him a name that “shall not be cut off.” Biological discontinuity is answered by everlasting Divine remembrance.

The location is also important: “in mine house and within my walls.” The formerly marginal person is relocated into sacred interiority. He does not remain perpetually outside the sanctuary perimeter. He receives a place inside.

📜 Isaiah 56:6

“Also the sonnes of the stranger that ioyne themselues to the LORD, to serue him, and to loue the Name of the LORD, to be his seruants, euery one that keepeth the Sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my Couenant:”

📝 Commentary

Foreigners are described through covenant verbs: join, serve, love, keep, take hold.

The phrase “love the Name of YHWH” is especially deep. The Name in Scripture represents revealed identity, authority, reputation, and covenant presence. Isaiah 52 had said YHWH's people would know His Name. Here foreigners love His Name.

This anticipates the New Testament's multinational devotion to the Name of Yeshua and the apostolic mission among the nations. Acts 15, quoting Amos 9, speaks of Gentiles upon whom the Divine Name is called. Ephesians 2 describes those once strangers and foreigners becoming fellow citizens and members of God's household.

Isaiah 56 therefore stands as a major prophetic precursor to that incorporation.

📜 Isaiah 56:7

“Euen them will I bring to my holy mountaine, and make them ioyfull in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted vpon mine Altar: for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.”

📌 1611 Side References

Isaiah 2:2.
Matthew 21:13; Mark 11:17; Luke 19:46.

📝 Commentary

This is one of Isaiah's greatest sacred-geographical texts. Foreigners are brought to my holy mountain, my house, and my altar. The movement is centripetal toward Zion.

Isaiah 2 had already envisioned nations streaming toward the mountain of YHWH to receive Torah. Now those nations enter the sanctuary's prayer-life.

The Hebrew phrase is:

בֵּיתִי בֵּית־תְּפִלָּה יִקָּרֵא לְכָל־הָעַמִּים

“My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.”

The Septuagint similarly has οἶκος προσευχῆς... πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν. Latin: domus orationis... cunctis populis.

Yeshua quotes this verse during the Temple cleansing. His action therefore invokes Isaiah's prophetic destiny of the Temple as sacred space for the nations. Ephesians 2 then develops an astonishing extension: Jews and Gentiles together become a living Temple, built together into a habitation of God through the Spirit.

Thus Isaiah's holy mountain and Paul's Spirit-built Temple belong to one expanding sacred geography.

📜 Isaiah 56:8

“The Lord GOD which gathereth the outcasts of Israel, saith, Yet will I gather others to him, †besides those that are gathered vnto him.”

📌 1611 Margin

† Heb. to his gathered.

📝 Commentary

YHWH is identified as Gatherer. Isaiah's entire later prophecy is filled with regathering: sons and daughters from cardinal directions, exiles returning, nations approaching, barren Zion enlarging.

Now the promise expands again:

“I will gather others.”

This resonates powerfully with John 10:16: “Other sheep I haue, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring... and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.”

Ephesians 2-3 again supplies the apostolic architecture: those once far away become fellow citizens, fellow heirs, and members of the same body. The movement is scattered → gathered, foreign → household, many peoples → one covenant body.

The God who once divided nations at Babel is also the God who gathers nations beneath Messiah.

📜 Isaiah 56:9

“¶ All ye beasts of the field, come to deuoure, yea all ye beasts in the forest.”

📝 Commentary

The chapter suddenly changes atmosphere. The inclusive sanctuary vision gives way to predatory summons. Field beasts and forest beasts are called to devour.

Prophetic literature frequently uses predatory animals both literally and symbolically for invading powers, violent rulers, and instruments of judgment. Jeremiah 12:9 similarly summons beasts against a corrupted inheritance. Ezekiel 34 depicts failed shepherds leaving sheep vulnerable to beasts. Daniel's apocalyptic visions go further, representing kingdoms themselves as monstrous beasts.

Isaiah need not be reduced to only one of those levels. The image works because the ecosystem of leadership has failed. When watchmen no longer watch, predators gain access. Verse 9 therefore functions as the terrible consequence of verses 10-12: the guardians are asleep, and the beasts are invited.

📜 Isaiah 56:10

“His watchmen are blinde: they are all ignorant, they are all dumbe dogs, they cannot barke: ||sleeping, lying downe, louing to slumber.”

📌 1611 Margin

|| Or, dreaming, or talking in their sleepe.

📝 Commentary

This verse is a devastating anatomy of failed spiritual perception. A watchman requires eyes to see, knowledge to interpret, voice to warn, and wakefulness to remain vigilant. Isaiah removes all four.

They are blind, ignorant, mute, and sleeping.

Compare Isaiah 52:8, where the faithful watchmen “see eye to eye” and lift their voices together when YHWH returns to Zion. Isaiah 56 gives the anti-watchman. The sensorium has collapsed.

Ezekiel 3 and 33 define the prophet-watchman's responsibility to perceive approaching danger and sound warning. Failure creates bloodguilt. The dog-image is equally striking. Guard dogs are valuable precisely because they detect what sleeping humans cannot and bark before danger reaches the dwelling.

These dogs cannot bark.

Spiritual leadership has lost its early-warning function. The 1611 marginal possibility “dreaming or talking in their sleep” adds an almost surreal phenomenology: leaders may still produce sounds and internal imagery while possessing no useful waking perception.

📜 Isaiah 56:11

“Yea they are †greedy dogges which †can neuer haue ynough, and they are shepheards that cannot vnderstand: they all looke to their owne way, euery one for his gaine, from his quarter.”

📌 1611 Margins

† Heb. strong of appetite.
† Heb. know not to be satisfied.

📝 Commentary

The watchmen's sensory failure now becomes appetite disorder. The 1611 margin is revealing: “strong of appetite.” Their hunger is powerful while their understanding is weak. They do not know how to be satisfied.

This is almost a spiritual pathology of infinite consumption. The shepherds who should feed the flock instead feed themselves. Ezekiel 34 condemns precisely this: shepherds consume fat and wool but fail to strengthen, heal, bind, or seek the sheep. Zechariah 11 also depicts destructive shepherding. Micah 3 uses horrifying consumption imagery for corrupt rulers.

Yeshua's John 10 shepherd discourse provides the Christological counterpart. The good shepherd gives His life for the sheep. Isaiah's false shepherd consumes; Yeshua gives Himself. The contrast reaches back to Isaiah 53, where the Servant voluntarily pours out His own soul.

📜 Isaiah 56:12

“Come ye, say they, I will fetch wine, and we will fill our selues with strong drinke, and to morrow shall be as this day, and much more abundant.”

📝 Commentary

The chapter ends with eschatological complacency. The leaders assume continuity: today is abundant, and tomorrow will be more abundant. Their worldview contains no approaching rupture.

This is the exact opposite of the prophetic consciousness of Isaiah 56:1:

“my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.”

The prophet sees imminent Divine disclosure. The blind shepherd sees only another prosperous tomorrow.

Yeshua later depicts the rich fool saying he has goods laid up for many years, unaware that his life ends that night. 1 Thessalonians 5 warns of people saying “Peace and safety” before sudden destruction. 2 Peter 3 describes mockers assuming that all things continue as before.

2 Esdras 16:21 offers a striking apocalyptic parallel: provisions may appear cheap and plentiful so people imagine themselves “in good case,” immediately before sword, famine, and confusion erupt.

The ancient prophetic diagnosis is consistent: abundance can anesthetize perception. Isaiah 56 therefore ends where its failed watchmen naturally lead. They possess no sight, no warning voice, no understanding, unlimited appetite, and confidence that tomorrow will simply magnify today.

That is the precise psychological condition in which judgment arrives unseen.

🔑 MASTER ARCHITECTURE OF ISAIAH 55-56

Isaiah 55 begins with:

“Come ye to the waters.”

Isaiah 56 reaches:

“I will bring them to my holy mountain.”

The two chapters therefore describe a movement of approach. First the thirsty come to water; then the listener comes to YHWH; unknown nations run toward the glorified Davidic figure; the wicked returns to YHWH; rain and snow descend from heaven; the Word goes forth from YHWH's mouth; the redeemed go forth with joy; foreigners are brought to the holy mountain; and further outcasts are gathered.

The repeated motion is extraordinary: come → incline → hear → live → seek → return → descend → go forth → prosper → sing → arise → join → take hold → bring → gather.

Isaiah's theology is intensely kinetic.

These chapters also create an enormous vertical system: higher heavens → rain and snow → Divine Word → earth → seed → bread → human life → transformed vegetation → holy mountain → sanctuary → altar → prayer of the nations.

Heaven acts upon earth. Earth answers heaven. At the center of the exchange is the effective Word of YHWH.

The Davidic Messiah stands within that system as witness, leader, commander, glorified one, and magnet of the nations. The New Testament identifies the free waters with Yeshua's invitation, the sure mercies of David with His resurrection, the house of prayer with His Temple declaration, the gathered outsiders with the expanding covenant people, and heavenly-earthly reconciliation with the cosmic headship described in Ephesians.

Isaiah 55-56 therefore gives us an extraordinary field of Messianic Hydrology, Davidic Resurrection Theology, Sacred Meteorology, Performative Divine Speech, Heaven-Earth Causality, Eschatological Botany, Covenant Anthropology, Sanctuary Geography, Foreign-Nation Incorporation, Eunuch Restoration, Onomastic Immortality, Mountain Theology, Living-Temple Correspondence, Watchman Phenomenology, Spiritual Sensorium Failure, Predatory Leadership, and Apocalyptic Complacency.

The great contrast closing the study is difficult to miss:

Isaiah 55 says YHWH's Word never returns empty. Isaiah 56 ends with shepherds who are themselves never satisfied.

One Divine utterance accomplishes its purpose completely. The corrupted appetite of man can consume endlessly and still remain empty.

That contrast may be one of the most subtle theological structures linking the two chapters.

#ApocalypticBookStudy #119

📜 Isaiah 55:1-13 - 56:1-12 📜 

🔑 Specialist Study: The Free Waters of Messiah, the Everlasting Davidic Covenant, the Word Descending like Rain from the Higher Heavens, Creation Answering in Song, the Stranger and Eunuch Drawn inside the Holy Mountain, the House of Prayer Enlarged among the Nations, and the Collapse of Blind Watchmen at the Threshold of Divine Salvation

ISAIAH 55 - BEGINS (PLEASE SEE THE NEXT POST FOR ISAIAH 56) 

📜 1611 Chapter Heading

“1 The Prophet, with the promises of Christ, calleth to faith, 6 and to repentance. 8 The happy successe of them that beleeue.”

The 1611 heading immediately places Isaiah 55 inside the Messianic movement of Isaiah 52-54. The Servant has suffered, borne sin, emerged beyond death, justified many, and opened the covenant toward an enlarged Zion. Isaiah 55 now sounds like the public invitation following that accomplished work. Water, wine, milk, bread, Davidic covenant, world-embracing witness, heaven-earth transcendence, rain, snow, seed, the effective Word, singing mountains, and transformed vegetation all become instruments of the invitation.

🔑📝📜VERSE + COMMENTARY STARTS HERE/NOW - 

📜 Isaiah 55:1

“Ho, euery one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money: come ye, buy and eat, yea come, buy wine and milke without money, and without price.”

📌 1611 Margin / Side Reference

John 7:37.

📝 Commentary

The chapter opens with the Hebrew summons הוֹי, hôy, an arresting public cry, followed by כָּל־צָמֵא, kol-tsāmē’, “everyone thirsting.” The Greek Septuagint similarly summons οἱ διψῶντες, the thirsty; Latin has omnes sitientes. The theological economy is deliberately paradoxical: buy without money. Something of immeasurable value is distributed outside ordinary monetary exchange.

This develops Isaiah 52:3, “ye shall be redeemed without money.” Redemption has produced a new economy in which the thirsty possess no purchasing power yet are invited to receive. Water, wine, and milk form a triad of life, festivity, and nourishment. Water sustains life; wine belongs to covenantal rejoicing and royal banquet imagery; milk signifies abundance and nutritive richness. Proverbs 9 similarly personifies Wisdom setting a table and calling the simple to eat and drink. Sirach 24 presents Wisdom as nourishment and overflowing waters. Revelation 21:6 and 22:17 eventually repeat the free-water invitation: “whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely.”

The 1611 margin directs us to John 7:37, where Yeshua cries, “If any man thirst, let him come vnto me, and drinke.” John immediately interprets this concerning the Spirit. Thus Isaiah's waters enter Johannine Christology and pneumatology simultaneously. The invitation of YHWH becomes the invitation issued publicly by Yeshua, and the promised water becomes the Spirit flowing from within the believer.

📜 Isaiah 55:2

“Wherefore doe yee †spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently vnto me, and eate ye that which is good, and let your soule delight it selfe in fatnesse.”

📌 1611 Margin

† Heb. weigh.

📝 Commentary

The 1611 margin preserves the older commercial reality. Silver was commonly weighed, so the Hebrew asks why people weigh out silver for what cannot truly nourish. Yet Isaiah immediately moves from economics into epistemology: “hearken diligently... and eat.” Hearing becomes ingestion.

Deuteronomy 8:3 had already established the principle that human life depends upon every word proceeding from the mouth of YHWH, later quoted by Yeshua in Matthew 4:4. Jeremiah 15:16 speaks of finding God's words and eating them. Ezekiel 2-3 and Revelation 10 depict prophetic scrolls actually being consumed symbolically. Isaiah therefore joins the auditory and digestive systems. Divine speech enters through hearing but nourishes the nephesh, the living person.

This creates a remarkable phenomenology of false and true nourishment. Humanity can expend enormous resources upon things incapable of sustaining the deepest level of life. The Divine Word, by contrast, is described in the semantic field of bread and rich food. The sequence anticipates verse 11, where the Word itself goes forth from the Divine mouth with effective power. Here that same Word is received as nourishment.

📜 Isaiah 55:3

“Incline your eare, and come vnto me: heare, and your soule shall liue, and I will make an euerlasting couenant with you, euen the sure mercies of Dauid.”

📌 1611 Side Reference

Acts 13:34.

📝 Commentary

Again the ear becomes an organ of life: incline → come → hear → live. Hebrew שִׁמְעוּ וּתְחִי נַפְשְׁכֶם, shim‘û ûteḥî napshəkhem, means “hear, and your soul shall live.”

The covenant is called בְּרִית עוֹלָם, berit ‘olam, everlasting covenant. Its content is the extraordinary phrase חַסְדֵי דָוִד הַנֶּאֱמָנִים, ḥasdei David hanne’emanim, the faithful or sure mercies of David. The Septuagint renders this τὰ ὅσια Δαυὶδ τὰ πιστά, the holy or faithful things of David. Acts 13:34 quotes precisely this Greek wording while Paul argues for the resurrection of Yeshua.

That is enormously important. In apostolic interpretation, Isaiah 55:3 becomes resurrection evidence. The everlasting Davidic covenant requires a Davidic ruler whose promised kingship cannot be terminated by death. Psalm 89, Psalm 132, 2 Samuel 7, and Isaiah 9 all stand behind this. The promised Davidic throne reaches its enduring realization in Messiah.

Thus the chapter's free waters are tied immediately to resurrection kingship. Isaiah 53's Servant died and then continued to see, act, and prosper. Isaiah 55 identifies the post-death Messianic horizon with the sure mercies promised to David.

📜 Isaiah 55:4

“Behold, I haue giuen him for a witnesse to the people, a leader and commander to the people.”

📝 Commentary

The Davidic figure of verse 3 now receives three functions: witness, leader, and commander. Hebrew עֵד, ‘ēd, means witness; נָגִיד, nāgîd, ruler, prince, or leader; מְצַוֵּה, metsawweh, commander.

The word nāgîd belongs to royal leadership vocabulary and is used elsewhere for rulers appointed over Yisra’el. The third title derives from the root tsawah, command, the same broad verbal field associated with commandments. The Messiah therefore bears both revelatory and governmental functions. As witness, He reveals truth; as leader, He governs movement; as commander, His word possesses authority.

Revelation 1:5 calls Yeshua “the faithful witness” and “the prince of the kings of the earth.” Revelation 19 presents Him as royal warrior commanding the eschatological victory. This also corresponds with Ephesians 1. The One who bears witness on earth becomes the One enthroned far above all principality, power, might, and dominion. Isaiah's Davidic commander is therefore already moving toward universal Messianic jurisdiction.

📜 Isaiah 55:5

“Behold, thou shalt call a nation that thou knowest not, and nations that knew not thee shall runne vnto thee, because of the LORD thy God, and for the holy One of Israel, for he hath glorified thee.”

📝 Commentary

The Davidic-Messianic horizon becomes international. Unknown nations hear a call and run toward the glorified one. This continues Isaiah 49:6, where the Servant becomes light to Gentiles and salvation to the ends of the earth; Isaiah 52:15, where nations and kings encounter unprecedented revelation; and Isaiah 54:3, where Zion's seed expands among the nations.

The verb run gives conversion kinetic form. The nations do not drift slowly into proximity. They move with urgency toward the one glorified by YHWH. Ephesians 2-3 supplies the apostolic unfolding: Gentiles formerly alienated from the commonwealth of Yisra’el become fellow heirs, members of the same body, and partakers of promise in Christ.

The national powers and territorial divisions of the old world are therefore being penetrated by a new Messianic gathering. The Holy One of Yisra’el has glorified His appointed figure, and the resulting glory exerts a centripetal pull upon the nations.

📜 Isaiah 55:6

“¶ Seeke ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye vpon him while he is neere.”

📝 Commentary

Isaiah introduces a theology of sacred opportunity. The Divine Presence is described through relational proximity: found and near. This does not imply YHWH ceases to be omnipresent. The language concerns the appointed season of accessible mercy.

Second Temple apocalyptic literature frequently emphasizes appointed times, bounded periods of repentance, and moments when judgment becomes irreversible. 2 Esdras repeatedly warns that history moves toward thresholds after which neglected opportunity cannot simply be recovered. The New Testament retains the same urgency. 2 Corinthians 6:2 says, “behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.”

The Greek concept kairos, an appointed or opportune time, fits the theology well. The verse also complements Ephesians 2:13, where those once far off are made near by the blood of Christ. Nearness is therefore covenant access as well as spatial imagery.

📜 Isaiah 55:7

“Let the wicked forsake his way, & the †vnrighteous man his thoughts: and let him returne vnto the LORD, and he will haue mercie vpon him, and to our God, for hee will †abundantly pardon.”

📌 1611 Margins

† Heb. the man of iniquitie.
† Heb. he will multiply to pardon.

📝 Commentary

This verse enters the internal architecture of repentance. Two things must change: way and thoughts. Hebrew דֶּרֶךְ, derekh, way, describes behavioral trajectory, while מַחֲשָׁבוֹת, maḥashavoth, thoughts or plans, describes the internal architecture from which actions arise.

Repentance is therefore both hodological, a change of way, and noetic, a transformation of thought. The 1611 marginal note is extraordinary: “he will multiply to pardon.” Hebrew יַרְבֶּה לִסְלוֹחַ, yarbeh lisloaḥ. Divine pardon is described through multiplication.

The human imagination may calculate guilt numerically, yet YHWH's forgiveness is expressed with a verb of increase. This prepares verses 8-9. When YHWH says His thoughts exceed human thoughts, the immediate context is His capacity for mercy. The famous “higher thoughts” passage therefore belongs directly to the theology of abundant pardon.

📜 Isaiah 55:8

“¶ For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your wayes my wayes, saith the LORD.”

📝 Commentary

Hebrew repeats the vocabulary of verse 7: מַחֲשְׁבוֹת, maḥashavoth, thoughts, and דְּרָכִים, derakhim, ways. Humanity has its thoughts and ways; YHWH possesses His.

The Greek Septuagint uses βουλαί, counsels or plans, and ὁδοί, ways. Latin uses cogitationes and viae. The verse concerns Divine transcendence, but its immediate subject remains astonishing mercy. Human beings frequently imagine forgiveness according to their own narrow calculus of deservedness. YHWH has just announced that He multiplies pardon.

His modes of thought exceed the limits of human retaliation, scarcity, and finite accounting. Divine cognition genuinely exceeds creaturely cognition. Job 38-41, Psalm 139, Romans 11:33-36, and Wisdom 9 all testify to the immeasurable depth of Divine counsel. Isaiah anchors transcendence in practical revelation: YHWH's higher thought produces a higher mercy.

📜 Isaiah 55:9

“For as the heauens are higher then the earth: so are my wayes higher then your wayes, and my thoughts then your thoughts.”

📝 Commentary

The difference between Divine and human cognition is now mapped onto cosmological verticality. Heaven stands above earth, so Divine ways stand above human ways.

The comparison assumes the ancient phenomenological universe in which heaven is the supernal region over terrestrial habitation. Biblical cosmology repeatedly organizes reality vertically: heaven above, earth beneath, waters, depths, Sheol, celestial host, and terrestrial nations. Isaiah has already used this vertical grammar repeatedly. YHWH stretches the heavens, numbers the host, founds the earth, commands the deep, and reigns over all.

Ephesians gives a complementary New Testament development through ta epourania, the heavenly places, where Christ is enthroned above celestial powers. Isaiah 55:9 therefore makes cosmology into epistemology. The visible distance between heaven and earth becomes the measuring analogy for the immeasurable distance between Divine and human counsel.

Yet the next verses show that this higher realm is not sealed away. Something descends from it: rain, snow, and the Word.

📜 Isaiah 55:10

“For as the raine commeth downe, and the snow from heauen, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring foorth and bud, that it may giue seed to the sower, and bread to the eater:”

📝 Commentary

Isaiah now develops a remarkable sacred meteorology. Rain and snow descend from heaven into earth, penetrate soil, generate fertility, produce seed, and ultimately become bread.

The sequence is an ancient causal system: heaven → precipitation → earth → germination → seed → bread → human life.

Psalm 147 similarly joins Divine Word, snow, frost, ice, wind, and flowing waters. Job 38 speaks of heavenly treasuries of snow and the pathways of rain. Sirach 43 marvels at frost, snow, clouds, and weather as ordered manifestations of Divine command.

Isaiah therefore treats atmospheric phenomena as visible analogues for invisible Divine operation. Rain becomes a causal parable. What descends from above enters the material realm and generates effects unavailable to barren soil by itself. This prepares verse 11's theology of the Word. The heaven-earth relation is communicative: the higher order acts upon the lower.

📜 Isaiah 55:11

“So shall my word bee that goeth foorth out of my mouth: it shall not returne vnto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.”

📝 Commentary

This is one of the strongest biblical statements of performative Divine speech. Hebrew דְּבָרִי, devarî, “my Word,” proceeds from the Divine mouth. It goes forth, is sent, accomplishes, and prospers. The Word is described almost as an emissary possessing mission and effect.

Greek uses ῥῆμά μου, rhēma mou, my spoken word; Latin has verbum meum. Genesis 1 provides the primordial pattern: God said, and reality answered. Psalm 33:6 says the heavens were made by the Word of YHWH. Psalm 147:15 says, “He sendeth forth his commandment upon earth: his word runneth very swiftly.”

The Word therefore possesses a form of causal velocity. Isaiah's analogy with precipitation is magnificent. As rain descending from heaven materially transforms the earth, Divine speech descending from the higher order transforms history. The Word does not return רֵיקָם, rêqām, empty.

This strongly anticipates Johannine theology, where the Divine Word enters the created order personally in Yeshua. Revelation 19 even gives the conquering Messiah the title “The Word of God.” The biblical Word is never inert information. It acts.

📜 Isaiah 55:12

“For ye shall goe out with ioy, and be led foorth with peace: the mountaines and the hilles shall breake foorth before you into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands.”

📝 Commentary

The successful Word of verse 11 now produces a transformed environment. The people leave with joy and shalom, then nature answers. Mountains and hills sing; trees clap.

This is one of Isaiah's clearest examples of cosmic liturgy. Psalm 96 calls the sea, fields, and trees to rejoice before YHWH. Psalm 98 has floods clap their hands and hills rejoice together. Psalm 148 summons heavens, angels, sun, moon, stars, waters, mountains, trees, and creatures into one praise-order. Romans 8 later describes creation itself groaning toward liberation, while Revelation depicts cosmic creation joining heavenly worship.

Isaiah's mountains and trees therefore participate in covenant restoration. The landscape is no passive scenery. Creation responds to redemption. This carries a remarkable phenomenological proposition: in prophetic vision, moral-spiritual restoration possesses ecological resonance. The entire environment becomes liturgical.

📜 Isaiah 55:13

“In stead of the thorne shall come vp the Firre tree, and in stead of the brier shall come vp the Myrtle tree, and it shall be to the LORD for a name, for an euerlasting signe that shall not bee cut off.”

📝 Commentary

The chapter closes with botanical transfiguration. Thorn becomes fir; brier becomes myrtle. The background reaches all the way to Genesis 3, where cursed ground produces thorns and thistles. Isaiah therefore ends with imagery of curse reversal.

The transformation also recalls Isaiah 35, where wilderness blossoms, and Isaiah 41:19, where YHWH plants cedar, acacia, myrtle, oil-tree, and other trees in the wilderness. The myrtle, הֲדַס, hadas, later appears in Zechariah's visionary world among the myrtle trees in the ravine.

The vegetation becomes “an everlasting sign.” Thus the restoration is semiotic. Creation becomes a sign-bearing medium testifying to YHWH's Name. Isaiah 55 moves from thirst to water, water to Word, Word to fertility, fertility to singing creation, and singing creation to an everlasting vegetal sign.

The chapter is an extraordinary union of Christic promise, covenant, hydrology, meteorology, speech-act theology, sacred botany, and eschatological ecology.

Welp, I might as well make the most of my forced anonymity courtesy of the algorithm and get something off my chest. 
And I purposely waited for a week post election to allow all the usual pundits enough time to pontificate. 
So, I’d like to offer this open letter to all of the winners. 
Ahem. 
Oh hai, y’all and congratulations. 
Seriously. 
The midterms were a rout of epic proportions. 
FFS, even a candidate in Iowa who’d dropped out of the race for health reasons was elected over his challenger. 
Unlike previous elections where one party would eke out a win, puff their collective chests and claim a mandate - you truly DO have a mandate. 
Here it is:
Stop. 
Him. 
We didn’t collectively vote for you as much as we voted against him. 
You’re our firewall. 
Apparently all of those record setting No Kings protests weren’t enough of a hint. 
We don’t want a ballroom, a helipad, an arch, a monument, or Saddam’s frigging Cheesecake Factory and we sure as hell don’t want his name tacked onto every goshdarned thing because he knows that nobody will memorialize him once he’s gone. 
For pity’s sake - he even hijacked our nation’s 250th birthday. 
We’re tired of the corruption, the cronyism and the in-your-face disrespect. 
This is not the time for you to hold hands and sing Kumbaya. 
So stop him. 
Please. 
Then we can talk about reversing some of the bad crap coming down the pike. There are things already set legislatively to start in 2027 that they’re going to blame on whoever’s in office then. 
In case your spines get wobbly, just take another look at the midterm results and remember what we the people can do when we’re righteously pissed off. 
So, Job Number One is to stop him. Capice? 
So glad we had this talk. 
Congrats again.

text:
Zarząd ZE PAK: 18 zł to „wartość godziwa”. KPMG nie ujawnia przedziału
------------------------------------------------------
Zarząd ZE PAK, kierowany przez Piotra Żaka, uznał, że cena 18 zł w wezwaniu ogłoszonym przez rodzinny Argumenol odpowiada wartości godziwej spółki. Opierał się na opinii KPMG, która nie podaje jednak żadnych liczb poza samym wnioskiem. Dla akcjonariuszy Midas to znajomy scenariusz.

Co się stało. We wtorek 10 listopada o 18:47 (już po wtorkowym wydaniu) ZE PAK opublikował raport bieżący nr 29/2026 ze stanowiskiem zarządu w sprawie wezwania Argumenol Investment (Cypr) na 17,3 mln akcji (34,04% kapitału) po 18 zł. Załączono do niego opinię o cenie (fairness opinion) KPMG Advisory z 10.11. KPMG zastosowało metodę sumy części (kopalnia, bloki węglowe, budowany blok gazowy, OZE, usługi, nowe projekty) i stwierdziło, że 18 zł „znajduje się w przedziale wartości godziwej”. Samego przedziału ani wartości segmentów nie ujawniło. Opinia nie jest formalną wyceną, opiera się na danych i założeniach zarządu, których KPMG nie weryfikowało, i jest kierowana wyłącznie do zarządu, a nie do akcjonariuszy.

Stanowisko zarządu. Zarząd ocenia pozytywnie wpływ wezwania na interes spółki, a także plan przymusowego wykupu (przy 95% głosów) i wycofania akcji z GPW. Pisze, że nie widzi zagrożenia dla zatrudnienia. Pod raportem podpisali się Piotr Żak, Maciej Nietopiel i Bartłomiej Drywa. Piotr Żak jest jednocześnie jednym z członków rodziny kontrolującej wzywającego. Cena 18 zł niewiele przewyższa ustawowe minimum: średnia z 3 miesięcy wynosi 17,74 zł, z 6 miesięcy 17,98 zł. Według Parkietu (6.10) wartość księgowa to ok. 38,5 zł na akcję. Analityk BM Pekao uznał jednak, że 18 zł „w dużej mierze” odpowiada realnej wartości. Warunek wezwania, czyli umowa o współpracy strategicznej z Argumenolem, nadal nie został spełniony (termin do 2.12).

W skrócie. Telewizja Polsat szeroko otwiera archiwum na YouTube: publikuje pełne odcinki seriali, programów i kabaretów. Wirtualnemedia (11.11) piszą, że za YouTube'a odpowiada nowy zespół (https://t.co/t86b3UcGn2. Kamil Kacperczyk, wcześniej Iberion i ZPR Media). Ekspert ocenia, że to monetyzacja zamortyzowanych treści. Kanał główny ma 1,79 mln subskrypcji. Brak nowych informacji w sprawie XXVI GC 619/17.

Co to może oznaczać dla wyceny Midas i akcjonariuszy mniejszościowych
Ocena, nie fakt. Bezpośrednio nic się nie zmienia: wycena Midas dotyczy dnia wykupu w 2016 r. (0,81 zł), a ZE PAK to inna spółka i inna branża. Pośrednio przydaje się argumentacji powodów. W opinii KPMG wprost zapisano, że historyczne notowania „nie stanowią wystarczającej podstawy” do oszacowania wartości godziwej. To potwierdza tezę, że cena oparta na ustawowych średnich kursach, czyli również cena przymusowego wykupu (art. 82 w zw. z art. 79 ustawy o ofercie), nie musi odpowiadać rzeczywistej wartości. Drugi punkt to wzorzec: ta sama grupa kontrolna wycofuje spółkę z giełdy po cenie bliskiej minimum, a zarząd powiązany z wzywającym ocenia ją pozytywnie. Kontrargumenty: KPMG uznało 18 zł za mieszczące się w przedziale, wezwanie dobrowolne podlega innym regułom niż wykup z 2016 r., a zachowanie z 2026 r. ma niewielką wagę dowodową dla stanu z 2016 r. Siła efektu: słaba, ilustracyjna. Skutku nie da się wyrazić liczbowo.

Źródła: ZE PAK RB 29/2026 (10.11.2026, ESPI/GPW) ze stanowiskiem zarządu i opinią KPMG; Trigon DM, dokument wezwania (28.10.2026); Parkiet, „Wycena ZE PAK-u pod presją rynku” (6.10.2026); https://t.co/O5C03l93Lb (11.11.2026).

ZE PAK board: PLN 18 is "fair value". KPMG keeps its range under wraps
ZE PAK's management board, chaired by Piotr Żak, says the PLN 18 price in the tender offer launched by the family-controlled Argumenol matches the company's fair value. It relies on a KPMG opinion that discloses no figures beyond its conclusion. For Midas minority shareholders, this is a familiar script.

What happened. At 18:47 on Tuesday 10 November, after Tuesday's edition had gone out, ZE PAK published current report 29/2026. It contains the board's position on the tender offer by Cyprus-based Argumenol Investment for 17.3m shares (34.04% of capital) at PLN 18, with a fairness opinion from KPMG Advisory dated 10 November attached. KPMG used a sum-of-the-parts approach (lignite mining, coal units, the gas unit under construction, renewables, services and new projects). It concluded that PLN 18 "falls within the fair value range" but disclosed neither the range nor any segment values. The opinion is not a formal valuation. It rests on management data and assumptions that KPMG did not verify, and it is addressed only to the board, not to shareholders.

The board's view. The board views the offer's impact on the company positively. It also supports the planned squeeze-out (if 95% of votes is reached) and the delisting from the WSE, and says it sees no threat to jobs. The report was signed by Piotr Żak, Maciej Nietopiel and Bartłomiej Drywa. Piotr Żak is also one of the family members who control the bidder. The PLN 18 price sits barely above the statutory floor: the 3-month average is PLN 17.74 and the 6-month average PLN 17.98. Parkiet (6 Oct) put book value at about PLN 38.5 per share, although a BM Pekao analyst said PLN 18 "largely" reflects real value. The offer's condition, a strategic cooperation agreement with Argumenol, has still not been met (deadline 2 Dec).

In brief. Telewizja Polsat is opening its archive on YouTube with full episodes of series, shows and cabaret. Wirtualnemedia (11 Nov) reports that a new team runs YouTube, including Kamil Kacperczyk (formerly at Iberion and ZPR Media). An expert calls it monetisation of fully amortised content. The main channel has 1.79m subscribers. No news in case XXVI GC 619/17.

What it could mean for the Midas valuation and minority shareholders
Assessment, not fact. Nothing changes directly: the Midas valuation is set as of the 2016 squeeze-out date (PLN 0.81), and ZE PAK is a different company in a different sector. Indirectly, it helps the plaintiffs' case. KPMG's opinion states that historical share prices "are not a sufficient basis" for estimating fair value. That supports the argument that a price based on statutory market averages, which also applies to squeeze-out prices (Art. 82 with Art. 79 of the Public Offering Act), need not match real value. There is also a pattern: the same controlling group is taking a company private at close to the minimum price, and a board linked to the bidder endorses it. Counterarguments: KPMG found PLN 18 within its range, a voluntary tender offer follows different rules from the 2016 squeeze-out, and 2026 conduct carries little evidential weight for 2016 value. Strength of the effect: weak and illustrative. It cannot be quantified.

Sources: ZE PAK current report 29/2026 (10 Nov 2026, ESPI/WSE) with the board position and KPMG opinion; Trigon DM tender offer document (28 Oct 2026); Parkiet, "Wycena ZE PAK-u pod presją rynku" (6 Oct 2026); https://t.co/O5C03l93Lb (11 Nov 2026).

text:
Walmart and Kroger are quietly rolling out an internal store technology across America that could either modernize retail or bankrupt the middle-class family budget.

Starting across thousands of locations heading into 2027, traditional paper price tags are being ripped off grocery shelves and replaced with cloud-connected digital screens. Raise the price of bottled water by 20 percent the second the afternoon temperature hits 90 degrees. Surge the cost of ground beef, milk, and sandwich bread between 5 PM and 6 PM when exhausted commuters are rushing home from work. Drop prices at 10 AM on a Tuesday, then hike them right back up the minute the after-school crowd walks through the sliding doors.

Every price change happens wirelessly in seconds from a central corporate dashboard. No store employee has to touch a single shelf.

Walmart has already signed a massive deployment deal with VusionGroup to wire 2,300 American supercenters with EdgeSense digital shelf rails by 2027. Kroger is expanding its own Microsoft-backed system called EDGE across hundreds of supermarkets. Over 60 million digital price tags are already blinking on US grocery aisles right now.

This is not supply chain inflation. This is Uber-style surge pricing built directly into the shelves where Americans buy baby formula, eggs, and medicine.

Last week I sat down for coffee with a former retail pricing director who spent 14 years building supermarket margin algorithms before leaving the industry. What he shared over the table completely changed how I look at a grocery aisle.

"Retailers just turned static shelves into live stock tickers. The question is not whether grocery chains will use instant price changes, because they already spent billions installing the hardware. The question is how much extra money a family of four will lose every week simply because both parents work until 5 PM and cannot shop during off-peak hours."

Here is how the digital grocery pricing system actually works, how it tracks you in the aisle, and the exact phone settings and checkout playbook you need to beat it.

With Kelsey Mitchell entering unrestricted free agency and the Indiana Fever turning the page under new front office leadership, high-level offseason speculation is already heating up. 👀🏀

If @IndianaFever looks to bring in a marquee star next to Caitlin Clark, Minnesota Lynx forward Napheesa Collier emerges as the ultimate target. 

Why the pairing makes complete sense:

• The perfect on court fit: 
@PHEEsespieces provides elite interior defense and rebounding alongside Aliyah Boston, while bringing elite stretch-scoring versatility (shooting over 40% from deep in consecutive seasons) next to league-leading playmaker @CaitlinClark. 

• Built for the high pressure spotlight: 
As a 5-time All-Star and co-founder of Unrivaled, Collier possesses both the basketball acumen and executive composure to navigate the intense scrutiny that comes with playing for Indiana. 

• The title pursuit: 
Pairing Collier with Clark and Boston would instantly elevate Indiana into championship-favorite status while offering Collier a fresh path toward an elusive WNBA ring. 

• The financial path: 
With salary cap dynamics shifting and potential roster flexibility, Indiana could position itself to offer a max contract slot if Mitchell moves on.

But let's accept it's not so easy to make it happen. Collier would have to decide to leave the Minnesota Lynx and then to join the Fever. Also Indiana would need the cap space to facilitate her max salary.

Fever fans, would you like to see Collier team-up with Clark?

Today at 11:00 AM, Canadians across our nation pause to honour Remembrance Day, and pay tribute to the millions of soldiers throughout Canadian history who have made the ultimate sacrifice in service to our country and in defence of the rights and freedoms we enjoy today.

Today, we reflect and remember those who are no longer with us, but also offer our sincere gratitude to the veterans who continue to stand with us. Their enduring strength and courage remind us of our collective duty to stand up and continue defending the rights and freedoms of everyone who calls this country home.

This year is a little different for my family; we’ve chosen to display photographs of my father from his time serving in the Royal Navy as part of the Lest We Forget Memorial Exhibit at Queen’s Park (pictures included at the end). My sincere thanks to @donnaskellympp for creating this memorial for MPPs to honour their family members who have served. For those who would like to visit, the exhibit will be open to the public until the end of November.

I want to extend my deepest gratitude to the St. James Cemetery and @CabbagetownBIA for allowing me to take part in your beautiful Remembrance Day ceremony this morning. Lest we forget.

Happy Veterans Day
To my son, who has faithfully served more than twenty years in the United States Navy, and to every man and woman who has worn the uniform of our Armed Forces—past and present—we offer our deepest thanks. From a grateful nation, we honor you.
May God’s light forever shine upon your paths, guiding your steps in peace and purpose. May His presence rest upon you and your families, and may the service you have given this country be forever honored and respected.
There are no finer patriots than those who place country above self, who stand ready to make the ultimate sacrifice for the freedom of others. You have been willing to lay down your lives in defense of this great republic, and that willingness reflects the highest form of love. As Scripture reminds us, “Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends” (John 15:13). And we pray that the light of the Lord continues to illuminate your way, for “Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path” (Psalm 119:105).
On this Veterans Day, may you feel the gratitude of a nation that stands free because of you. May you be surrounded by peace, strength, and the quiet knowledge that your service has mattered more than words can say.
With honor, respect, and heartfelt thanks—  
Happy Veterans Day to all who have served.  
God bless you and keep you, now and forevermore!🙏🇺🇸❤️🤍💙

text:
California voters have rejected Proposition 40, the so-called billionaires' tax, according to an Associated Press projection reported by ABC News.

Hold on. Look at the money. Building a Better California, the main group opposing the measure, raised $333.1 million this year, most of it from billionaires, per ABC News. Google co-founder Sergey Brin was the top donor at $102 million, listed as based in Reno, Nevada.

The measure would have put a 5% tax on the wealth of taxpayers and trusts with assets over $1 billion, roughly 200 people. Backers said it would raise about $100 billion over five years after steep healthcare funding cuts. Gov. Gavin Newsom became its most prominent opponent, arguing billionaires could leave the state to dodge it.

Read that again. This was not just left versus right. It split Democrats. Rep. Ro Khanna, a leading backer, said: "He [Newsom] doesn't want to offend some of the billionaires who he wants to finance his campaigns." That is Khanna's claim, and the article offers no evidence for it.

The voters made the call, and a state wealth tax is off the table in California.

text:
Duct-taped, shot in the back of the head and dumped in a river. Cynthia Hoffman was 19, developmentally disabled, and believed Denali Brehmer was her best friend. Brehmer set it up because a man online promised her $9 million for photos of a murder. He was a broke 21-year-old living in his grandparents' basement. Asked what she felt when the gun went off, she said: "Well, problem solved."

Anchorage, Alaska. 2019. Denali Brehmer was 18. Online, she met a man who called himself "Tyler," a millionaire from Kansas.

She checked him out. She searched his photos. She looked up his phone number. She checked his PayPal. Everything matched the name he gave her.

Then Tyler made an offer: $9 million for photos and videos of the murder of "someone in Alaska."

Brehmer chose Cynthia "CeeCee" Hoffman. Cynthia was 19 and developmentally disabled. She had met Denali at a mall and considered her her best friend.

Brehmer recruited four other young people to help her. On June 2, 2019, she and a 16-year-old friend invited Cynthia on a hike to Thunderbird Falls, just outside Anchorage.

At the falls, Cynthia was bound with duct tape. Brehmer recorded it for Tyler.

In the video below, Brehmer describes what happened next. Cynthia started "freaking out," saying she would go to the police. Then the 16-year-old walked up behind her and shot her once in the back of the head. "I'm not the one that shot her," Brehmer says. "I'm just the one that had the plan." And how did she feel in that moment? "Well, I just went along with it because problem solved. I know it sounds heartless. But at the time, that's what I was thinking. Problem solved."

Cynthia's body was dumped in the Eklutna River.

Tyler was not a millionaire. His real name was Darin Schilmiller. He was a broke, unemployed 21-year-old from Indiana, living in his grandparents' basement. There was never any money.

Brehmer pleaded guilty to first-degree murder. In 2024 the judge gave her the maximum: 99 years, calling her conduct "cold, calculated, and carried out to a T." Schilmiller also got 99 years. The 16-year-old who pulled the trigger got 85.

"He was a good catfisher," Brehmer says now. "I'll give him props for that."

Would you trust a best friend after reading this?

text:
$IONQ : cyber risk will never be lower than it is today

"You're at the trough of cybersecurity risk you're going to experience for the rest of your life right now."

@NiccoloDeMasi said it in Miami Beach at Cantor Convergence, in front of a room full of finance and crypto leaders. Across from him, Jeff John Roberts, Finance & Crypto Editor at Fortune, had warned the audience the panel would be "a little bit scary."

Niccolo took them back to 1942. Ask the teams racing to build the bomb how far along they were, and the answers ran from 15 years to two. Quantum has the same spread today, and IonQ sits at the short end: 30 years of work since the first quantum logic gate in 1994, about $6 billion invested, a place among the very few in DARPA's Stage C, and the first partner NVIDIA chose for its Boston data center, because its machines can sit in a data center "and not get vibrated out of alignment."

Roberts asked whether anyone could simply copy it. IonQ makes its own chips in its own foundry, with a supply chain entirely in the US, and can build "millions of machines." His words: "There's no one else like us." Copying the know-how? "Definitely no."

The track record backs it up. Revenue went from $40 million in 2024 to $130 million in 2025 and over $500 million this year, with the goal of becoming "a multi-billion dollar revenue company" within three years. IonQ has hit "not just financial guidance the last 5 or 6 years, but our technical guidance as well." "Quantum is now, it's inflecting now."

That head start is why IonQ can describe the threat so precisely. In April it published how it will build a machine that corrects its own errors. Two months ago came a paper showing that 20,000 qubits could break elliptic curve encryption in 26 or 27 days, roughly 2028 in the lab, written in consultation with the NSA with the final details withheld. RSA 2048, the lock banks and telecoms rely on, follows about a year later.

The attacks have started without quantum. In the last month alone, nations from Italy to France to Japan to Malaysia were hit, along with the FBI and DHS websites and Binance, and French and Italian supermarkets lost cooling power. AI models are only getting started, and once they work with powerful quantum computers they will do "even more dastardly things." He expects a "historically large uptick in investments in cybersecurity defenses."

Then Roberts asked: "You're saying some pretty bleak stuff backstage. How bad is it going to be?"

Niccolo answered straight. For the first time since Bletchley Park and Enigma, code breakers have the momentum over code makers. The bad guys are "years, hopefully. Quarters, worst case" behind. Data stolen today will be decrypted later, and the world will truly focus "when you start losing power to hospitals and water treatment plants go off."

The race is global. China invests 10 years ahead in quantum key distribution, on the ground and in space, and could one day say: "I might be behind you in… cryptography, but I'm ahead of you in defense." In Europe, the countries further east lean in harder, because they see an "increasingly hot war that's happening in cybersecurity," and IonQ already does quantum networking across a lot of Eastern Europe. "We're spiky at both," computing and defense.

His answer comes in three layers: lock down the network, move to the post-quantum cryptography the White House mandated on June 22, and put quantum key distribution at the core of data centers, "because it's unhackable." In his words, IonQ is "the largest QKD company in the Western world," and its customers with "a strong security posture" never make the news. To the crypto crowd in the room: "Come and find me."

Cyber risk will never be lower than today. Niccolo's message: act now instead of waiting for the panic, and be "the hardest target." IonQ is in a position to help every company and every country get there, from the chips to the networks. "We're here to help. Please, genuine offer, please do spread the word."

text:
That Sunday evening we were sitting around his parents' dining table when Daniel raised his glass and told them that Valeria was expecting his child. Valeria was the woman he dated before me. He said her name lightly, as if he were sharing news about an old friend. His father stopped cutting his steak. Lucia's eyes widened. His mother, Carmen, asked how far along she was.

"Almost five months," Daniel answered in Spanish.

Five months. Only three weeks earlier he had taken me to dinner for our tenth wedding anniversary. He held my hand across the table and promised we would keep trying to build a family. For six years I went through appointments, tests, treatments, and months of hope followed by the same quiet grief. Daniel watched me cry after every failed attempt. He held me in bed and told me we were enough. Now he was telling his family another woman was carrying his child.

Lucia glanced toward the kitchen where I was bringing out dessert. "What are you going to tell her?" she asked.

Daniel looked at me and smiled. "Nothing yet. She still thinks Valeria moved to Miami."

His father gave a low laugh. "She will find out eventually."

"That can be managed," Carmen said. Then she looked toward me, waiting until I set the cake on the table.

"Don't worry," she said in Spanish. "We'll make her raise this baby."

Everyone laughed.

My hands turned cold around the serving knife.

I wanted to sweep the plates off the table and demand that Daniel explain how he could sit beside me while planning a life around another woman's child.

Instead, I smiled.

"Would anyone like coffee?"

Daniel gave his mother a pleased look.

"See?" he said in Spanish. "She has no idea."

I served the coffee. I cleared their plates. And when Daniel reached beneath the table to squeeze my knee, I did not pull away.

Not yet.

That night he fell asleep quickly. I lay beside him staring at the ceiling while every sentence from dinner repeated inside my head.

Valeria was pregnant. His family knew. They had some plan involving me. And they believed the years I spent trying to become a mother made me easy to control.

The next morning I called in sick for the first time in four years.

I did not confront Daniel. I did not call his mother. I went to the coffee shop across from my office and sat in the far corner with a notebook. I wrote down every Spanish sentence I remembered from dinner. Then I wrote the dates Daniel claimed to be traveling for work. There were eleven trips in the past year. Some had been real. I had seen hotel receipts and work emails. Others suddenly looked different.

Around noon an unfamiliar number called me.

"Is this Maya Reed?" a woman asked.

"Yes."

"My name is Valeria Ortiz."

The room seemed to disappear around me.

"I think you know who I am."

"I do now."

Her breathing became uneven. "I need to show you something. Please don't tell Daniel I called."

We met one hour later at a small cafe near the train station.

Valeria looked nothing like the woman I imagined during the drive there. She was not dressed in expensive clothes. She was not smiling proudly. Her face was pale and she kept one hand over the curve of her stomach as if she were protecting it.

She placed a thick envelope on the table.

"I'm sorry," she said.

I looked at the envelope but did not touch it.

"How long?"

"The relationship ended months ago."

"That isn't what I asked."

Her eyes filled.

"It started last summer."

I closed my eyes. One year. A year of appointments, injections, and Daniel telling me not to give up.

"What do you want from me?"

"I don't want anything from you. I need your help."

She pushed the envelope closer.

Inside was a private agreement prepared by a law firm. The first page offered Valeria money if she agreed not to ask Daniel for financial support and did not use his family name without permission.

I submitted a statement today to the Allegheny County Health Department expressing my strong support for U.S. Steel and Nippon Steel's proposed $3 billion investment in a modern hot strip mill at Edgar Thomson Works in Braddock.

For more than 40 years, Braddock and surrounding Mon Valley communities have suffered from industrial decline, population loss, deteriorating housing and disappearing economic opportunities.

This investment offers something these communities desperately need: a catalyst for economic revitalization.

The project will replace equipment dating to 1938 with advanced technology, strengthen the competitiveness of American steelmaking, and support thousands of construction-related and existing industrial jobs.

But its potential impact goes far beyond the steel mill.

Good-paying jobs generate income that supports local restaurants, retailers and community services. Industrial investment attracts suppliers and potentially other advanced manufacturing businesses. A stronger local economy creates demand for housing rehabilitation and additional private investment.

We've seen how major investments helped transform former industrial properties at SouthSide Works, the Waterfront in Homestead and Hazelwood Green. Braddock deserves an opportunity for a similar economic resurgence.

I recognize the legitimate concerns about air quality. U.S. Steel must meet applicable environmental standards and use effective pollution controls. Modern production technology offers significant improvements in energy efficiency and waste reduction compared with the antiquated equipment it will replace.

But we must also ask: What is the realistic alternative?

Where will the money come from to rehabilitate Braddock's housing? What will attract small businesses without customers who have the income to support them? And how will we attract future industrial investment if our region develops a reputation for turning away businesses prepared to invest billions of dollars and create jobs?

Government grants and charitable initiatives have important roles, but they cannot replace a productive private-sector economy.

Public policy always involves trade-offs. We must carefully weigh the benefits against the costs.

When measured against its potential to create and preserve good-paying jobs, rebuild our communities, strengthen American manufacturing and demonstrate that Western Pennsylvania welcomes investment, this project more than passes that test.

Braddock has endured decades of decline. It deserves a future built on opportunity, investment and economic growth.

Let's build that future right here in Western Pennsylvania. 🇺🇸

text:
Artificial intelligence has not so far produced a clean story of mass unemployment. Aggregate employment in developed countries remains broadly stable, and recent assessments have found limited evidence that AI has shifted the headline numbers. But a troubling change may be hiding beneath the surface: the quiet weakening of the first rung of the career ladder.

The most worrisome evidence is showing up exactly where we should expect it first: in early-career hiring. A working paper released in November 2025 by the Stanford Digital Economy Lab found that workers aged 22 to 25 in the most AI-exposed occupations experienced a 16% relative decline in employment after the spread of generative AI, even after controlling for other factors that might affect firms’ employment decisions. An Anthropic report from March 2026 provides suggestive evidence for a similar conclusion.

More experienced workers in those same occupations did not suffer the same decline. Employment is also not declining in the entry-level jobs with low AI exposure. The concern is specific to early-career jobs that are exposed to AI.

That is not a minor signal. It suggests that firms may be using AI to substitute for the junior tasks through which people traditionally gain their first foothold—at least for those in jobs where generative AI is used extensively, like software developers, customer service representatives, computer programmers, and information systems managers.

The time is now to make changes in the way we train, prepare, and support young people who are about to enter the workforce. Educational institutions need to reorient for the era of an AI-augmented workforce. Governments must incentivize businesses to hire and train early-career workers. Businesses, in turn, need to recognize the importance of developing a long-term workforce experienced in AI—a process that begins with entry-level workers. And students themselves should take on the responsibility of not only becoming AI fluent but learning how to apply that knowledge in various fields.

In short, we must change the way we have traditionally thought of entry-level work.

This is especially true because the broader labor market for recent graduates is also softening. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York reported that in the fourth quarter of 2025, the unemployment rate for recent college graduates rose to 5.6%, while the underemployment rate (the share of graduates working in jobs that typically do not require a college degree) reached 42.5%, its highest level since the covid pandemic. No single statistic can prove that AI is the sole cause of that deterioration. Hiring in general is way down post-pandemic, and young people are particularly vulnerable to the slowdown. But it would be a mistake to ignore the possibility that AI is accelerating an already difficult transition from school to work.

Behind these statistics is a great deal of personal distress. Recent graduates today often submit hundreds of applications before they receive a single offer, and surveys consistently find elevated rates of anxiety, financial precarity, and burnout among young workers in extended job searches. If AI quietly closes the door on typical early jobs, people will pay the price in delayed independence, postponed family formation, and the sense that their first serious professional efforts have been refused.

It also matters because entry-level jobs are part of the economy’s training system. Junior analysts learn which numbers can be trusted. Young software developers learn how production systems fail. New marketers learn how customers behave outside the neat language of dashboards.

Early-career legal and financial staff learn how rules, judgment, deadlines, and human relationships actually interact. If AI absorbs more of the drafting, triage, coding, summarizing, and administrative preparation that once helped train entry-level workers, firms may become more efficient in the short run while society becomes less capable in the longer run.

The right way to improve the skills of young workers is not to tell them, “Learn to code.” That advice, which shaped more than a decade of federal initiatives and university expansion, rested on the premise that coding was a stable, scalable skill almost anyone could learn and parlay into a middle-class job. The premise no longer holds. The layer of work AI handles well—translating a specification into routine code, reproducing standard patterns, debugging predictable errors—is precisely the layer that “learn to code” programs were built around.

Supervising AI systems in their work is now a much more relevant skill. So understanding the outputs AI systems produce will become very important.

To help people develop such skills, we should require universities, community colleges, and professional programs to embed AI literacy, data literacy, prompt-based workflow skills, verification skills, and domain judgment into ordinary degrees. Every graduate should know how to use AI tools, check their output, understand their limits, and combine them with human expertise. This matters even for graduates entering occupations that look relatively safe from AI, such as those in health care. Almost every job contains tasks—drafting, summarizing, scheduling, research, basic data work, routine communication—for which AI is already a substantial productivity tool.

The competition most young workers will experience is not human versus machine but colleague versus AI-augmented colleague. For most young workers, the realistic path to making themselves valuable is not to avoid AI but to become fluent in the technology and combine that with domain judgment, contextual reasoning, and human relationship skills. To this end, schools should emphasize paid co-ops, apprenticeships, and employer-linked projects so students build judgment in real workplaces before they graduate.

Governments should also create targeted tax credits, wage subsidies, and training grants for employers that hire early-career workers into structured, AI-augmented roles. The architecture for this kind of conditional, behavior-linked subsidy already exists in US tax policy. What is missing is a version of these instruments built specifically around early-career AI-augmented work.

Firms, for their part, should stop making hiring decisions based only on short-run cost savings from AI. Young workers are not valuable only for the tasks they perform this quarter. Their value lies in learning, skill formation, institutional memory, and future productivity. Entry-level hiring is not just an expense. It is an investment in the future stock of judgment inside the firm. The most effective AI-augmented senior workforce of the late 2030s will be drawn overwhelmingly from the junior cohort of today. Firms that automate away the learning stage may improve their immediate margins but find themselves, a decade from now, without anyone who understands how their own AI-driven workflows actually behave.

Students graduating this spring and next face a tough labor market in transition. AI fluency is becoming a commodity. Domain expertise without AI fluency is being outpaced. The combination is what is genuinely scarce. The mechanical engineer with knowledge of manufacturing and AI proficiency; the software programmer with knowledge of financial services who is also a whiz at AI—these are the types of people who will be in demand.

Georgios Petropoulos is an assistant professor at the USC Marshall School of Business. His research focuses on the implications of information technologies for innovation, competition policy, and labor markets.

text:
How to turn viral UGC into paying customers using consumer psychology (we used this to drive 14M+ app downloads from 1.5B+ views):

Stop obsessing over formats. Trends change constantly, but the psychology behind why people watch and buy stays the same. THAT is what you need to understand.

Stanford behavioral scientist BJ Fogg found that behavior requires motivation, ability, and a prompt. 

If you want someone to leave TikTok and download your app, you need to give them a strong enough reason to act.

Motivation comes from three places: sensation (pain/pleasure), anticipation (hope/fear), and belonging (fitting in/being left out). 

You're competing with the dopamine hit of scrolling, so focus on anticipation and belonging through your contnet to motivate viewers to leave the app.

Belonging: Make viewers FEEL like the video was made for them. 

Anticipation: Make viewers EXCITED to try your product. Two ways to do this by showing your product in the video:

> Product as solution: position your product as a solution to whatever pain point your product solves. Show them the dream of a better life that your product offers.

> Product as hook: Make the product itself entertaining to watch. Think Cal AI, Cheaterbuster, or Sherlock, where the scanning experience grabs attention. 

You have ~20 seconds to convince someone your product is worth MORE than their next few scrolls.

Show them the outcome, whether that's learning a language, making extra money, or solving a problem they've been obsessing over.

Hope this helps!

New research from Stanford Medicine is challenging how we think about brain aging, cognitive resilience, and the earliest signs of neurodegenerative disease.

Published in Science Advances on November 4, 2026, the study identified distinct brain activity patterns associated with cognitive resilience and vulnerability to Alzheimer's disease.

Researchers developed a scoring system based on functional brain connectivity and applied it to more than 1,300 adults who showed no signs of cognitive impairment.

The findings suggest that brain activity patterns may help predict future cognitive decline, potentially years before noticeable symptoms.

This is significant because traditional Alzheimer's research has largely focused on biomarkers such as amyloid and tau.

But what if the way the brain communicates across its networks could offer an earlier warning?

As a psychiatrist, I find this direction of neuroscience particularly compelling.

The future of brain health may depend not only on detecting disease but also on understanding what makes certain brains more resilient.

However, this research does not establish a diagnostic test, and scientists have not yet demonstrated that changing these activity patterns prevents Alzheimer's.

The next challenge is translating these discoveries into safe, effective interventions.

text:
Vanessa Williams was Miss America, the first Black woman ever crowned, when Penthouse printed nude photos of her and reportedly made $14 million on a single issue. The photographer who took them, her former boss, said Penthouse paid him $50,000. She got nothing, and 10 months into her reign she was given 72 hours to give up the crown.

She was a musical theater student at Syracuse. In 1983 her show got canceled, there was scholarship money on offer, and she entered a local pageant. She won Syracuse in April, New York in July and Atlantic City in September.

In the summer of 1982 she had worked as an assistant and makeup artist for a photographer in Mount Kisco, New York. In the video below she says that after about a month he asked to take some pictures of her: "They'd be really artistic. No one's ever gonna see them."

Her year as Miss America took her to a state dinner at the White House, where Lena Horne burst into tears meeting her. It also brought death threats from people who said a Black woman could not represent America.

In July 1984 a New York Post reporter called her about photos coming out in Penthouse. "I know that I hadn't signed a release," she says, "so there's no way that anyone would be able to publish these pictures." Penthouse printed them on a model release from the 1982 shoot, and she has said for 40 years that she never signed one.

She resigned on July 23, 1984, and the runner-up wore the crown for the last 7 weeks. Penthouse ran a second set from another photographer in January 1985. She sued the photographer and Bob Guccione for a reported $500 million, then dropped the case a year later.

She says it set her career back about 10 years. In 1992 "Save the Best for Last" spent 5 weeks at No. 1, and in 2015 Miss America apologized to her and her mother on live TV.

Penthouse reportedly made $14 million from those photos, and the woman in them lost her crown and was paid nothing.

Was Vanessa Williams robbed by a boss who told her no one would ever see those pictures, or did a model release from the shoot make them his to sell?

Veterans Day

To me, being a Veteran means to be Volunteer.

1991 I volunteer to go into the Army after turning down an offer from the Marine Corps the year before. Honestly, I tried to get my offer reinstated, but the Marines only took 2nd year law student as they send all officers through OSC.
1991 I missed the Army interview at Creighton. So when I contacted the Army they said they would grant me an interview, but I had to get to Fort Riley on my own. So I jumped in the truck and drove there.

After my interview I was offered a position as a JAG officer. I did not hesitate and accepted immediately. I turned down job offers with two Accounting Firms, and one Law Firm. I remember telling my friend Mark Cichocki I was going into the Army. I was sitting in Rio Verde. Mark's response was unique, does your Dad know what the F%^K you are doing?

After being accepted into JAG I volunteered to go to Fort Bragg. I could have gone to Europe, Hawaii etc. But I wanted to go to Bragg and be a Paratrooper. Guess the movie the Green Berets played a role here.

After Airborne School and being at Bragg for a year or so I was asked by my friend John McAfee to use my truck. While driving down the road John said he needed to ask me a favor. You see John had been tasked with going to Somalia, and he did not want to go alone. He and his wife thought he would be better off, and safer if I went with him. So not wanting to let John down, since I had nothing better to do for 6 months, I volunteered to go to Somalia. BTW, John rarely left the compound in Mogadishu, I was the one always out and going into Harm's Way. So much so that LTC Horton, my boss, sat me down and told me I had to quit leading convoys and playing John Wayne as a JAG Officer, because if anything happened to me, he would have to do my job as well, and he would not be happy about it.
